sheets.name: RCMs
rows: Lack of an established and updated policy framework and related processes may result in reputational, operational, and fraud risks.
The underwriting policy is defined, documented, and formally approved by the Board of Directors.
Failure to periodically review and update policies and procedures may lead to non-compliance and operational inefficiencies.
The underwriting policy is reviewed and approved annually by the Board.
Failure to follow defined procedures may result in reputational, operational, and fraud risks.
SOPs for the underwriting process are defined, documented, and enforced.
Non-adherence to IRDAI guidelines may lead to financial, reputational, and regulatory risks.
Underwriting policies and procedures are aligned with IRDAI circulars and updated as required.
Issuing policies to ineligible individuals may result in compliance breaches and financial losses.

1. Due diligence guidelines are specified for various customer segments (individuals, firms, companies, NRIs, PEPs, etc.). 2. All proposals undergo branch-level quality checks before system entry. 3. Automated validations for age, income, medical history, and other criteria are performed prior to issuance. 4. Exceptions are handled through manual underwriting. 5.As per policy, apprvol of Cheif underwriter is mandatory for PEP cases.
6. Blacklisted pincodes are mapped in the system for restricting the policy issuance
Failure to collect required documents during onboarding may result in compliance issues.

1. Collect all mandatory Officially Valid Documents (Passport, Aadhaar, DL, etc.), with PAN/Form 60 required in all cases. 2. Enforce medical grids and mandatory Medical Examination Reports (MERs) as triggered. 3. Income documents are required based on premium and sum assured thresholds.
Non-compliance with KYC, AML, or CFT regulations may result in regulatory penalties.
Collect proof of identity, address, photograph, and PAN/Form 60 at onboarding.
Inadequate identification of high-risk customers may lead to financial crimes and regulatory non-compliance.
Applications from NRIs, PEPs, and HNWIs are classified as high-risk per underwriting guidelines.
Configuration of unapproved STP rules may compromise process integrity.
The Underwriting function ensures adherence to defined Straight-Through Processing (STP) rules by reviewing and approving all rule configurations and changes prior to implementation.
Unauthorized changes may result in incorrect processing and regulatory breaches.
Changes to STP rules are permitted only with prior approval from the Head of Underwriting.
Lack of AML checks in STP cases may result in regulatory violations.
The Underwriting function ensures AML compliance for Straight-Through Processing (STP) transactions through branch-level checks
Improper STP rule configuration may result in incorrect auto-approval of proposals.
1. STP outcomes are randomly monitored by the Quality Control (QC) team.
Failure to review STP rules may result in incorrect processing and increased operational risk.
Evidence of approval, such as documented email communications, is maintained to confirm that modifications were authorized in accordance with governance standards
Inaccurate STP decisions may lead to unassessed or misclassified risks.
Quality checks are performed and reports maintained by the department.
Incorrect decisions may result in rejection of viable proposals and financial losses.

1. System validations and medical grids are configured to raise requirements automatically. 2. Underwriting team receives training during onboarding and as per training calendars. 3. Complex cases are escalated to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) for review. 4. Medical reports are valid as per defined guidelines.
Fraudulent submissions may result in inappropriate policy issuance and claims risk.
1. Medical tests are conducted only through approved TPAs and panel doctors. 2. High-value cases require valid income proofs, uploaded and reviewed during underwriting.
Insufficient premiums for high-risk profiles may result in underwriting losses.

High-risk cases are automatically failed in the STP process and subsequently undergo manual underwriting. Additionally, a Video MER  is triggered automatically for such cases. Underwriters exercise judgment during manual review to validate risk factors and premium adequacy.
Issuing policies without insurable interest may result in compliance and claims issues.
The underwriting team verifies declared relationships and insurable interest through KYC documents.
Reviving policies without underwriting may reinstate coverage without reassessing risk.

1. Revival rules are mapped to lapse duration and may require automatic reinstatement, Declaration of Good Health (DGH), or medical underwriting. 
2. Policies lapsed for over one year require underwriting sign-off.
Non-adherence to onboarding guidelines may result in operational and compliance risks.
1. Agreements are executed with TPAs for medical examinations. 2. Due diligence is performed for empanelled vendors.
Failure to evaluate vendors may result in poor service and compliance issues.
Vendor performance is evaluated semi-annually as per procurement policy.
Delays in proposal processing may lead to customer dissatisfaction and inefficiencies.
TAT guidelines specified in SLAs must be complied with.
Non-compliance with approval authority may result in unauthorized decisions.
Exceptions require approval from the Chief Underwriter or Head of Customer Onboarding.
Delays in processing may result in operational inefficiencies.
Cases are processed within T+2 days, where T is the day the last document is received.
Lack of Underwriting for Rider Addition
Failure to assess risk during rider addition may result in inappropriate coverage.
Riders are added only at the time of issuing the base plan, and underwriting evaluation is performed along with the base policy.
Unauthorized backdating may result in coverage without proper risk assessment.

As per SOP, dating back is generally allowed for traditional products and may be permitted for other products only as an exception by Chief Underwriter / AVP & above of Customer Onboarding. Backdating is allowed within the same financial year but not prior to the product launch date.
Splitting proposals without oversight may result in misclassification of risk.
1. System detects duplicate logins within a 3-month window. 2. Mandatory declaration required for second policy issuance. 3. Exceptions routed to Senior Underwriter for approval.
Delays in requesting additional data may result in processing inefficiencies and customer dissatisfaction.
Underwriting team is responsible for triggering medical requirements during the underwriting process only
Absence of proper segregation may lead to conflicts of interest and increased risk.
1. Cases are automatically routed based on predefined limits. 2. Head of Underwriting may reassign cases in exceptional circumstances.
Lack of Underwriting for Policy Changes
Failure to conduct underwriting for key policy changes may increase risk exposure.

BAWC team contacts the customer for confirmation during policy issuance and there is a change in the age found and subsequently If the revised age does not fit within the product parameters, the policy is cancelled
Failure to submit required reports may result in non-compliance.
Various MIS reports are prepared and shared with stakeholders (e.g., Reduced Sum Assured Cases, EDD/UBO Cases, AML Report, Reinsurance Data).
Premiums paid by unrelated third parties may indicate money laundering or undue influence.
Allowed payor list is defined; exceptions require Chief Underwriter approval and relationship validation.
Fraud or anti-selection risks in special products (Keyman, Employer, HUF).
Product-specific checklists ensure all required documentation is obtained, including corporate documents, UBO questionnaires, and enhanced due diligence.
Risk that new product launched without UAT or inadequate UAT
Launching a new product without proper User Acceptance Testing (UAT), or with inadequate UAT, may result in system errors, incorrect processing, and increased operational risk.

Any new product launch, a set of requirements is requested from the UW team. For products configured in BRMS standardization ensures alignment with existing product structures. The UW team validates whether the new product fits within predefined parameters.
If the product does not fit existing configurations, both the New Business team and the Underwriting team conduct UAT from their respective sides.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Absence or Obsolescence of Policy Framework and Related Processes
Risk of not having an established and updated policy framework and related processes.
Policies and procedures are defined and documented in the SOP and actively followed.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Failure to Periodically Review and Update Documented Policies and Procedures

If policies and procedures are not reviewed and updated regularly, it may result in non-compliance, inconsistent process execution, increased operational risk, and reduced organizational effectiveness.
The SOP is reviewed annually or as per version control trends to ensure it remains current and relevant.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies

If policies and procedures are not reviewed and updated regularly, it may result in non-compliance, inconsistent process execution, increased operational risk, and reduced organizational effectiveness.
Roles and responsibilities for each activity are defined in the SOP.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Incomplete or Inadequate Proposal Form Filled by Customer
Risk of incomplete or inadequate proposal forms submitted by customers.

1. Physical proposal forms must be fully completed, correctly dated, signed, and witnessed as prescribed.
2. Digi Quick proposal forms must be fully completed, with customer acceptance received.
3.Branch users conduct pre-issuance QC, Verifieding customer and product details along with submitted documents.
4. Cases with insufficient documents or discrepancies are returned to sales, with remarks captured in the RTS column.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Failure to obtain complete and substantial documents such as age proof, address proof, income proof, PAN/Form 60, Aadhaar/FATCA (for NRI).

1. RO/BO scrutinizes application forms and documents, ensuring all mandatory documents are collected (e.g., suitability analysis form, ACR/SPR, age proof, address proof, income proof, PAN/Form 60, Aadhaar/FATCA for NRI).
2. After scanning, cases flow into Omni under NB Data Entry workflow.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Risk of photographs older than six months being provided at the time of new business application.
Branch users conduct pre-issuance QC, Verifieding customer and product details along with submitted documents; NB team conducts post-issuance QC.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Creation of Multiple IDs or Codes for the Same Life Insured
Multiple IDs or codes created for the same Life Insured.
Dedupe is run on Digiquick to trace duplication.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Policy Issued to Different Life Assured Using the Same PAN
Policy issued to different Life Assured with the same PAN.
Dedupe is run on Digiquick to trace duplication.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Missing or Incorrect Contact Details for Life Assured
Email and mobile details not available, or the same agent’s mobile number updated for multiple Life Assured.
Branch Ops conducts pre-issuance QC and NB team conducts post-issuance QC; dedupe is run on Digiquick to trace duplication.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Moral Hazard Report (MHR) Not Obtained for High Sum Assured Cases
MHR not obtained for cases with sum assured above ₹50 lakhs.
QC is performed by Branch Ops pre-issuance and by NB team post-issuance.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Policy Issued with Mismatched Payer and Proposer Details
Policy issued when payer and proposer details do not match.
Third-party declaration is obtained, signed by both payer and proposer when they differ.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Agents Confidential Report (ACR) / Specified Person Report (SPR) Not Obtained or Dated After Proposal Submission
ACR/SPR not obtained or dated after proposal submission.
ACR/SPR Obtained through OTP at time of proposal and available in omni doc application
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Agent’s Confidential Report (ACR) Issued by Agent for Own Policy or Where Agent Is a Beneficiary
ACR issued by agent for own policy, relatives, or where agent is beneficiary.
During process walkthrough, it was informed that it is responsibility of Branch OPS during pre issuance QC and verify that the agent is not a beneficiary.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Inadequate Tracking of Not Taken Up (NTU) Cases
Lack of tracking and monitoring of NTU cases may result in missed policy conversion opportunities.
Proposals not complied within 30 days are moved to the NB Queue in omni-flow, marked NTU, and refunded.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Incorrect premium collection can cause delays, incorrect policy status, and financial reconciliation issues.
SHT is detected during underwriting and issuance; requirement is raised and communicated to the customer.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Pending Cases at Requirement Stage Beyond Defined Timelines
Cases pending at requirement stage and not closed within defined timelines.
WIP report is sent daily to branches to ensure adherence to timelines.
Post-Issuance of Policy, Inadequate Quality Control Mechanism
Insufficient quality control may result in undetected errors in policy details, KYC, endorsements, or premium calculations.

1. Post-Issuance QC report published monthly to guide BO/RO Ops.
2. Policy document PDF generated from XML files, with electronic signature affixed after quality check.
Adherence to Regulatory Compliances including AML/CFT Guidelines
Non-Adherence to AML/KYC/Suspicious Transactions Guidelines for New Business
Failure to comply with AML, KYC, and STR guidelines may result in regulatory penalties.

1. Validations in Life Asia prevent issuance without PAN.
2. Suspicious/fraudulent transactions reported monthly to Compliance Department.
Adherence to Regulatory Compliances including AML/CFT Guidelines

1. Policy stamps used correctly; stamp duty balances reduced daily.
2. Adequate balance maintained for printing; monthly reconciliation prepared.
Adherence to Regulatory Compliances including AML/CFT Guidelines
Non-Compliance with KYC - RBI Master Director Guidelines
First 8 digits of Aadhaar card not masked.
Aadhaar card is masked before document upload.
CKYC & EIA Processing including Record Maintenance
CKYC ID Not Generated/Generated Beyond Timelines
Failure to generate CKYC ID within prescribed timelines during onboarding.

1. Daily issuance Excel file shared with vendor via automated mail.
2. Internal TAT of T+7 days monitored daily as per SOP.
CKYC & EIA Processing including Record Maintenance
Same CKYC ID Mapped to Multiple Customers
Incorrect mapping of CKYC ID to multiple customers may result in regulatory non-compliance.
Client-level dedupe verification performed by NB Team.
CKYC & EIA Processing including Record Maintenance
CKYC ID Number Not Uploaded in LifeAsia
Failure to upload CKYC ID in LifeAsia poses compliance and operational risk.
NB team uploads CKYC numbers in LifeAsia with IT Team support.
CKYC & EIA Processing including Record Maintenance
Failure to generate EIA (Electronic Insurance Authority) for a customer is a significant operational and compliance risk.
NB team maintains EIA generation tracker and shares pending cases fortnightly.
CKYC & EIA Processing including Record Maintenance
Same EIA Number Mapped to Multiple Customers
Mapping the same EIA number to multiple customers risks identity mismanagement and regulatory non-compliance.
Client-level dedupe verification performed by NB Team.
CKYC & EIA Processing including Record Maintenance
EIA is not generated within the defined TAT

Delay in creating the EIA account and crediting the policy beyond the stipulated TAT may lead to:
• Non-compliance with IRDAI guidelines.
• Customer dissatisfaction due to delayed access to policy documents.

1. Daily issuance Excel file shared with vendor via automated mail.
2. Internal TAT of T+10 days and regulatory TAT of T+15days monitored daily as per SOP.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Failure to maintain MIS/reports or incorrect record keeping.

NB Team maintains the following trackers:
1. Inward Report
2. Issuance Report
3. Receipting Details
4. SDE discard tracker
5. NTU cases
6. Issuance faliure report
7. Discrepancy Report
8. Stamp Duty MIS
9. Rejection MIS
10. NB Monthly review PPT
Absence of List of Vendors (Existing & New)

i. Procurement Team selects vendors and negotiates major expenses.
ii. Vendor selection per technical/commercial criteria in outsourcing guidelines/policy.
iii. Vendor performance evaluated half-yearly per scoring matrix and Procurement Policy.
Review of Policy Printing, Document Dispatch, and RTO Management
Inadequate Tracking of Policy Dispatch, Delay in Communication, Absence of RTO Tracking
Lack of effective tracking for policy dispatch and RTO cases, delays in communicating dispatch status.

1. Dispatch process documented in SOP.
2. Dispatch tracker monitors policy document dispatch to customers.
Adherence to Office Document Management Guidelines
Failure to classify documents as per guidelines may hinder retrieval and reference, affecting efficiency.

Documents classified as: a. Confidential
b. Restricted
c. Internal
d. Public
Errors in customer details, coverage, premium, or conditions may cause disputes and dissatisfaction.
XML files generated and sent to printing vendor for comparison with documents; errors corrected and revised XML sent to vendor.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Submission of tampered or forged KYC documents poses regulatory and fraud risks.

During the walkthrough it is informed that it is to be part Branch Operation teams.
All the documents are collected, scan and uploaded in the Omnidocs.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Incorrect NAV due to system errors, manual mistakes, or timing mismatches may cause financial discrepancies and disputes.
During the process walkthrough it was informed that NAV is automatically calculated in the system from the policy issuance date.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Delays in premium receipt issuance may cause customer dissatisfaction due to lack of timely payment confirmation.
During process walkthrough, it was noted that, premium receipt is automatically issued at the time of proposal stage. Also, during our mystery shopping, we have experience the same thing.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Cases Wrongly Discarded by Branches/NB Team
Incorrectly discarding valid cases may result in lost revenue and missed opportunities.
During the process walkthrough it was informed Branch will send  the contract rejected cases to the HO along with the reasons of rejection and HO will discard the same.
Review of NB Premium Collection, Receipting, and Reconciliation
Policies sold without proper disclosure, suitability assessment, or with misleading information may cause grievances and non-compliance.
Customer validation performed via questions in the advisory script.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Wrong Customer Mobile Number Filled in Application Form
Incorrect mobile number entry may prevent delivery of OTPs, updates, reminders, and notifications.
Customer validation is performed through BAWC calling .Also OTPs are generated while proposal form filing.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Sales Illustration Dated On or Before Proposal Date
Issuing sales illustration dated on or before proposal may cause regulatory non-compliance.
Sales illustration form is auto generated at time of proposal.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Live Photograph Not capture.Risk of Impersonation.
Customer Live Photograph not captured: The customer's live photograph was not obtained during onboarding, which may impact identity verification and compliance.
Currently, both options are available to capture the live photo of the customer as well as to upload the photo graph of the customer
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies

Welcome calling failed but policy not closed: The welcome call to the customer was unsuccessful, yet the policy was not closed by the company, which may result in incomplete customer validation and increased operational risk.

1. Calling team to ensure 100% calling in first 2 business days from the date of allocation. 
Rechurning on the applicable cases to continue till we achieve desired closure %. 
2. Operations team at service provider’s end to ensure required attempts, min. 3 and max no limit. Daily Briefing & Call Listening sessions to be conducted for tele-calling agents in order to 
minimize the errors.
3.Basic hygiene of day-to-day operations to be followed – alternate numbers, reattempt in different 
time zone, call back as per scheduled.
Compliance with IRDA and Reulatory guidelines

Policy applied by Advisor to achieve month-end target, later cancelled: Policies are sometimes applied by advisors to meet month-end targets and subsequently cancelled, leading to potential manipulation of business metrics and operational inefficiencies.

1.The policy should not be issued unless all requirements are fulfilled and the premium is received in any other mode.
2.In case of premium payment via cheque, issuance occurs only after the cheque is realized.
Compliance with IRDA and Reulatory guidelines

Policy issued but premium not received / delay in receiving premium: Policies have been issued without receiving the premium payment, or there have been delays in premium receipt, which can cause financial discrepancies and compliance risks.
The premium is collected at the time of submitting the proposal application form. The application is accepted only after the premium has been received.
Compliance with IRDA and Reulatory guidelines
Incorrect risk commencement date provided to customer: The risk commencement date communicated to the customer was incorrect, which may result in disputes and regulatory non-compliance.
The Risk Commencement Date (RCD) must not be earlier than the premium realization date. It should be set on or after the later of the premium realization date or the underwriting decision date.
Review of Policy Printing, Document Dispatch, and RTO Management
Absence of tracking over Return to Sales cases

Absence of proper tracking and control over “Return-to-Sales” cases can lead to unintentional cancellation or discarding of policies, resulting in non-compliance with regulatory guidelines for policy delivery and fulfillment.

RTS report is in place.
RTS cases crossing TAT are treated as new proposals and old are discarded.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies and TAT.
Absence of tracking over proposal to issuance and issuance to dispatch TAT.

Absence of tracking for turnaround time (TAT) between key stages of proposal to issuance and issuance to dispatch which can lead to delays, operational inefficiencies, and non-compliance with regulatory timelines.

1.Processing of an insurance proposal, including seeking any additional requirements and making a decision on the proposal, should be completed within T+7 days from the later of (a) the date of receipt of the proposal or (b) the date of receipt of additional requirements. 
2.A copy of the policy, along with the proposal form, should be provided within T+15 days.
3.The New Business team must ensure that the defined turnaround times (TAT) are not breached. A tracker is maintained to monitor compliance with these timelines.
Adherence to Regulatory Compliances including AML/CFT Guidelines
Risk of delay in communicating decision of the policy issuance.

Risk of not communicating Decision to the customer (other than issued) within 15 Days from Login or last requirement received, leading to Breach of Regulation & this being PPI guidelines, risk of penalty by IRDA Audit.
Communicating the decision through email / sms/ letters within the defined tat of T+15days from the last requirement date.
Review of Policy Printing, Document Dispatch, and RTO Management
Delay in assignment of Employer Employee cases .
Policy bonds dispatched to customer without assignment in Employer- employee cases
An endorsement form is attached to the policy bond, which includes the details of both the assignor and the assignee.
Delay in refund of premium or adjusting of premium against the policy leads to unallocated Deposit
If in any case policy is rejected the refund should be made within 30days.
Inconsistent processes due to outdated policies.
SOPs are reviewed periodically; version control is maintained.
Policies not updated for changing business/regulatory needs.
SOPs are reviewed periodically; version control is maintained.
SOPs not updated as per IRDAI circulars.
Compliance team updates SOPs promptly with new IRDAI guidelines.
System blocks policy issuance without PAN; annual KYC audits conducted.
New Business team verifies proposal, KYC, and mandatory documents.
Obtain and verify approved customer quote before onboarding.
Requests processed with missing member details.
Operations team checks proposal forms and member data for completeness.
Master policy created without premium receipt.
System auto-reconciles receipts and updates transactions.
Operations reconcile premiums; track short payments; credit excess to MPH.
Invalid or duplicate member details created.
System validates member details; KYC responsibility with MPH.
Risk date before premium receipt or dead policy issued.
Maker-checker process ensures accurate risk commencement date.
Upload data within T+2 days; monitor TAT daily and report monthly.
Reconcile premium before adding members; communicate shortfalls to MPH.
Calculate and communicate refunds via endorsement letter.
Master policy not delivered to MPH.
Send hard copy to sales; email soft copy to sales and MPH.
Application entries not done in Digi Quick and SDE for all inward applications.
Data entry is reconciled with transaction details from the bank data center team.
Resolve pending/discrepancy cases before transition from Return to Sales.
Premium received only via direct debit; reconciled with transaction details; short payment requirement raised if needed.
Incorrect premium amount collected from MPH.
Premium auto-calculated based on ROI, sum assured, and age for each member.
COI not sent or delivered to members, causing dissatisfaction.
Soft copy sent via WhatsApp/SMS; hard copy dispatched to registered address; delivery tracked and recorded.
Annual inspection audit or certificate not obtained.
Conduct annual MPH audit or obtain external auditor certificate.
RTO of COI not re-delivered or discarded timely.
If customer not traceable within 180 days after two redelivery attempts, COI is discarded and tracked.
Inadequate data received from banks for PMJJBY.
Renewal member data reconciled with active member data; non-renewed members terminated; policy renewed for eligible members.
Incorrect premium amount collected from MPH.

Premium reconciled with transaction details; discrepancies corrected; reconciliation module used for uploads; policy renewed only after receipt of short payment; premium collected on pro-rata basis at enrolment.
Ineligible members enrolled in PMJJY schemes.
Eligibility verified based on age and account status; renewals processed only for eligible members.
Policy cancellation requests not processed timely.
Cancellation requests received via registered email and processed within two days.
Not all cancellation requests recorded in CRM.
Requests received via registered email and logged in CRM within one day.
Incorrect refund amount processed to MPH account.
Termination date entered in system; refund amount auto-calculated.
Refund provided to incorrect bank account of MPH.
Request includes MPH account details; accounts updated in system; refund processed within two days.
MIS Not Shared as per Frequency
MIS not updated as required or contains incorrect data.
MIS/reports maintained and shared with stakeholders at defined frequency as per SOP.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Absence or Obsolescence of Policy Framework and Related Processes
Lack of an established and updated policy framework and related processes.

An approved procurement policy is maintained and actively followed. Version control mechanisms ensure updates are properly documented, tracked, and communicated, maintaining consistency and compliance across procurement activities.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Failure to Periodically Review and Update Documented Policies and Procedures
If policies and procedures are not reviewed and updated regularly, it may lead to non-compliance, inconsistent processes, increased operational risk, and reduced effectiveness.
Policies are reviewed annually or as per version control trends to ensure they remain current and relevant.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Non-Adherence due to Lack of Procurement Policy Communication
Procurement policy not circulated to stakeholders, leading to non-compliance.
The procurement policy is distributed and made accessible to all relevant parties.
Unplanned Procurements Leading to Budget Overspend
Unplanned or unapproved procurements may result in costs exceeding the allocated budget.

1. Business functions prepare adequate budget plans for procurement, identifying and finalizing requirements. 2. The Central Procurement Department (CPD) consolidates this information and develops a procurement calendar to align purchasing activities with approved budgets and project timelines.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Inadequate Completion of Purchase Requisition Forms
Incomplete or inaccurate Purchase Requisition Forms may result in incorrect procurement, delays, and budgeting errors.

1. The Purchase Requisition in the Oracle system includes mandatory fields such as item specifications, budget amount, quantity, and rate, without which the request cannot proceed. 2. Each Purchase Requisition is reviewed and approved by the Head of Department (HOD) before submission for procurement processing.
Non-Adherence with Quotation and RFQ Requirements
Failure to obtain multiple quotations or publish RFQs as required may result in non-compliance and reduced transparency.

1. The Procurement team reviews the Purchase Requisition, especially when a vendor reference is provided by the user department. 2. The Procurement team obtains multiple quotations from vendors as per the procurement process. 3. RFQs are published in newspapers or on the official website, as defined in the procurement policy.
Vendor proposals may be evaluated in a biased or insufficient manner, resulting in non-compliance and potential financial or reputational loss.

1. Vendor evaluations are conducted by a committee as per the matrix defined in the procurement policy. 2. Technical and financial scoring results are evaluated and form part of the recommendation, which is approved by the committee.
Cost-Driven Vendor Selection Impacting Quality and Timelines
Focusing solely on lowest cost may compromise quality, delay timelines, and breach SLAs.
Financial scoring results are evaluated and form part of the recommendation, which is approved by the committee.
Non-Approval of High-Value Procurements by PCCC and Outsourcing Committee
Procurements exceeding Rs. 10 lakhs may proceed without required approvals from the Purchase Committee Clearance (PCCC) and Outsourcing Committee.

1. At the time of raising a Purchase Requisition, the business function obtains approvals from the PCCC and Outsourcing Committee via email. 2. The Procurement team scrutinizes the purchase requisition request and obtains the approval of the PCCC and Outsourcing Committee.
Procurement Initiated Without Required Approvals and Budget
Procurement may be initiated without receiving a Purchase Requisition, PCCC approval, and approved budget.

1. Procurement actions are allowed only after a valid Purchase Requisition is submitted with the approved budget amount. 2. The Oracle system enforces restrictions to prevent procurement activities from proceeding without PR approvals.
Purchase Orders may be issued without proper approvals or outside authorized limits.

1. Purchase Orders are issued solely by the Purchase department and validated against the approved requisition. 2. Purchase Orders are approved as per the Delegation of Authority matrix within the Oracle system.
Procurement may be executed by bypassing the formal process or without issuing a Purchase Order, resulting in non-compliance.
System restrictions in Oracle ensure Purchase Orders are linked to approved requisitions, and vendor invoices are processed only against the corresponding Purchase Order.
Duplicate Purchase Orders may be created for the same requisition, leading to duplicate payments and financial losses.
Oracle workflow ensures Purchase Orders are linked to approved requisitions and do not exceed the approved value.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Missing GRN/SRN Leading to Inaccurate Accruals and Payments
Absence of Goods Receipt Notes (GRN) or Service Receipt Notes (SRN) may result in unjustified payments and financial discrepancies.
All received goods and services are recorded through GRN or SRN entries in the Oracle workflow.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Employees may incur expenses without approval, leading to unauthorized spending and non-compliance.
All employee expenses require proper authorization.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Purchase Splitting to Circumvent Approval Limits
Purchases may be split into smaller transactions to bypass approval thresholds.
The Procurement team maintains a tracker to monitor cumulative spend per vendor, department, or service.
Inadequate negotiation may lead to overpayment and reduced cost efficiency.
1. Procurement team negotiates rates with shortlisted vendors. 2. Negotiated rates and savings are documented and submitted for committee review and approval.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Uncoordinated purchasing may expose the organization to price fluctuations and inconsistent terms.
1. Procurement maintains and periodically reviews the rate card. 2. Purchase orders are raised based on the rate card or contract.
Insufficient Vendor Due Diligence During Onboarding
Vendor credentials and financial stability are not adequately verified, with essential documents missing.
Finance & Accounts maintains the vendor onboarding checklist and supporting documents.
Incomplete Contracts and Insufficient Legal Oversight
Contracts may lack essential clauses, weakening enforceability and exposing the organization to risks.
All legal documents are reviewed by Legal. Standard terms in Purchase Orders are used and not altered.
Unauthorized Changes to Rate Contracts/Purchase Orders
Rate contracts may be altered without proper authorization, leading to inconsistent pricing and disputes.
Any change in rates or Purchase Orders requires CPD approval.
Non-Compliance with Internal Document Management Guidelines
Poor documentation may lead to incomplete records and audit difficulties.
1. Procurement maintains a tracker for monitoring and retrieval. 2. Dedicated folders contain all related records for each recommendation note.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Delays may disrupt project timelines and increase costs.
Procurement timelines are monitored to ensure timely completion.
Outsourced activities may not comply with regulatory or internal guidelines, leading to penalties and inefficiencies.
All outsourcing procurements follow the Outsourcing Policy and require committee approvals.
Vendor performance is not periodically evaluated, resulting in poor service quality and missed improvement opportunities.
Vendor performance is evaluated semi-annually using a checklist, with recommendations documented for management review.
Adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and Policies
Issues with vendors may remain unresolved, leading to operational disruptions and customer dissatisfaction.
The Procurement Department maintains a complaint register for tracking and resolution.
Non-Adherence to Procurement Process During Vendor Renewal
Vendor renewals bypassing the standard process may lead to non-compliance
Renewals are based on documented performance evaluations.

After OTC request resolution in digiCARE, the corresponding update in Life Asia may fail due to validation errors or system batch failures, leading to incorrect policy master data, customer dissatisfaction, and regulatory TAT breaches (IRDAI TAT: 7 days).

System auto-runs daily batch processes to update Life Asia for validation-fail cases. SD users wait for the auto-batch on T+1. If Life Asia is not updated by T+2, SD users manually update via Clients & Groups >> Client Maintenance >> Modify Client in Life Asia and manually close the digiCARE request. OTC requests open beyond 2 days are escalated to Manager/Sr. Manager – Central Ops as per the escalation matrix.
Incorrect CTST Classification of OTC Requests

OTC requests logged under incorrect Call Type/Sub Type (CTST) may result in misdirected processing, wrong TAT tracking, incorrect communication to customers, and regulatory non-compliance with IRDAI TAT requirements.

Requests logged under incorrect CTST are identified during SD scrutiny and rejected at that stage. SD users validate CTST selection against defined request categories before processing. Rejection reason logged in digiCARE. Customer communication (SMS/email) sent upon rejection. Touchpoint users trained on correct CTST selection per digiCARE User Guide.
Non-OTC Requests Processed with Incomplete or Deficient Documents

Non-OTC requests require additional documentation. Processing without proper document scrutiny against the checklist may result in incorrect policy changes, regulatory non-compliance, financial loss, and customer disputes. Specific risk: Ownership change to non-blood relative without Underwriter consent.

SD users perform detailed document scrutiny against the defined checklist for each Non-OTC request type. Decisions: Approve (documents complete and valid), Reassign (incomplete documents at touchpoint), CFR (requirements awaited from customer – auto-closes after 3 days if no response), or Reject (per exception management). For ownership change to non-blood relatives, Underwriter consent is mandatory. Auto-update to Life Asia on approval; manual update where auto-update fails.
Financial Non-Payout Transactions Processed Without Underwriting Decision

Transactions that affect the customer's risk profile (DOB change, occupation change, sum assured increase/decrease, rider addition, policy/premium term change) require Underwriting team decision. Processing without UW approval may result in incorrect risk classification, incorrect premium computation, regulatory non-compliance, and financial loss.

SD team refers all Financial Non-Payout requests that affect the customer's risk profile to the Underwriting team via mail/workflow before processing. UW provides decision within T+3 days. SD processes the request in Life Asia/digiCARE only after receiving UW approval. Non-FTR requests are updated in digiCARE and allocated to maker/creator queue for further action. Exceptions (e.g., DOB change at client level, age-decreasing changes within product boundary) are processed per defined exception matrix without UW referral.
Backdated Fund Switch Processed Without Appropriate Approval

Backdated fund switch requests, if processed without proper authority approval, may result in incorrect NAV application, financial impact to the policyholder, and regulatory non-compliance. Policy terms restrict fund switch dates.

Backdated fund switch requests mandatorily require approval from the SD Head before processing. Request is held in digiCARE pending SD Head sign-off. Without this approval, the request is not processed. All approvals documented and retained. Standard fund switch requests (current date) processed via OTC platform in CRM or WhatsApp; exception cases only flow to HO Service Delivery.
Fraudulent or Money-Laundering Payout to Wrong Beneficiary

Surrender/partial withdrawal payouts may be made to a fraudulent party or money launderer where the payout bank account differs from the source bank account on record, violating AML/CFT Master Guidelines 2022 and IRDAI policyholder protection regulations, resulting in financial loss, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.

SD users apply the RAG (Red/Amber/Green) matrix before payout: Scenario 1 (different source bank, contact number matches) = Amber – mandatory tele-calling on application-form number; account must be >3 months old for payouts >₹2 lakhs. Scenario 2 (different source bank and contact number) = Red – tele-calling for <₹2 lakh; Outsourced Video Verification/Video KYC for ≥₹2 lakh. RAG deviation requires outsourced video verification, positive FCU report, or AVP recommendation with HOD sign-off.

Payout requests (surrender, partial withdrawal, FLC, CFI, policy loan) may be incorrectly processed or approved beyond the designated authority's limit, leading to financial loss, partner disputes, and regulatory non-compliance. DOA: DM/AM – ₹3L; Manager – ₹5L; Sr. Manager/AVP – ₹15L; VP/SVP – Full.

SD user (Maker) scrutinises documents against checklist, enters bank details in 'HO Bank Details' field in digiCARE, checks the verified checkbox, and submits. Request flows to DOA approval queue. Approver validates and approves/rejects per DOA matrix. Payouts beyond the approver's DOA limit are escalated to the next authority level. Payouts open beyond 5 days escalated to Manager – SD; beyond 6 days to Sr. Manager/AVP – SD. All approvals retained as audit evidence.
Payout Credited to Incorrect / Closed Bank Account

Auto payee creation may fail (e.g., cooperative bank accounts, loan accounts, NRE accounts) or bank details may be incorrect, leading to NEFT failures, payment to wrong accounts, financial loss, and reconciliation issues requiring manual reprocessing.

Auto payee creation occurs post DOA approval; where auto-creation fails, SD Checker user creates a voucher file with all mandatory details and creates a payment number manually via Receivables & Payables >> Payments >> Create Payment. Penny drop failure: bank details verified manually for cooperative banks, loan accounts, and NRE accounts. Payment number approved per DOA. Finance processes NEFT/IMPS and updates UTR in Life Asia. Finance rejects payment number for bank-rejected cases and updates reason in Life Asia. SD team downloads presentment report and reprocesses with valid details. Weekly NEFT reversal MIS reviewed by Process Owner.
Freelook Cancellation Not Processed Within IRDAI TAT / Incorrect Refund

FLC requests not processed within 7-day IRDAI TAT or processed with incorrect refund computation (e.g., non-recovery of GST for NRI policies, premium forfeiture not applied for CFI cases, annuity/survival benefit recovery not done) result in regulatory penalties, customer disputes, and financial misstatement.

Branch uploads mandatory documents in digiCARE and updates retention details. Request moves to HO Retention Queue; if customer not retained, moves to HO Payout team. SD user scrutinises documents vs checklist; enters bank details in HO Bank Details. Retention/sales team notified via email. FLC processed post NSD/exceptional approval. Maker checks verified checkbox; request flows to DOA queue. Auto policy freelook update in Life Asia and auto-payee creation post approval. For NRI: 15CA/CB filing mandatory (Surrender). CFI/FLC NRI GST recovery done manually. Penal interest auto-calculated by Life Asia for delayed payouts.
Incorrect Policy Loan Registration or Unauthorised Disbursement

Policy loan requests may be registered incorrectly in Life Asia (wrong loan amount, IFSC code, payee name) or approved beyond authorised limits, resulting in financial loss, incorrect lien on the policy, and partner disputes. Incorrect loan outstanding deduction from surrender amount for assigned policies may also lead to incorrect payout.

SD Maker scrutinises documents, captures LDR date, bank account number, IFSC, payee name, and loan amount in digiCARE. Maker assigns policy to SUD Life (Contract Servicing >> Minor Alterations >> Assignment) and registers loan in Life Asia (Contract Servicing >> Policy Loans >> Register Policy Loan). SD Checker verifies all details and approves the loan (Contract Servicing >> Policy Loans >> Policy Loan Approval). Payee creation follows same steps as surrender (bank code L1; suspense LPLI). If policy assigned to SUD Life, payout to policy owner after deduction of outstanding loan and accumulated interest.
Breach of IRDAI-Mandated TATs for Policy Servicing Requests

Failure to process OTC, Non-OTC, Financial Non-Payout, and Financial Payout requests within the IRDAI-mandated 7-day TAT (per Master Circular on Protection of Policyholder's Interest 2024) may result in regulatory penalties, penal interest on delayed payouts, customer dissatisfaction, and IGMS escalations.

Daily open case reviews conducted; action taken on higher-ageing cases. PS Inventory MIS reviewed daily by Process Owner. Escalation matrix enforced: OTC open >2 days – Manager/Sr. Manager Central Ops; Non-OTC open >3 days – Manager SD; >5 days – Sr. Manager/AVP SD; Financial Payout open >5 days – Manager SD; >6 days – Sr. Manager/AVP SD. Any service request processed beyond DOA matrix requires Manager & above approval. Penal interest auto-calculated and paid by Life Asia for delayed financial payouts (except CFI & Loan refund).
Penal Interest Not Paid or Incorrectly Calculated for Delayed Payouts

Where financial payouts are delayed beyond IRDAI-mandated timelines, penal interest must be automatically calculated and paid. System failures or gaps in reconciliation may result in penal interest not being triggered, leading to regulatory non-compliance and additional penalties.

Penal interest for delayed payouts is automatically calculated and paid by Life Asia (except CFI and Loan refund cases). Monthly reconciliation is performed by the SD/Finance team to verify that penal interest has been correctly triggered and paid for all delayed cases. Exceptions identified during reconciliation are manually corrected and paid. Reconciliation evidence retained.
Incorrect Payout Calculated for Pension / Annuity Products

Pension and annuity product payouts involve complex benefit structures (commuted value, annuity derivation, surrender eligibility criteria). Incorrect computation may result in over/under payment, financial loss, regulatory non-compliance, and customer disputes. Specific risk: Guaranteed Pension Plan – full surrender only if annuity of ₹1,000/month cannot be derived post commuted amount (60%); Immediate Annuity/Saral Pension – surrender restricted to specific annuity options.

Maker-Checker process for all pension product payment value calculations, as defined. SD team verifies product eligibility for surrender (Immediate Annuity Plan/Saral Pension Plan: only Annuity options 2, 3, 6 (Plan A) and 2, 6 (Plan B) on UW-confirmed critical illness; Guaranteed Pension Plan: full surrender only where annuity of ₹1,000/month cannot be derived post 60% commuted amount). Aarogyam plan: surrender cannot be processed if health claim registered. Monthly sample-checking by Servicing Manager of system-based calculations.
Non-Compliance with KYC / AML Requirements for Policy Servicing

Failure to collect, verify, and update KYC documents (OVD, PAN card, Aadhaar-PAN linkage) during servicing requests (profile changes, payout requests) may result in violations of AML/CFT Master Guidelines 2022, IRDAI regulations, penalties, and facilitation of money laundering/terrorist financing.

For profile changes requiring OVD update: SD user verifies documents and updates OVD details in Life Asia (Clients & Groups >> Client Maintenance >> Modify Client >> AML). PAN Card updated per IRDAI KYC requirements. For all payout requests: Aadhaar-PAN linkage verified in Life Asia before payout approval. For NRI payout: 15CA/CB filed before payment; repartition letter submitted to Finance post authorisation. Documents scanned and stored in Omni-docs for retention as per IRDAI Minimum Information Regulations 2020.
Inadequate Controls for High-Risk Policy Categories

Policies issued under Employer-Employee, Keyman, MWP, and HUF structures carry elevated risk of misuse or incorrect processing due to their complex ownership and beneficiary structures. Inadequate verification may result in incorrect payouts, AML non-compliance, and regulatory penalties.

An additional checkpoint verification is mandated for policies under Employer-Employee, Keyman, MWP, and HUF categories. Employer-Employee assignment is processed by the New Business team, not Service Delivery. All such cases are subject to enhanced scrutiny before any servicing action. FCU verification may be triggered where fraud indicators are present. All approvals documented and retained.
Incorrect Assignment / Re-assignment Affecting Nomination & Payout

Incorrect assignment or re-assignment of a policy may deactivate the nomination incorrectly, result in payout to the wrong party, or fail to reinstate nomination post re-assignment. For policies assigned to banks, outstanding loan deductions at surrender may be missed.

Conditional and absolute assignment processed after document verification in digiCARE by HO Non-Financial team. Nomination auto-deactivated post assignment (except SUD Life loan assignments). Post approval, policy assigned in Life Asia and request auto-closed in digiCARE. Re-assignment: Branch raises request with all mandatory documents; child case for Nominee addition auto-created; SD user verifies and approves in digiCARE; policy re-assigned and nomination reinstated (Contract Servicing >> Minor Alterations >> Reassignment). For assigned policies at payout: payment made to policy owner after deduction of outstanding loan and accumulated interest.
Failure to Send Timely Acknowledgement, Requirement, or Rejection Communication

Failure to send timely acknowledgement (SMS/email/letter) for service requests, communicate additional requirements (CFR), or inform customers of rejection may violate IRDAI policyholder protection norms, lead to customer dissatisfaction, IGMS complaints, and regulatory penalties.

System automatically sends SMS/email acknowledgement upon request registration. For CFR (requirements from customer): SMS/email/letter with requirements sent; if customer does not respond within 3 days, request auto-closed. For rejection: SMS/email/letter with rejection reason sent to customer. Post-request closure: SMS/email communication auto-sent by system. Payout communications uploaded in Omni-docs. Annual communications (bonus statement, unit statement, pension statement) sent yearly. Regulatory communications reviewed quarterly (BAP report, compliance checklist, AML reporting).
Uncleared Suspense Balances and Untracked Payee Creation

Unmonitored suspense balances (arising from CFI premium forfeiture, CFI/FLC NRI GST recovery, bank-rejected payments, and auto payee creation failures) may result in financial misstatement, unidentified liabilities, and regulatory exposure.

Suspense management MIS reviewed weekly by Process Owner  Payee created management report reviewed daily. NEFT reversals reviewed weekly. PS Inventory reviewed daily. CFI premium forfeiture: SD cancels policy and informs respective team to knock off suspense. CFI payout recovery: SD recovers amount manually from final payout and informs Finance to knock off suspense. CFI/FLC NRI GST infused: recovered manually from final payout.
Recurring Processing Errors Due to Absence of Quality Review

Without periodic quality checks and complaint monitoring, systematic processing errors, incorrect decisions, or non-adherence to SOP may go undetected, leading to recurring regulatory breaches, customer complaints (IGMS), and audit findings.

PS Quality Check performed monthly by Servicing Manager using sample-checking methodology to verify accuracy of processing decisions and calculations. Monthly review of complaints related to servicing. Complaint trends analysed; root causes identified and corrective actions documented. BAP Report, Compliance Checklist, and AML Reporting submitted to regulator quarterly. SOP reviewed and updated periodically by the team.
Non-Compliance with NRI Payout Requirements (15CA/CB, Repartition)

For NRI policyholders, failure to file Form 15CA/CB before payout, non-submission of repartition letter, incorrect TDS application, or use of incorrect bank account type (NRE vs NRO) may result in FEMA violations, income tax non-compliance, regulatory penalties, and financial loss.

For surrender/payout to NRI customers: Form 15CA/CB filed by the Taxation team before payment authorisation. Repartition letter submitted to Finance post payment authorisation. NRI status verified in digiCARE during request registration (NRI status field mandatory). Penny drop failure for NRE accounts: bank details are verified manually. RAG matrix applied for bank account mismatch scenarios.
Fraudulent Payout Processed Without FCU Verification

High-risk payout scenarios (Red RAG: different source bank account and contact number; bank statement not provided; customer not ready to share OTP at branch) require FCU or video verification. Bypassing FCU controls may result in fraudulent payout, financial loss, and regulatory non-compliance.

Red RAG cases (≥₹2 lakh): Outsourced Video Verification/Video KYC with SLA (T+1 data to agency; T+3 FCU revert; T+4 processing). Bank statement not provided: Service Delivery Head approval or FCU approval mandatory. Customer walk-in at branch/not ready to share OTP: Zonal Operation Head approval is required. FCU verification: customer considered verified if any two parameters confirmed (DOB, Nominee Name, Address, Premium Mode, Modal Premium, Sum Assured). Non-contactable customers referred to FCU team.
Failure to Identify & Intimate Policyholders Before Due Date

If payout data is not extracted sufficiently in advance or intimation is not triggered via letter/email/SMS, policyholders may not submit required documents in time, causing payment delays beyond IRDAI TAT, penal interest liability, and unclaimed amount build-up.

Payout data extracted from Life Asia monthly batch file in advance: T-180 days (general), T-90 days (maturity non-pension), T-365 days (pension). System-triggered intimation via letter, email, and SMS to policyholder with the list of all requirements to be called for. Calls allocated from HO to branches for customer tracking. Reminder communications sent on defined frequency for non-responsive policyholders. All requirements called for in one go. CRM raised for each case to track document receipt and follow-up.
Inability to Procure Bank Details / Documents for Non-STP Cases Causing Delays

For non-STP cases where no active credit mandate exists, failure to procure bank details through internal sources (flat file, application form, CRM scrubbing, PAN scrubbing, tele-calling) or external vendor within defined timelines results in extended open cases, delayed payouts, penal interest, and movement to unclaimed.

Internal sources pursued in sequence: NB/renewal flat file, application form, CRM/bank/other tracker scrubbing, client-level data scrubbing, PAN scrubbing, tele-calling, ISO visit to policyholder's address, data allocation to branches. CRM raised under 'request' if bank details found; under 'query' with outcome remarks if not found. External vendor allocated after all internal sources exhausted. Vendor documents verified by Fin Ops within T+15 days of receipt. CRM raised under 'request' for verified cases; vendor informed of deficiencies. Vendor continues tracing for 6 months; outcome remarks shared with SUD thereafter. Vendor TAT monitored daily.
Payout Processed to Invalid or Unverified Bank Account

Payout credited to an invalid, closed, or mismatched bank account due to failure to perform mandatory IMPS/KARZA verification, incorrect name matching, or bypassing bank validation for source/non-source accounts. Results in payment failure, NEFT rejection, financial loss, fraud exposure, and unclaimed accumulation.

IMPS/KARZA verification is mandatory before payment for all accounts (source and non-source). KARZA provides real-time validation (₹1 credited). Name matching criteria strictly applied: full name match accepted; partial/abbreviated names accepted based on KYC; joint accounts based on KYC and bank statement; current accounts if individual proprietary. Mismatch or failed validation triggers alternate account proof requirement from policyholder. KARZA not successful for cooperative/rural/gramin banks and NRE accounts – IMPS used in those cases. Source account verified through maker-checker process; non-source accounts subject to RAG matrix. All verification responses uploaded in DMS. Exception to be approved by supervisor.
Fraudulent or AML-Risk Payout via Non-Source Bank Account

Non-source bank account payouts carry elevated fraud and money-laundering risk. Failure to apply the RAG matrix (Red/Amber/Green classification), perform mandatory tele-verification/video KYC, or obtain FCU clearance for high-risk cases may result in fraudulent payout, financial loss, regulatory penalties under AML/CFT guidelines, and reputational damage.

RAG matrix mandatorily applied for all non-source bank account payouts. Classification determines verification mode: Green cases processed directly post bank validation. Amber cases: tele-calling with specific verification parameters (any 2 of: DOB, Nominee Name, Address, Premium Mode, Modal Premium, Sum Assured confirmed). Red cases: tele-calling for <₹2L; outsourced Video Verification/Video KYC for ≥₹2L. FCU referral for non-contactable or failed verification. Deviation matrix: Outsourced video verification OR positive FCU report OR AVP recommendation with HOD sign-off required. Checker verifies RAG matrix compliance before approval in BPOS. Source account exceptions (NRI/PIO, assigned policies, different payor-policyholder, pension, multiple accounts with specific payout request) also processed post document receipt.
Incorrect Payout Processed Due to Inadequate Maker-Checker Controls

Payouts may be processed with incorrect beneficiary details, wrong bank accounts, incorrect payout amounts, or without proper document scrutiny if maker-checker segregation is not enforced, or if the same person acts as both maker and checker. Results in financial loss, wrong payouts, regulatory non-compliance, and audit findings.

Strict segregation: HO Maker and Checker report to different line managers. Maker at Branch: verifies documents per checklist, registers case in CRM, scans documents to CRM/Omni, inputs bank details in BPOS. Maker at HO: extracts report, scrutinises documents per checklist, verifies RAG matrix, validates independent bank verification response, verifies bank details in BPOS, sends discrepancies to branch. Checker at HO: independently validates bank account details in BPOS, verifies RAG matrix compliance, validates IMPS/KARZA response, resolves mismatches via supervisor, activates bank details in Life Asia only on confirmation. Cases sent for DOA approval in advance; moved to approval bucket on due date. Maker, Checker, and Approver are not the same person.
Payout Approved by Unauthorised or Insufficiently Authorised Personnel

Payouts approved by personnel without adequate delegation of authority may result in unauthorised payouts, exceeding approval limits, financial misstatement, and regulatory non-compliance. DOA matrix: Manager ≤₹10L; Sr. Manager ≤₹20L; AVP ≤₹50L; SVP >₹50L.

Customised payout approval authority granted based on skill, experience, and DOA within defined limits: Manager up to ₹10 Lakhs; Sr. Manager up to ₹20 Lakhs; AVP up to ₹50 Lakhs; SVP above ₹50 Lakhs. Cases queued for approval in BPOS/Life Asia; approved on due date as per DOA. Checker validates all checkpoints before approving in BPOS. For bank account mismatch cases, checker escalates to supervisor before approval. Finance team authorises payment reference number per financial matrix post Fin Ops approval. High-value cases escalated to appropriate DOA level before payment release.
Delayed Payouts Beyond Regulatory TAT / Penal Interest Not Paid

Payouts not made within IRDAI-mandated TAT result in penal interest liability at RBI bank rate fixed at start of FY. Penal interest not paid alongside main benefit, or bank rate not applied correctly, constitutes regulatory non-compliance under IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2017, attracts IRDAI inquiry and penalties.

Life Asia Payout Pending Report reviewed daily by Management to monitor open cases. Business MIS/PPT reviewed monthly. Penal interest auto-calculated and auto-paid by Life Asia for all delayed cases (except CFI and Loan refund). Finance team validates penal interest calculation before payment. Quarterly regulatory reporting: penal interest paid (Claims & Benefits), claims ageing data, claims movement data, benefits paid (statewise) – submitted to IRDAI. Vendor performance for document/COE collection monitored daily for early settlement to minimise penal interest. Bank rate per RBI applied from start of FY for penal interest computation. 8.50% for 25-26 as per SOP.
Maturity Payout Made to Wrong Beneficiary / Incorrect Amount

Maturity benefit paid to incorrect beneficiary (e.g., to life assured instead of policyholder where they differ; wrong HUF Karta; assigned policies paid to policyholder instead of assignee; MWP policies paid to beneficiary instead of trustee; minor life assured where beneficial interest not transferred on majority) or incorrect net amount (policy loan outstanding not deducted) results in financial loss, legal disputes, and regulatory non-compliance.

Payment rules applied: (a) Where Life Assured(LA) wa minor – beneficial interest transfer checked; (b) Different policyholder and LA – payment to policyholder; (c) HUF – payment to Karta; (d) Assigned policies – payment to assignee (discharge from assignee required if assignee declines); (e) Policy loan – outstanding loan and interest deducted before payout; (f) MWP policies – payment to trustee; (g) Death post maturity date but before payment – payment to valid nominee per Insurance Laws Amendment Act 2015. Checker verifies beneficiary and payment amount against Life Asia records before approval. Fin Ops identifies policies in death status and hands over to Death Claims team. PAN card verified and updated in LA before payout.
Incorrect Processing of Pension Maturity (Commutation / Annuity Purchase)

Pension maturity requires: commutation of 1/3 or 60% (per product T&C) paid to policyholder; balance 2/3 or 40% used to purchase annuity from SUD or open market. Incorrect split, failure to transfer funds to new business suspense for SUD annuity, or incorrect NEFT payout to open-market insurer, or non-compliance with IRDAI minimum annuity of ₹1,000/month may result in regulatory non-compliance and financial misstatement.

Pension maturity: commuted amount (1/3 or 60% per product T&C) paid to policyholder; balance for annuity purchase. If SUD annuity: funds transferred to new business suspense; annuity policy issued. If open market: NEFT/cheque payout in favour of insurer. Annuity option sheet mandatory (per document checklist). IRDAI minimum annuity amount (₹1,000/month) verified; if corpus insufficient, entire proceeds paid such proceeds of the policy may be paid to the policyholder or beneficiary as lump sum. . Annuity option form collected before processing. Checker verifies split computation and fund transfer/payout routing before approval.
Annuity Paid Without Valid COE / Overpayment Post Death of Annuitant

Annuity paid without a valid Certificate of Existence (COE) constitutes payment to a potentially deceased annuitant, resulting in excess annuity payments that must be recovered from death claim or purchase price. COE not validated at client level (all SUD annuity policies clubbed) may miss validity lapse across multiple policies.

COE collected once per year from annuitant. On every month, if COE is valid, annuity liability generated by Life Asia (currently 26th of each month); payee codes created for payout. If COE invalid/expired: system generates liability but suppresses payee code creation – payment cannot proceed. Post COE update: system auto-creates payee code on T+1. COE validated at client level (all SUD annuity policies clubbed). Video verification by vendor (Gowel Next) for COE collection where direct contact fails. CRM raised by Policy Servicing team for COE updation. Annuities not paid immediately post new issuance – paid on next monthly cycle with broken period. Authorised signatories for COE: Bank Branch Manager, Gazetted Officer, Registered Medical Practitioner, Postmaster, School/College Principal, SUD Official (Manager and above), Class I Govt Official.
Excess Annuity Paid Post Death Not Recovered

If annuity continues to be paid after the annuitant's death (before COE check cycle) or where life annuity option was not selected, excess payments must be recovered. Failure to identify and recover excess annuity from death claim or purchase price leads to financial loss.

Life Asia auto-handles annuity on death claim registration: if non-life annuity option selected – system stops future annuity and recovers excess paid from date of death from death claim. If life annuity option selected – system stops future annuity and recovers excess if any from death claim. Joint annuity: annuity to second annuitant released only after first annuitant's death claim registered in system. Policy surrender: system generates outstanding payouts and stops future payouts/liabilities. Finance reverses payment reference number for bank rejections; reason updated in Life Asia.
Survival Benefit Paid for Ineligible Policies (Lapsed / Death / Incorrect Status)

Survival benefit paid to a lapsed policy (no entitlement), or processed for a policy where the life assured is deceased (should be death claim), or survival benefit previously paid discovered posthumously (to be recovered from death claim) results in incorrect financial outflows, regulatory non-compliance, and customer/legal disputes.

Before processing survival benefit: policy status checked in Life Asia. If policy is lapsed: no survival benefit payable; request handed to Customer Engagement team. If policy status is death: survival benefit request handed to Claims team for processing as unpaid survival benefits under death claim settlement. If policy is in force or paid-up: survival benefit processed per product terms and conditions. Unpaid survival benefits fallen due before death are processed and paid while settling death claim. Outstanding loan and loan interest deducted from survival benefit before payout. All payouts in electronic mode only; exception requires supervisor approval. Maker-Checker and DOA matrix applied. TDS validation by Finance/Taxation; penal interest check by Fin Ops.
Incorrect Termination Payout for ULIP / Non-ULIP Policies

For non-ULIP policies there is no termination payout, so processing a payout would be erroneous. For ULIP, termination only occurs post revival period; fund value is payable immediately. System-driven CRM auto-generation on DigiCare for terminated cases (live). Non-STP cases (NRI, assigned policies) sent to branches. Errors in classification may result in wrong payouts.

System (DigiCare) auto-generates work item for terminated cases on due date based on STP/Non-STP rule engine. STP cases: payout generated post maker-checker. Non-STP cases (NRI, Assignment): allocated to respective SUD branch for further action. Non-ULIP termination: no payout generated (policy feature). ULIP: fund value payable immediately post lock-in/revival period expiry on customer silence. Fin Ops verifies: policy in death status – handed to Death Claims; PAN card checked and updated in LA; fraudulent/suspicious cases referred to FCU. Bank details verified per source/non-source rules. IMPS/KARZA verification mandatory. NRI cases: FATCA + 15CA/CB before payment (T+2 days post Tax team confirmation).
Failed / Rejected Payments Not Reprocessed Timely Leading to Unclaimed

NEFT rejections (bank account closed, invalid IFSC, name mismatch, cooperative/rural bank issues) not actioned promptly result in payments remaining in suspense, exceeding 365-day limit, and moving to unclaimed. Internal rejections not reviewed and reprocessed result in delayed payouts and penal interest.

Finance team reverses payment reference number on bank rejection and updates reason in Life Asia. Rejected cases visible in LA Payout Pending report (reviewed daily) and individual presentment report. Internal rejections: reviewed and reprocessed immediately. External rejections: Fin Ops activates multiple recovery activities (tele-calling, branch allocation, vendor engagement, alternate bank account collection). If no alternate bank account received: case moves to unclaimed after365 days . Payout letter with payment details (success/failure) sent to policyholder via letter/SMS/email. Finance Reconciliation MIS reviewed monthly. Electronic mode mandatory; cheque issuance stopped.
Proposal Deposit Refund Made to Incorrect Account or Wrong Amount

Pre-issuance refunds (PNR, withdrawal, postpone, decline, reject, excess premium) may be processed to incorrect bank account, wrong amount, or without verifying source account details, resulting in financial loss, customer disputes, and reconciliation failures.

Individual NB refunds: account details in Life Asia matched against flat file at time of payment; if matching, payment processed directly. If mismatch: department verifies payee, obtains customer request, corrects bank details; case processed in Life Asia and sent for payment authorisation. Sundry account receipts: refund to customer bank account from application form, subject to bank account proof from customer. Payment approver checks correctness of payment and amount per DOA in Life Asia. Finance team takes dump of payment reference numbers and authorises after verifying transactions. Consolidated payment voucher authorised before Finance processes payment. Refund tracker maintained manually to track all refund transactions and prevent miss-outs. Group NB refunds: payment made to same account from where amount received; bank account details of payor verified. Payment voucher authorised per DOA by seniors. Failed transactions: payment reference numbers reversed; amount moved to unclaimed fund account if not processed within 365 days.
Excess Premium Not Identified / Refunded Timely

Premium suspense balances representing excess collections may remain unrefunded due to failure to download and scrutinise the premium suspense report from BI Portal, or failure to procure bank details for cases where account details are not available, resulting in unclaimed amount accumulation.

Fin Ops downloads premium suspense report from BI Portal. Scrutiny of cases with available account numbers. Bank verification (IMPS/KARZA) for cleared cases. Payment reference number created in Life Asia; approved per DOA. Finance team authorises approved payment reference numbers. Voucher created and approved by Fin Ops. Unsuccessful transactions: payment reference reversed by Finance; policy falls back to premium suspense report. Cases with no bank details sent to branches for customer document procurement. Cases not processed within 365 days moved to unclaimed bucket. Finance Reconciliation MIS reviewed monthly for open suspense items.
Amounts Not Moved to Unclaimed Within 365 Days of Due Date

Amounts payable but not settled within 365 days from liability creation/due date must be moved to unclaimed as per IRDAI Master Circular on Unclaimed Amounts. Failure to identify and move amounts timely is a regulatory violation, resulting in penalties, IRDAI scrutiny, and incorrect financial disclosure. Specific timelines: maturity/termination – T+365 from due date; surrender – T+180; vesting – T+365; proposal deposits – T+365; payment failures from suspense – T+365.

Cases crossing 365 days from liability creation (or specific timelines per unclaimed movement matrix) are system-moved to unclaimed. Fin Ops downloads consolidated unclaimed report from BI Portal daily. Data distributed zone-wise for case closure. Unclaimed report reviewed daily by Management. BI Portal and recon module used to check premiums received and payments made. Customer intimation sent once a year via reminder communication requesting documents. Display of unclaimed amounts on website per IRDAI requirement (policy No., PAN, Name, DOB, Aadhaar search facility). Policy-wise detailed records of unclaimed amounts and interest/investment income maintained. Concurrent Auditor verification quarterly. Separate agenda placed before Policyholders' Protection Committee with age-wise analysis, settlement progress, and reduction steps. Form A & B with committee meeting minutes submitted to IRDAI half-yearly.
Increase in Unclaimed Amount / Non-Reduction of Existing Unclaimed

Failure to actively pursue settlement of unclaimed cases through multi-channel activities results in growing unclaimed portfolio, increased penal interest exposure, regulatory action, and customer harm. Unclaimed amounts must be actively reduced through customer tracing.

Internal activities: NB data scrubbing (application forms, DMS documents); renewal data from flat file; tele-calling using contact numbers from application form and system; data allocation to branches; ISO visit to policyholder's address; PAN-based data extraction; CRM raised with remarks after all internal efforts. External activities: PAN-based data sharing to vendor for multi-modal investigation. On receipt of customer documents: case moved from unclaimed bucket to specific payout suspense; bank details verified via IMPS/KARZA; auto payment generated; approved per DOA; Finance authorises. Cheque issuance stopped; digital NEFT to bank accounts only. SMS sent to respective bank branches for digital credit. Finance Reconciliation MIS monthly; Unclaimed Report daily; IRDAI quarterly reports (Claims Ageing, Unclaimed Ageing, Settlement Progress, L-39, L-40).

Amounts not settled within 10 years from liability creation must be transferred to Senior Citizens Welfare Fund (SCWF). Failure to transfer timely, notify IRDAI within 7 days, maintain policy-wise records, or adjust claims received before SCWF transfer constitutes regulatory non-compliance under IRDAI Master Circular on Unclaimed Amounts §13-17.

Amounts not settled within 10 years from liability creation date transferred to SCWF. IRDAI notified within 7 days of transfer date in prescribed format. If customer approaches within 25 years: recalled from SCWF and paid. If any claim received from policyholder before SCWF transfer: amount adjusted from amount due for SCWF transfer before remitting. Policy-wise detailed records of unclaimed amounts and interest/investment income maintained. Concurrent Auditor verifies unclaimed amounts and income credited thereon on quarterly basis. Policyholders' Protection Committee: separate agenda with age-wise analysis, settlement progress, steps to reduce; Form A & B with committee meeting minutes submitted to IRDAI half-yearly.
Incorrect Group Benefit Payout (Fund Adequacy / Wrong Beneficiary / Unauthorised Amount)

Group scheme payouts (Gratuity, Leave Encashment, Savings Linked, Superannuation) to wrong master policyholder, without verifying fund adequacy, or without proper DOA approval may result in financial loss, scheme trustee disputes, and regulatory non-compliance.

Request received from Master Policyholder via HR department/Group Sales team. Registered in CRM with documents uploaded. Fin Ops extracts case list from CRM. Payment and bank account details verified against proposal form and service request. Fund adequacy in master policyholder's fund verified before processing. Payment reference created in Group Asia. Finance team extracts unapproved payment reference list from Group Asia, verifies details, and shares approval remarks with Fin Ops. Fin Ops prepares and approves payment voucher per DOA. Finance processes payment and communicates success/failure to Fin Ops. Successful payouts: records updated; unit statement sent for ULIP. Failed payouts: payment reference recreated after details correction. Communication sent to client on successful payment.
Non-Electronic Payout Processed in Violation of IRDAI Circular

IRDAI Circular ref. IRDA/F&A/CIR/GLD/056/02/2014 mandates all maturity, survival benefit, and other policyholder payments only through electronic mode (NEFT/IMPS/EFT). Cheque issuance or cash payment constitutes regulatory non-compliance, attracts penalties, and creates audit findings.

All payouts processed through electronic mode only (NEFT/IMPS/EFT). Cheque issuance stopped. Exceptions to electronic mode only processed with supervisor approval and documented. Auto payment generated in Life Asia using bank account details available in system. Payment reference authorised by Finance and processed through bank. SMS notifications sent to policyholder and respective bank branches confirming digital credit. All outgoing customer communications (acknowledgement, requirement, payment confirmation) sent via letter, SMS, or email – no physical cash or cheque issued.
Non-Whitelisted SMS Sent to Policyholders in Violation of IRDAI Circular

Sending non-registered or non-whitelisted SMS messages to policyholders (intimation, acknowledgement, payment confirmation) violates IRDAI Circular on Fraudulent Messages/Unsolicited Commercial Messages (24-03-2021), exposes policyholders to fraud risk, and results in regulatory non-compliance.

Only registered/whitelisted SMS templates sent to policyholders. No deviation or system bypass permitted. Communication channels for customer contact: letter, SMS, email as per approved templates. Form and communication changes require prior Compliance team approval with 5-day follow-up frequency; escalation to Head – Compliance if delayed beyond two weeks. All compliance approvals stored in Fin Ops records before release. System-generated communications use pre-approved templates only.
Fraudulent Payout Processed Due to Inadequate Fraud Detection
