Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Errors in depreciation calculation and asset valuation
Useful life may be applied incorrectly or depreciation markers (I/V/D) misused, resulting in wrong depreciation expense and misstated asset values.

Finance reviews FAR entries to confirm correct use of markers – I (Initial Value) for new assets, V (Additional Value) for additions, D (Depreciation). Useful life is applied as per policy (Computer Hardware 3/6 yrs, Software 3 yrs, Furniture 10 yrs, AC 10 yrs, etc.).
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Incorrect capitalisation and depreciation start dates
Assets may be capitalised before being 'put to use' or with incorrect dates, causing inaccurate depreciation start dates and misstated liabilities.
Assets are capitalised only upon receipt of a formal 'put-to-use' confirmation from the user department or project owner. The commission date drives depreciation start in FAR.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Inaccurate tracking and capitalisation of CWIP
Capital Work in Progress may not be tracked or cleared properly, leading to open items, wrong capitalisation, and misstated balances.

Finance maintains a detailed CWIP register capturing project codes, vendor details, invoices, and capitalisation status. Operations management periodically reviews CWIP and communicates assets put into service to Finance for capitalisation.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Capex payments without proper approval and documentation
Capex payouts may be processed without proper DOA approval or missing supporting documents (invoice, PO, delivery challan, PCCC), weakening documentation integrity.

All Capex payouts require approval strictly as per the DOA matrix before processing. Supporting documents (original tax invoice, delivery challan, PO, PCCC approval) are verified before releasing payment.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Regulatory non-compliance in tax deductions on Capex
Incorrect deduction of TDS/GST at payout stage may result in regulatory non-compliance and penalties.

Finance checks every Capex payout to ensure TDS/GST is deducted correctly as per law and vendor type. System rules and invoice details are used for validation. Any errors are fixed before releasing payment, and balances are reconciled regularly with statutory returns.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Mismatch between financial ledgers and Fixed Asset Register (FAR)
Financial ledgers may not reconcile with FAR, causing discrepancies in gross block, depreciation block, and net block reporting.

Finance reconciles FAR with financial ledgers regularly (gross block, accumulated depreciation, net block – category-wise). Any differences are investigated, corrected with documentation, and reviewed by management.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Improper mapping of IT asset codes between FAR and IT register
IT asset codes may not be properly mapped between FAR and IT register, leading to reconciliation gaps and risk of untracked assets.

Finance and IT periodically reconcile FAR with the IT asset register to ensure proper code mapping and complete tracking. Sun code is mapped by IT against each asset serial number. Mismatches are corrected with documentation and reviewed by management.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Inadequate physical verification of fixed assets
Annual physical verification may be delayed, incomplete, or not reconciled with FAR, resulting in unreported losses, disposals, or damaged assets.

Finance and user teams (IT / Facility) carry out annual physical verification in Q3/Q4. Results are reconciled with FAR, and any losses, disposals, or damaged assets are investigated, documented, approved, and updated in records.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Incorrect disposal and insurance accounting of assets
Assets disposed may not be removed timely from FAR, or insurance recoveries may not be booked correctly, leading to misstated profit/loss.

Finance promptly removes disposed assets from FAR upon competent authority approval and records insurance recoveries correctly. All disposal entries are verified, approved, and ledgers updated to keep profit/loss accurate.
Fixed Asset Addition, Deletion and Depreciation
Untagged or mis-tagged assets leading to tracking failures
Assets without pre-numbered identification tags may be misidentified, duplicated in FAR, or remain untracked during physical verification.

Pre-numbered identification tags are affixed to fixed assets on acquisition. IT team maps Sun FAR codes against serial numbers in the IT register. Facility team codes non-IT assets. Tags are verified during annual physical verification.
Misstatement of financial statements due to inaccurate monthly closing
Financial statements may be misstated if monthly closing activities (expense booking, provisioning, advance consumption, depreciation, vendor confirmations) are delayed, inaccurate, or incomplete.

Finance closes books each month by recording expenses, making provisions with HOD approval, posting depreciation, and adjusting advances. Vendor balances are confirmed annually, and all entries are reviewed and documented.
Omission or inaccuracy in Notes to Accounts
Missing or incorrect disclosures in Notes to Accounts (MSMED, related party, director remuneration, capital commitments, CSR) can lead to qualified audit opinions and regulatory action.

Finance prepares Notes to Accounts on a quarterly basis covering: operating lease commitments (lock-in basis), capital commitments (PO/IT/Facility input), MSMED disclosures (vendor registration list), related party (Dai-ichi GLs), director remuneration (IRDA approval + HR input), CSR (Board approval + GL). All notes are reviewed by AVP before submission to Reporting team.
Delay or omission in MIS and regulatory reporting
Failure to prepare or submit MIS and regulatory reports on time may result in inadequate oversight, management blind spots, and regulatory non-compliance (IRDAI outsourcing report).

Finance prepares and circulates defined MIS reports: TAT/EOD report (daily – Finance HOD), payroll statutory reconciliation (monthly – HR), Opex Schedule-3 analysis (monthly – Finance HOD), Opex PPT (monthly – Finance dept), IRDA Outsourcing report (quarterly/annual – Auditors/IRDAI). Reports are maintained in the common Finance folder.
Missing or inaccurate security deposit confirmations
Failure to obtain yearly confirmations may lead to audit issues or misstatement of balances.
Finance team obtains security deposit confirmations from banks/landlords on a yearly basis, matches confirmations with internal records, and submits to auditors as part of annual audit documentation.
Unauthorised or duplicate vendor masters leading to fraudulent payments
Vendor masters created without proper KYC (PAN, GST, cancelled cheque) or with duplicate codes may facilitate fraudulent payments or tax mismatches.

Vendor master is created only after receipt of duly filled vendor master creation form along with KYC documents (PAN, GST registration, address proof, cancelled cheque). GL codes are reviewed annually; duplicate codes are deactivated in SUN & VMS. Inactive codes (no transaction >2 years) are also deactivated.
Inability to raise invoices due to missing Financial Year Master
If the Financial Year Master is not created at year start, invoices and claims cannot be raised in the new period, causing operational delays.

Finance team creates the Financial Year Master in both EMS and VMS at the beginning of each financial year (April 1). This is a mandatory step before the first invoice/claim of the new FY can be raised.
Failure to establish, approve, or implement a Board-approved policy may result in regulatory non-compliance, penalties, reputational damage, and operational inefficiencies.

Board of Directors approves the commission and agent appointment policy. Finance & Accounts ensures implementation and periodic review of Board-approved policies and co-ordinates with Compliance to monitor IRDAI adherence; approvals and policy documents are retained.
Inconsistent Processes Due to Outdated / Unapproved SOPs
Inconsistent or undocumented processes due to outdated policies may result in accounting errors, reconciliation failures, and regulatory non-compliance.
SOPs are reviewed and updated periodically with version control maintained. Regular training ensures team adherence to current procedures.
Absence of Documented Policy and Procedure for Policy Accounting

Policy accounting activities may be performed without standardized guidance if there is no formally defined and documented SOP, resulting in errors in accounting entries, reconciliation failures, non-compliance with regulatory requirements, and increased risk of fraud or misstatement.

Finance team prepares and maintains a documented SOP for all policy accounting processes including receipt of bank files, reconciliations, journal postings, refunds, and reporting. The SOP is reviewed and updated as processes change.
Flat Files Not Received from Banks
Required flat files from banks may not be received on time or at all, resulting in delays in policy accounting, incomplete reconciliations, and potential misstatement of financial records.

Finance team checks daily if files are received from banks. If not received, the concerned bank IT department is informed via email and follow-up is done until receipt. Delays are escalated per the defined escalation matrix.
Flat File Does Not Match Bank Statement

The flat file received from the bank may contain discrepancies when compared to the bank statement, leading to incorrect reconciliations, inaccurate postings in the policy accounting system, and potential misstatement of financial records.

Flat files are reconciled against bank statements before upload. Any discrepancies are investigated and resolved with the bank or operations team prior to posting in the Recon module. Upload proceeds only after confirmation of accuracy. Known standard differences (e.g., BOI cheque dishonour entries, EPAY reversals) are documented and handled per defined protocol.
Flat File Format Mismatch Not Properly Handled
When bank flat files do not match the standard format, delays or incorrect manual handling can lead to missing, duplicated, or misclassified transactions.

Finance team performs sample data quality checks after uploading bank flat files into the Recon module. The system enforces format validations and blocks non-standard uploads. If a format mismatch is detected, the team reports the issue to the bank or manually adjusts the file before re-uploading. The Recon module also prevents duplicate uploads by validating transaction ID, date, and amount.
The same flat file may be uploaded more than once, resulting in duplicate transactions in the policy accounting system, causing reconciliation issues and potential misstatement of financial records.

System logic is built-in to prevent double upload of flat files in the Recon module. The Recon module displays an error message if a user attempts to upload a duplicate file (validated on Application Name, Transaction ID, Date, and Amount).
RPA BOT Tally Errors or False Positives
BOT may fail to correctly tally statements with flat files, or flag false discrepancies, causing incorrect acceptance or unnecessary manual intervention and delayed postings.

Finance team monitors BOT-generated alerts when discrepancies are flagged between bank statements and flat files. If the BOT fails to tally correctly or raises false positives, the team investigates the issue and manually uploads the corrected files into the Recon module.
Manual Consolidation Errors in CSV Files
Combining multiple CSV files in Excel can introduce data loss (e.g., leading zeros), misalignment, or accidental edits, causing inaccurate uploads.

Finance team performs quality checks when manually consolidating CSV files in Excel. They ensure correct formatting, preserve leading zeros, and validate alignment before uploading to the Recon module.
Excluding 'after 3 PM' transactions or removing 'previous day uploaded' records may cause omissions or double counting if timing rules are applied inconsistently.

Finance team applies consistent timing rules for transaction inclusion. Transactions after 3 PM or from previous days are flagged and reviewed during daily reconciliation to prevent omissions or double counting.
CASA files being uploaded separately and not consolidated may bypass standard checks, leading to inconsistent validations and potential posting errors.

CASA files are handled separately with distinct validation steps. Finance team ensures these files undergo format checks and are reconciled independently before upload to avoid bypassing standard controls.
eAB / eCB Limited Fields Processing Risk
Limited fields in eAB/eCB files and manual upload in UBI format may cause incomplete mapping or missing attributes, leading to partial or incorrect postings.
Finance team manually reviews eAB/eCB files and supplements missing attributes before uploading in UBI format. This ensures completeness and correct mapping.
Manual Upload Without Adequate Authorization or Segregation
Manual upload steps may be performed without proper authorization or independent review, increasing the risk of unauthorized changes or fraud.
Manual uploads are subject to maker-checker validation. Finance team ensures uploads are independently reviewed and approved to prevent unauthorized changes.
Group / New Business / Renewal Transaction Misclassification
Errors in classifying transactions among NB, Renewal, and Group accounts may misstate revenue and affect downstream policy accounting and reporting.
Finance team validates transaction classification (NB, Renewal, Group) during reconciliation. Misclassified entries are corrected before posting.
Accounting of Collection in Policy Administration System
Journal Entry Not Passed in Life Asia / Group Asia
Failure to pass the required journal entry in Life Asia / Group Asia for bank collections may result in incomplete accounting, reconciliation mismatches, and misstated financial balances.

Daily flat file vs journal entries are verified as part of EOD checklist. Daily bank reconciliation is done for premium collection accounts to identify differences. Any difference is identified during the Proposal Deposit Reconciliation on a daily basis.
Accounting of Collection in Policy Administration System
Journal Entry Does Not Match Flat File
Discrepancies between the journal entry passed in Life Asia / Group Asia and the flat file data may result in incorrect accounting entries and reconciliation failures.

Journal entry is verified by checker before approval by downloading each bank flat file from the Recon module. Differences are identified during collection bank reconciliation. During daily Proposal Deposit Reconciliation, any mismatch is identified.
Accounting of Collection in Policy Administration System
Incorrect GL Selection While Passing Journal Vouchers
Incorrect selection of Life Asia / Group Asia GL codes while passing JVs can result in misclassification of balances and distort financial reporting.

BI report creates asset and liability GL-wise values for premium collection accounts, which is used to pass journal entries. Checker verifies the GL entry before approval in the LA/GA system. Deposit balance reconciliation is done on a daily basis to identify compensating differences.
Accounting of Collection in Policy Administration System
Incorrect Entry for Bucket Shifting Items in Life Asia / Group Asia
Incorrect bucket shifting entries in Life Asia / Group Asia can result in misclassification of funds and inaccurate account balances.

BI report for bucket shifting is configured to provide 'From' and 'To' GLs by which user creates JV in LA/GA. Incorrect shifting entries, if any, are identified on daily basis during Proposal Deposit Reconciliation.
Delay in Completing Policy Accounting Processes Within Defined TAT

Policy accounting activities such as flat file upload, reconciliation, and related actions may not be completed within the defined TAT, leading to delays in financial reporting, reconciliations, and customer payouts.

Finance team tracks completion of accounting activities against defined TAT. Delays are escalated per the escalation matrix (Level 1: Manager/Sr. Manager; Level 2: AVP/Process Owner; Level 3: SVP Finance and Accounts) to ensure timely reporting and payouts.
Delay in sending ARF receipts to Microcom or posting in Sun System may result in incomplete accounting and misstatement of balances.
Finance team monitors ARF receipts daily and ensures timely posting in Sun System. Delays are flagged and followed up with Microcom.
Incorrect Matching of ARF Receipts with Bank Collections
Errors in matching receipts with bank collections (due to manual VLOOKUP or data mismatch) can lead to incorrect re-credit/reversal entries and inaccurate financial records.
Finance team uses VLOOKUP to match ARF receipts with bank collections. Mismatches are identified and corrected before posting re-credit or reversal entries.
Unrealized Receipts Not Followed Up (Credit Awaited Items)
Receipts marked as 'credit awaited' may not be tracked or escalated timely, causing prolonged unreconciled items and inaccurate reporting.
Finance team tracks unrealized receipts marked as credit awaited and shares pending items with branches for follow-up. Escalations are made for prolonged items.
Credit / Debit Mismatch Between Life Asia Bank Codes and Flat File Not Detected
Discrepancies between Life Asia bank codes and flat file codes may go unnoticed, leading to incorrect accounting entries and reconciliation breaks.
Finance team verifies journal entries and performs daily bank reconciliation to detect mismatches between Life Asia bank codes and flat file codes.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Bucket Shifting Incorrect or Not Processed
Incorrect handling of bucket shifting or PNR refunds in the Recon module can result in misclassification of funds and inaccurate balances.

Bucket shifting is done based on QRD raised by Branch and closed after shifting. Remarks are updated in QRD closures for non-shifting items. Bucket shifting report is extracted from Recon module and journal entry is passed in LA/GA. Automated journal entry is created via report to avoid incorrect journals, and identified during daily reconciliation for any variation.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Incorrect PNR (Refund) Action Taken in Recon Module
Errors in taking PNR action in the Recon module or posting JV in Life Asia/Group Asia can lead to inaccurate accounting and reconciliation issues.

Journal entry is tallied with approved voucher at payment stage. Any difference in excess PNR action is identified at the daily reconciliation stage between Sun System balance and Recon module open items.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Delay in Processing Refunds Beyond 45-Day Regulatory Threshold
Refunds for proposals not received within 45 days may not be processed on time, leading to customer dissatisfaction and regulatory non-compliance under IRDAI policyholder protection norms.
Finance team monitors refund tracker for proposals older than 45 days. Delays are escalated to ensure timely processing and compliance.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Incorrect Refund Due to Data Mismatch (CRM vs Recon Flat File)
Errors in validating transaction ID, amount, or bank details between CRM and Recon flat file can result in refunding the wrong customer or incorrect amount.
Finance team validates transaction ID, amount, and bank details between CRM and Recon flat file before processing refunds. Mismatches are corrected prior to payout.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Missing AML / KYC Verification Before Refund Processing
Refunds may be processed without proper AML/KYC checks, exposing the company to compliance and fraud risks.
Finance team ensures AML/KYC documents are validated before processing refunds. Incomplete or missing documents result in rejection of the refund request and update of CRM.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Refunds for sundry or clearing accounts may be processed incorrectly if account details are not validated properly.
Finance team validates account details before processing refunds from sundry or clearing accounts to prevent misdirected payments.
Refund Process (PNR) and Open Item Bucket Shifting
Refund Status Not Updated in CRM After Payout
Refund status may not be updated in CRM after payout, leading to incorrect tracking and unresolved customer queries.
Finance team updates CRM with refund status after payout and closes the case to ensure accurate tracking and resolution.
Lack of Segregation of Duties (SoD) in Payment Authorization
The same individual may initiate and authorize payee codes (maker and checker roles not adequately segregated), creating risk of unauthorized or fraudulent payouts.

Payee code preparation (maker) and authorization/approval (checker) are performed by different individuals. System access controls in Life Asia/Group Asia enforce role-based access to prevent the same user from both preparing and authorizing payments. EOD reports flag any SoD violations for review.
Duplicate or Wrong Payouts Due to Register Errors

Duplicate entries or incorrect payee/bank details in the Unified Refund & Claim Register and year-wise Excel files may result in duplicate or wrong payouts, leading to financial loss, customer dissatisfaction, reconciliation breaks, and regulatory non-compliance.

All claim/refund payments are recorded in a centralized Unified Refund & Claim Register with key identifiers (policy number, payee code/name, bank details, claim amount), maintained Routine duplicate/exception checks are performed; on identification of a duplicate or wrong payout, the Operations team is notified to stop and reverse the payout, update core systems and bank instructions, and rectify the entry in the Unified Register.
NRI Payout Processed Without Mandatory Repatriation Letter

Payments to NRI beneficiaries processed without obtaining the required NRI repatriation letter in prescribed format expose the company to FEMA/regulatory non-compliance and may result in bank rejection or incorrect payout.

For NRI payouts, HDFC Offline payout mode is mandatorily used. Before submitting bank payment instructions, repatriation letters in the prescribed format are obtained from the Operations department and submitted along with the signed bank payment instructions to the bank's generic email ID.
Inaccurate Fund Provisioning Leading to Payment Delays or Excess Idle Cash

Errors in projecting and requesting funds, or not adhering to the INR 15 lakh minimum buffer (or approved higher limits), may cause payment delays, operational disruptions, idle cash, missed investment income, or overdraft/penalty charges.

On payout day (before 1:00 p.m.), Finance team prepares an authorized BI-based (Individual & Group) fund projection and places a net fund request to Investments after adjusting for (i) book balance, (ii) known bank rejections not yet accounted, and (iii) unposted bank receipts, ensuring a minimum INR 15 lakh contingency buffer per agreed policy. Any requirement to exceed the buffer is documented with written justification, recommended by Head-Operations/Claims, and approved by Head-Finance.
Open Items in Bank Reconciliation Not Actioned Timely
Unresolved open items in bank reconciliation statements (e.g., uncleared payments, unapplied credits) may lead to misstated bank balances, inaccurate fund projections, and erroneous payouts.

Daily bank reconciliation is performed for all payout bank accounts (BOI, UBI, HDFC, Deutsche Bank). Open items are identified, investigated, and actioned within defined timelines. Items outstanding beyond defined thresholds are escalated per the escalation matrix. The EOD checklist includes bank reconciliation status.
Incorrect TDS / Withholding and Non-Compliance in Tax Payments

Failure to correctly verify TDS/TCS applicability and rates, reliance on incomplete BI data, or improper treatment of reversals can lead to wrong tax deduction/non-deduction, delayed payouts, and inability to adjust taxes already remitted, resulting in interest and penalties.

Tax Team downloads the BI 'Payee Code Authorization report for all payee types', validates tax applicability and rates (including PAN status, Section 194DA/195/194A, thresholds, surcharge/cess), and confirms Form 15CA/15CB requirements (co-ordinating with a practising CA). Any exceptions are communicated and payments are placed on hold until fully resolved. If reversal is required: (i) same-month reversals reverse both payment liability and tax; (ii) subsequent-month reversals reverse only the liability, with prior-month tax handled via JV in LA/GA. Monthly reconciliations tie deductions, remittances, and JVs.

Issuing cheques where bank/contact details are unavailable, and in court/exceptional cases, especially across multiple banks with mixed automated (Deutsche Bank SFTP) and manual issuance, creates risks of unauthorized issuance, duplicate, or misdirected payments.

Cheque payouts are initiated only against approved office notes and management decision criteria. Pre-printed cheque delivery via Deutsche Bank (T+2 TAT). All exceptions require Operations Head recommendation and Finance Head approval per the bank authorization matrix. Cancelled cheques are securely retained and not destroyed.
Stale Cheques Not Monitored Leading to Misstated Liabilities and Unclaimed Funds

Failure to monitor cheques issued but not cleared within 3 months (stale period) may lead to unreversed liabilities, incorrect balance recognition, and failure to transfer funds to Unclaimed as required.

All issued cheques are tracked daily through BI and manual cheque logs. Any cheque not cleared within 3 months is classified as stale, triggering mandatory reversal of presentment and payee code in Life Asia/Group Asia with the standardized 'Stale' rejection code, which auto-moves the liability to Unclaimed on a retrospective basis. For lost-in-transit cheques, stop-payment bank confirmation is obtained before reversal. Revalidation/reissuance requires a new payee code with fresh authorization.
Policy Payout Accounting and Bank Rejection Handling
Inaccurate or Incomplete Accounting of Payments and Bank Rejections

Errors or delays in recording accounting entries for payout presentment transactions in Life Asia/Group Asia and Oracle, or failure to update rejection reasons and reversal details, may result in misstated liabilities, incorrect GL balances, reconciliation mismatches, tax misstatements, and delayed reversal of unexecuted payouts.

Accounting entries for all payouts are auto-generated in Life Asia/Group Asia and flow to Oracle via integrated files the following day, using pre-configured GL, cash-flow, and product parameters. For bank rejections, the team immediately reverses presentment and the payee code, updates standardized rejection reason codes, and ensures correct tax reversal logic based on the month of authorization. Manual entries are posted through Oracle Excel upload with mandatory fields, subject to strict maker-checker review. BI presentment/reversal reports are matched daily with Oracle.
Policy Payout Accounting and Bank Rejection Handling
Improper Handling of Bank Rejections (Non-Reversal or Delayed Reversal)

Failure to promptly reverse presentment and the payee code in Life Asia/Group Asia, or incorrect/non-updation of standardized rejection reasons (internal/external), may result in unreversed liabilities, duplicate payouts, incorrect tax treatment, and GL reconciliation discrepancies.

For every bank rejection, Finance team immediately reverses the presentment and then the payee code in Life Asia/Group Asia. The system auto-generates accounting entries for reversal and ensures correct tax treatment based on the month of original authorization. Reversal details are updated in the Unified Claim Register for traceability. BI 'Presentment/Reversal' reports are reconciled daily with Oracle entries to confirm completeness and prevent duplicate items.
Policy Payout Accounting and Bank Rejection Handling
Payment Details Not Updated in Life Asia / Group Asia After Payout

Failure to update payment details (payee bank name, account number, mode of payment, present date) in Life Asia/Group Asia after processing may result in incomplete records, reconciliation breaks, and inability to trace payments.

Payment details (payee bank name, payee bank account number, mode of payment - EFT/NEFT/RTGS/Cheque, and present date) are updated in Life Asia/Group Asia immediately after payout processing. For bulk payee codes, updates are done through the Nastier Excel file. Payment details are also updated in the Unified Claim Register for future reference.
Misstatement from Incorrect Reinsurance Accounting (Accruals / Status)

Inaccurate recognition of reinsurance claim receivables/payables, failure to reflect claim status, or incorrect FX/bank-charge treatment can distort Schedule IV and solvency-relevant balances. Lack of monthly reconciliation with the Actuarial team increases risk of open-item ageing and financial reporting errors.

All reinsurance claims are accounted at policy/claim level based on monthly status files from the Actuarial team, with prescribed GL codes and journal types for each status (registered, accepted/intimated, paid, repudiated). Product-wise and vendor-wise reconciliations with Actuarial are performed monthly with sign-offs. Oracle ledger/BI extracts are matched to claim registers to clear ageing and ensure accuracy.
Incorrect or Delayed Accounting and Settlement of Reinsurance Payouts Including FX

Incorrect application of GL codes, delays in reflecting claim status, or incorrect processing of reinsurance payouts including FX settlements can result in misstated receivables/payables, reconciliation variances with Actuarial data, and delayed recoveries.

Entries are passed per SOP-defined GL codes and journal types. FX gain/loss and bank charges are posted correctly where settlements are in foreign currency. Monthly product-wise and vendor-wise reconciliations validate receivable ageing and settlement status. Reinsurance premium and claims are stated in INR for accrual purposes; FX treatment applies only on actual settlement.
Incorrect Accounting Treatment for Repudiation of Claims

Failure to reverse benefits paid/expensed and to correctly recognize premium refunds and contingent liabilities as per the Board-approved repudiation accounting policy may lead to misstated financial statements and non-compliance with IRDAI guidelines.

Upon repudiation: (i) expenses accounted at intimation are reversed; (ii) repudiated claims are shown under contingent liability for one year (or until litigation resolves); (iii) premium refunds for ULIP/traditional policies are accounted per SOP-defined scenarios per IRDA circular dated 28 October 2015; (iv) GL codes 4030100037 (Dr) and 2050000038 (Cr) are used; (v) quarterly disclosure schedules are maintained and reviewed with the Legal & Compliance team.
Failure to Identify and Transfer Unclaimed Policy Amounts as Required

Unclaimed amounts (including stale cheque liabilities, unreversed payee codes, and aged payables) not transferred to the Unclaimed suspense account may result in misstated liabilities and non-compliance with IRDAI unclaimed amounts regulations.

Finance team monitors unclaimed amounts through the BI unclaimed report and the stale cheque listing. On reversal of a stale payee code, the system automatically moves the liability to Unclaimed on a retrospective basis from the liability creation date. A policy-wise stale cheque listing is shared with the Claims processing team within three days of month-end. Unclaimed amounts are disclosed in financial statements and managed per IRDAI regulations.
Failure to follow defined procedures may result in reputational, operational, and fraud risks.

SOPs for the Premium Accounting process are defined, documented, and enforced. SOPs are reviewed at least annually by the Finance Head, version-controlled, and formally approved before re-issue. Any mid-year amendments are communicated to all concerned users as prescribed in SOP Section 18 (SOP Updation Process). Maker-checker and access controls govern who may initiate and approve SOP changes.
Adherence to TATs covered in SOP
Non-adherence to TATs and process performance metrics
Premium Accounting activities may exceed defined TATs, resulting in delays in daily operations, month-end/quarter-end closures, inaccurate financial reporting, and escalation of operational risks.

The Premium Accounting team tracks all critical activities against TAT benchmarks defined by the HOD. Deviations are escalated to the HOD with root-cause analysis and corrective steps. TAT adherence metrics are incorporated into operational dashboards to ensure transparency and continuous monitoring, enabling efficient book closures and standardised process performance.
Accounting of Individual and Group Premium
Inaccurate or Incomplete Premium Accounting Across Individual Business

Premium transactions may be incorrectly recorded, duplicated, omitted, or posted to wrong GL accounts in the Policy Management System (Life/Group Asia), leading to misstated financial statements and non-compliance with IRDAI reporting requirements.

All premium transactions are validated and posted using automated and manual accounting entries configured within the systems. The 22 categories of daily interface uploads enumerated in SOP 5.1 (Collection, Cheque Dishonour, Refund Payable, Premium Billing, Commission, ULIP Fund entries, Admin Charges, Mortality, Switching, Policy Admin & Misc Charges, GST, Freelook Cancellation, Rider Premium, Partial Withdrawal, Revival, Surrender, Maturity, Death Claim, Annuity, Policy Fund Transfer, Alter/Cancel from Inception, and Cancellation/Rejection entries) are each subject to maker-checker review prior to posting.
Accounting of Individual and Group Premium
Inaccurate or Incomplete Premium Accounting Across Individual Business

Premium transactions may be incorrectly recorded, duplicated, omitted, or posted to wrong GL accounts, leading to misstated financial statements, incorrect customer records, and non-compliance with IRDAI reporting requirements.

Finance & Accounts verifies that the IT team sends Interface upload files on a daily basis. All accounting entries for transactions appearing in Life/Group Asia are confirmed to be recorded. Correct and complete Interface files are validated against entries in Life/Group Asia before upload. Maker-checker controls ensure accuracy of the verification process.
Upload Procedure of Life/Group Asia Integrated Files
Incomplete or unauthorised interface file receipt and custody
If the automated interface fails, entries may be omitted or duplicated in the GL, causing misstated balances and a weakened audit trail.

The DIAICHI CONVERTER1 macro is version-controlled and stored in a restricted path accessible only to authorised users. Finance documents file name, period, DR/CR totals, and T-codes pre/post conversion. Macro run logs/screens, TRD run IDs, Held Ledger screenshots, and reconciliations to interface control totals are retained as evidence. Maker-checker is enforced: upload through Sun Transfer Desk (profile STD_IMP_LEDG) is performed by one person and independently validated for period, totals, and mapping by a second person before posting to Held Ledger.
Incorrect or incomplete Group MIS impacting downstream accounting

If the MIS contains wrong product details, incorrect premium amounts, missing GST/service tax data, or incomplete related-party indicators, it may lead to inaccurate GL postings, tax misstatements, regulatory non-compliance, and reconciliation gaps between GIAS, MIS, and Sun System.

GST rate is verified product-wise (Saving/Risk) against actual service tax amount in Group MIS. Finance validates all 10 mandatory MIS fields: Product Name, Name of Scheme, Master Policyholder, Policy Number, Business Type (New/Renewal), Mode of Premium, Channel (BOI/UBI/Broker), Base Premium breakdown with MTD & YTD figures, Tolerance Amount, and Related Party indicator. Finance cross-checks and reconciles discrepancies with Operations before proceeding to accounting. Related party indicators and tolerance amounts are specifically confirmed given their downstream impact on regulatory disclosures.
Incorrect Recognition or Reversal of Due Premiums

Errors in LA/GA batch logic, incorrect eligibility identification, wrong T-code posting, or failure to validate BIU-provided policy lists may result in overstatement/understatement of premium income, mismatched accruals, inaccurate reporting to IRDAI, and misclassification in Sun System.

LA/GA automated batch identifies all eligible traditional non-linked policies and generates Sun download entries for booking (Life Asia: BJ70, Group Asia: BZ57) and reversals (Life Asia: BJ71, Group Asia: BZ58). Finance uploads the batch file into Sun System and performs maker-checker verification.
Incorrect Recognition or Reversal of Due Premiums

Errors in LA/GA batch logic, incorrect eligibility identification, or failure to validate BIU-provided policy lists may result in overstatement/understatement of premium income, mismatched accruals, and inaccurate IRDAI reporting.

Policy-wise breakup from BIU is reviewed by Finance against defined checkpoints: policy status must be Traditional, In-Force, and within grace-period rules (30 days for Yearly/Half-Yearly/Quarterly modes; 15 days for Monthly mode). Reconciliations between LA/GA, BIU reports, and Sun GL ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance with revenue-recognition policies. Any discrepancy is escalated to IT/BIU for resolution before finalisation.
Netting-off of GST on Allocation Charges from Linked Premium
Incorrect Monthly Netting or Recognition of GST on Linked Premium Allocation Charges

If GST on allocation charges is not correctly netted or delayed during EOM, premium income and GST liabilities may be misstated, resulting in inaccurate GST payables, customer fund discrepancies, regulatory non-compliance, and reconciliation mismatches between the Policy Management System and Sun System.

EOM batch generates netting-off entries for all ULIP year-wise premium streams (1st Year to 10th Year) via T-code BZ09, crediting Premium Invest (Contra) against the relevant year-wise GST allocation charge accounts. Maker-checker controls and periodic reconciliations between the Policy Management System and Sun System ensure correctness of GST netting. Discrepancies are escalated to IT/Operations for resolution. Audit evidence is retained for GST compliance.
Life/Group Asia Reconciliation with SUN System
Inaccurate or Incomplete Reconciliation Between Life Asia/Group Asia and Sun System

If reconciliations are not performed promptly, this may lead to unresolved mismatches, misstated financial reporting, incorrect sub-ledger to GL linkages, delayed corrections, and regulatory non-compliance in financial disclosures.

After Sun upload posting, a fresh workbook is created daily containing alternate reference codes, descriptions, and mapped LA/GA GL codes. The BI system-generated LA/GA trial balance is pasted and validated — posting flag 'P' total difference must equal zero. Sun balances are derived using correct journal types (ZLAIF for Life Asia, ZGRIN for Group Asia).
Life/Group Asia Reconciliation with SUN System
Inaccurate or Incomplete Reconciliation Between Life Asia/Group Asia and Sun System
If reconciliation differences are not escalated and resolved promptly, cumulative mismatches may accumulate, leading to misstated financial reporting and audit findings.

A line-by-line comparison is performed at alternate reference and GL levels to identify variances. Any difference is immediately escalated to HOD and IT for investigation and rectification. If reconciliation cannot be completed due to operational reasons, Finance HOD is informed and cumulative reconciliation is performed the following day. Vision summary links in the reconciliation file enable direct derivation of Sun balances.
MIS Reporting & Statutory/Procedural Compliance for Premium Accounting
Non-Compliance with Statutory Reporting Requirements and Internal Control Breakdowns in Premium Accounting

Failure to reconcile premium MIS with the books of account, incorrect or delayed reporting to IRDAI, non-adherence to statutory timelines, inaccurate premium segmentation, or weak internal controls may result in regulatory non-compliance, financial misstatements, reputational risk, IRDAI penalties, and audit qualifications.

Premium numbers are required to be reported to IRDAI on periodic basis as per statutory provisions. BIU department prepares premium reports as per IRDAI-mandated periodicity (Monthly NB, Monthly BAP, Quarterly BAP, IRDA Health Returns, Life Council, Public Disclosures, etc.) and per the reporting calendar defined in SOP 8.1. Finance & Accounts ensures timely Schedule 1 closure as a prerequisite to all regulatory submissions.
MIS Reporting & Statutory/Procedural Compliance for Premium Accounting
Non-Compliance with Statutory Reporting Requirements and Internal Control Breakdowns in Premium Accounting
If BIU premium reports are submitted to IRDAI without reconciliation to Sun System, inaccurate figures may be filed, resulting in regulatory penalties and reputational risk.

Finance cross-checks and verifies figures in IRDAI reports sent by Business Intelligence Unit against Sun System segment-wise balances. Post-verification, Finance confirms accuracy through documented email approval to Operations team. Final soft copy and hard copy are forwarded to IRDAI by the Compliance team. Maker-checker segregation ensures accuracy and a full audit trail is maintained.
MIS Reporting & Statutory/Procedural Compliance for Premium Accounting
Non-Compliance with Statutory Reporting Requirements and Internal Control Breakdowns in Premium Accounting
If audit queries are not addressed, wrong uploads not restricted, or LA/GA GL mismatches not resolved, financial reporting may be misstated and audit observations may remain unresolved.

Premium Accounting team ensures statutory compliance, responds to internal/external audit queries, supports financial audit requirements, maintains ledger-level reconciliations between Sun System and Life/Group Asia, validates T-codes in integrated uploads, evaluates automation failures through root-cause analysis, and maintains proper internal controls to prevent erroneous or unauthorised postings.
Inaccurate or Incomplete Internal MIS Reporting for Premium-Related Information

If monthly MIS reports contain incorrect premium segmentation, misclassified product/channel data, inaccurate policyholder charges, incorrect GST figures, or unvalidated variance analysis, it may lead to flawed actuarial assumptions, incorrect business decisions, GST filing errors, and misreporting to internal stakeholders.

After month-end Schedule 1 closure, the Premium Accounting team prepares the following MIS: (1) Product-wise premium details (Single/FYP/Renewal) shared with Actuarial; (2) Channel-wise premium breakup for internal use; (3) Policyholder charges details (month-on-month); (4) Premium variance analysis; (5) Policy-wise GST details for Retail and Group (shared with Taxation for return filing). All MIS outputs are validated through reconciliations with SUN GL, system trial balances, and prior-month benchmarks. Maker-checker review ensures accuracy before circulation.
Inaccurate or Incomplete Internal MIS Reporting for Premium-Related Information
Incorrect GST codes or misclassified premium segments in the GST MIS may lead to erroneous GST return filings, tax misstatements, and regulatory penalties.

GST MIS is verified for correctness of GST codes, product-wise GST rates, and premium classifications for both Retail and Group business. Validated MIS is shared with Taxation team for return filing. Final MIS reports are circulated to Actuarial, Taxation, and relevant stakeholders with documentation maintained for audit trail and future reference.
Inaccurate, Incomplete, or Delayed Submission of Audit Data

If audit datasets are extracted incorrectly, not validated against Schedule 1, incomplete, or provided late, audits may be compromised, financial misstatements may go undetected, and audit qualifications may result.

Premium Accounting obtains policy-wise and summary-level premium data from BIU and Sun System/Vision for: Retail New Business, Retail Renewals, Group premium, Retail and Group Due Premium, and product-wise premium income. Each dataset undergoes mandatory internal validation against Schedule 1 to ensure accuracy and completeness before being provided to auditors.
Financial Closing and Preparation of Disclosures
Delayed or Inaccurate Schedule 1 Closure Impacting Financial Reporting

Failure to close Schedule 1 accurately and within defined timelines may lead to incomplete or misstated premium figures, delays in financial closure, errors in statutory disclosures, and regulatory non-compliance.

Premium Accounting performs month-end activities to ensure timely Schedule 1 closure by validating premium balances in Sun System, reconciling LA/GA system outputs, resolving outstanding differences, and confirming completeness of premium accounting entries.
Financial Closing and Preparation of Disclosures
Delayed or Inaccurate Schedule 1 Closure Impacting Financial Reporting
Failure to communicate finalised Schedule 1 figures within defined timelines may cause delays in financial closure and IRDAI filing.

Finalised Schedule 1 premium figures are communicated to Finance for incorporation into financial statements and associated disclosures, ensuring adherence to defined timelines for financial closing and IRDAI reporting. Documentation and audit trail are maintained to support internal and statutory audit requirements.
Incomplete or Inaccurate Reporting of Related Party Premium Transactions

Policyholder transactions involving related parties may be incorrectly tagged, partially captured, omitted, or inaccurately extracted from the Policy Administration System or BIU reports, resulting in misstatement or non-compliance in related party disclosures.

On a quarterly basis, Premium Accounting extracts related-party tagged policyholder transactions via a system-generated Vision-based report and reconciles with BIU-provided policy-wise premium listing and Sunfile records containing related party codes. All 22 RP codes (RP001–RP022) are validated for completeness. The validated dataset is reviewed for accuracy before submission to the Financial Reporting team.
Misstatement of ULIP Fund-wise Revenue Account and Balance Sheet

ULIP-related GL accounts may be incorrectly mapped or not reconciled with 'Provision for Linked Liability' and 'Change in Valuation for Unit Portion', leading to inaccurate fund-wise financial statements and potential non-compliance with the IRDAI Master Circular.

Premium Accounting performs reconciliation of all ULIP transaction-related GL balances against 'Provision for Linked Liability' and the corresponding 'Change in Valuation for Unit Portion'. This reconciliation is documented and reviewed to ensure fund-wise Revenue Accounts and Balance Sheets for ULIP business (Appendix 5) comply with IRDAI reporting guidelines.

Deviations between the Linked Liability and the Change in Valuation may not be detected promptly, leading to incorrect ULIP financial balances, misstated fund-level reporting, and potential regulatory non-compliance.

Technical Accounting team uses Vision-generated report built on Alternate Reference Numbers and ULIP-specific T-codes to monitor all ULIP-related GL entries. Any deviation between Linked Liability and Change in Valuation is investigated, evaluated, and promptly escalated to the IT team for root-cause analysis and correction.

Unit GL balances may be incorrect or not updated accurately for the selected accounting period if the Vision-based reconciliation is not properly reviewed. Undetected differences may lead to misstated ULIP financial balances.

Vision-based Unit Reconciliation file is updated with the relevant period and date, and the workbook is refreshed to pull system-updated GL figures. The reconciliation output is reviewed to confirm the 'Variance' column is zero. Any variances identified are promptly escalated to the LA Support team for root-cause analysis and system corrections.
Fund Revenue Statement Preparation (UL1 and UL2)
Inaccurate or Incomplete Preparation of Fund Revenue Statement (UL1 and UL2)

If Vision mapping, segment-wise investment income, valuation reserves, ULIP charges, or unit-portion GLs are not accurately validated, the Fund Revenue Statement may contain incorrect inflow/outflow details, leading to regulatory non-compliance and financial misreporting.

Fund Revenue Statements are generated via Vision-based GL mapping supported by a control sheet validating three-way reconciliation: (1) Finance books, (2) Investment records, and (3) ULIP reserves. Monthly investment trial balances are split into Life/Pension/Group segments and investment income is matched with Sun System postings. Change in valuation is derived from monthly reserve files and validated at segment level.
Fund Revenue Statement Preparation (UL1 and UL2)
Inaccurate or Incomplete Preparation of Fund Revenue Statement (UL1 and UL2)
Incorrect fund-wise charge data or unit-portion GL mismatches in UL1/UL2 may result in misreporting of ULIP income and expense schedules to IRDAI.

UL1 is prepared using Vision-extracted ULIP charges (including Fund Management Charges), supplemented by fund-wise charge data from Investment Back Office during quarterly close. UL2 is prepared using Vision-extracted Schedule-4 expense GLs, ensuring unit-portion outflows reconcile with Premium Invest (Cr) values. Maker-checker review is applied before finalisation.
Fund Revenue Statement Preparation (UL1 and UL2)
Inaccurate or Incomplete Preparation of Fund Revenue Statement (UL1 and UL2)
If net inflows do not equal net outflows for all ULIP segments, or the statement is not in IRDAI-prescribed format, regulatory non-compliance and incorrect Appendix-5 disclosures will result.

The Fund Revenue Statement is finalised only when net inflows equal net outflows for all segments (Linked Life, Linked Pension, Linked Group). The statement is prepared in IRDAI-prescribed format and submitted to Financial Reporting for Appendix-5 disclosure. All validations, exceptions, and reconciliations are documented and follow maker-checker review for audit and regulatory compliance.
Adherence to Business Continuity Plan (BCP) by Technical Accounting Team
Inadequate Continuity of Technical Accounting Operations

Disruptions impacting staff, IT applications, infrastructure, or vendors may cause the team to fail in resuming critical processes, leading to delays in financial reporting, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational impact.

BCP covers the following priority activities: (1) Premium Receipt Flat File Upload, (2) Recon Module access, (3) Receipt Reconciliation, (4) Passing JV in LA/GA, (5) Processing LA/GA–Sun System integrated file — all requiring access to Recon Module, LA/GA, BI Portal, Sun System, and MS Office/Outlook. BCP is updated for system, personnel, and dependency changes. BCP execution readiness is validated through periodic testing with documented results. Gaps identified during testing are addressed before the next BCP cycle. RTO is defined at 3 days as per BIA.
Adherence to Quality Control by Premium Accounting Team
Inaccurate or Unreviewed ULIP GL Postings
ULIP-related GL balances may reflect incorrect contra entries, unusual movements, erroneous charges, or system-posted inaccuracies if quality checks are not effectively performed.

Quality checks include: (i) daily tallying of contra accounts — Premium Income vs. Premium Invest and Premium Non-Invest; (ii) review of policy expenses, mortality charges, policy administration charges, and positive/negative fluctuation ledgers; (iii) sample checks of system-generated premium entries with related charges and GST for select products; (iv) monitoring exception reports for policyholder charges exceeding defined thresholds. Any variation or unusual movement is escalated to IT or Operations for further analysis and corrective action.
Adherence to SOP on Risk Factors and Mitigation Measures
Inadequate Identification and Mitigation of Premium Accounting Risks

Key operational, financial, or compliance-related risks may be incorrectly or insufficiently identified, assessed, or mitigated, resulting in control gaps, financial misstatements, and regulatory breaches.

Premium Accounting team periodically evaluates process-level risks by assessing financial and operational impact and estimating likelihood of occurrence. Appropriate preventive and detective controls are designed and implemented. Risks are categorised by severity (impact >₹5 crore = High; ₹50L–₹5Cr = Medium; up to ₹50L = Low) and frequency (>5 times/month = High; 3-5 = Medium; up to 3 = Low). Risk events occurring despite mitigation measures are promptly escalated to all relevant stakeholders.
Adherence to SOP on Risk Factors and Mitigation Measures
Inadequate Identification and Mitigation of Premium Accounting Risks
Failure to communicate risk events to stakeholders may result in delayed corrective action, regulatory breach, and compounding operational losses.

Risks are classified and categorised on the basis of frequency and impact. Any incident involving a risk event, despite mitigation measures, is promptly escalated to all relevant stakeholders. The escalation matrix defined in SOP Section 14.3 is followed: Level 1 = Deputy Manager, Level 2 = Senior Manager, Level 3 = Vice President.
Adherence to IFC complying with Section 134 of Companies Act, 2013

Inadequate IFC practices may result in inaccurate data transfers, untallied trial balances, untested system developments, incorrect accounting, unreconciled assets/liabilities, GST non-compliance, errors in statutory reports, or lack of timely reporting, potentially masking fraud or errors.

Premium Accounting team ensures effective IFC through: (1) monitoring data flow from Life/Group Asia to Sun System; (2) daily TB reconciliation; (3) UAT for new system/product developments with financial impact; (4) reconciliation of assets and liabilities on a periodic basis with immediate action on open items; (5) compliance with GST laws; (6) correctness and completeness of statutory premium reports; (7) sharing exception MIS with stakeholders; (8) periodic MIS/dashboard and presentations to management on premium income.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Incorrect or Incomplete Reversal of Premium Income and Charges on Freelook Cancellation

Upon freelook cancellation, all related premium income, commission, GST, and applicable charges must be reversed. For Traditional products, proportionate mortality charges are deducted before refund. For ULIP products, NAV loss entry is passed (where applicable) and all unit-linked charges reversed. Failure to correctly process these reversals may result in overstated premium income, unrecovered commissions, incorrect GST payable balances, and delayed/incorrect customer refunds.

Finance verifies all freelook cancellation entries against the standardised accounting entry templates defined in SOP (Traditional: reversal of FYP/GST + proportionate mortality + refund payable creation + bank presentment; ULIP: reversal of charges/GST + NAV loss entry + reversal from fund/non-invest + commission reversal + coverage debt set-off + proportionate mortality + refund payable). Maker-checker review confirms completeness of reversals. Refund payable GL (2050000055) and bank presentment to HDFC Payment A/c are confirmed before closure. Stamp duty recovery on freelook is separately verified.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Misapplication of CFI Accounting Treatment vs. Freelook Cancellation Treatment

CFI entries have a materially different treatment from freelook cancellations: under CFI, NAV loss is NOT accounted, and all charges are reversed in Premium Suspense. If CFI is incorrectly processed as freelook (or vice versa), NAV losses may be incorrectly booked or omitted, premium suspense balances may be misstated, and fund liability postings may be inaccurate, leading to financial misstatements and incorrect customer settlement.

Finance verifies transaction type (CFI vs. freelook) in Life Asia before initiating accounting entries. CFI entries are processed per SOP templates: Reversal of Charges & GST, Premium Reversal (debit FYP, credit PREMSUSP), Commission Reversal, Coverage Debt Set-off, Non-Invest Fund Reversal, and Reversal from Fund A/c to Premium Invest. Specifically, CFI entries do NOT include a NAV Loss Entry (unlike freelook). Maker-checker confirms the correct template has been applied. Finance retains screenshots of Life Asia transaction type for audit trail.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Incorrect Accounting of X-Charge (Revival Fee) for Lapsed Policies

X-Charge entries involve: (1) X-Charge creation/due (Dr Lapse X Charges Due A/c / Cr Revival Charges from Policyholder); (2) X-Charge receipt via Bank; (3) Adjustment from pending death claims (Dr Pending Claims / Cr Lapse X Charges Due A/c); (4) Adjustment from policy loan (Dr Premium Deposit / Cr Loan Bank A/c and Lapse X Charges Due A/c). Incorrect entries may overstate or understate revival charges, result in incorrect lapse recovery balances, and distort claims or loan settlement amounts.

Finance verifies X-Charge accounting entries in Life Asia against the standardised SOP entry templates for all four scenarios: creation, receipt, adjustment from claims, and adjustment from policy loan. GL code 1060100030 (Lapse X Charges Due A/c) is reconciled monthly to confirm outstanding revival amounts are correctly reflected. Adjustments from claims or loans are cross-verified against the respective claim payment or loan disbursement records. Maker-checker review is applied to all manual adjustments.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Incorrect Fund Transfer to Discontinued Fund or Misclassification of Discontinuance Charges

On ULIP policy discontinuance, fund value must be transferred from Fund Invest A/c (FUNDINV-GRFD) to Discontinued Ulip Policy Fund Liabilities (A/c 2040101010), and discontinuance charges plus GST must be recovered from the Discontinued Fund (A/c 2040101013). Incorrect entries may misstate the Discontinued Fund balance, omit GST on discontinuance charges, or misclassify policyholder liabilities, leading to incorrect fund valuations and regulatory non-compliance.

Finance verifies discontinuance accounting entries against SOP templates: (1) Discontinuance: Dr Fund Invests / Cr Discontinued Fund (2040101010); (2) Charges on discontinuance: Dr Discontinued Fund / Cr Discontinued Policy Charges (3030100023) + GST Payable (2050504021) + Fund Invest Disc Fund (2040101013). Discontinued Fund GL (2040101010 and 2040101013) is reconciled against the Investment team's discontinued fund records on a monthly basis. Maker-checker review is applied to all discontinuance entries.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Incorrect or Missing Accounting Entries for ULIP Fund Switches and Premium Redirections

Fund switches involve: (1) Switch flow — transfer between existing and new fund via Pending Switch control account (2090000013); (2) Switch charges — debit Pending Switch / credit ULIP Switching Charge (3010200040) + GST; (3) Fluctuation effect — recording positive/negative fluctuation for both existing and new funds. Premium redirection involves Coverage Debt creation, Prem Redirection Charge (3010200041), GST, and Unit Dealing Entry. Errors may overstate or understate fund balances, omit switch charges, or create unreconciled Pending Switch balances.

Finance verifies fund switch and premium redirection entries in Life Asia against SOP accounting entry templates. Pending Switch control account (2090000013) is monitored daily to ensure it nets to zero after switch completion. Positive/negative fluctuation entries (FLUCPOS/FLUCNEG) are verified for both the exiting and entering funds. Premium redirection charges and associated GST (3010200041 / GST Payable Other Charges) are confirmed against product terms. Maker-checker review is applied. Any open Pending Switch balance at day-end is escalated to IT.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Incorrect Stamp Duty Accounting – Advance Purchase, Consumption, or Freelook Recovery

Stamp duty involves three accounting events: (1) Advance Stamp Duty purchase (Dr Advance Stamp Duty A/c / Cr Stamp Transfer to LA/GA A/c); (2) Consumption on policy issuance (Dr Policy Stamp Consumed A/c / Cr Advance Stamp Duty A/c); (3) Recovery on freelook cancellation (Dr Premium Deposit 1060100025 / Cr Stamp Duty Recovery Freelook 3030100033). Errors may result in misstated advance stamp duty balances, unclaimed stamp duty credits, or incorrect freelook refund amounts.

Finance verifies all three stamp duty accounting events (advance, consumption, freelook recovery) against SOP templates. Advance Stamp Duty A/c (1040300039) is reconciled monthly against physical/digital stamp records. Consumption entries are validated against the number of policies issued in the period. Freelook stamp duty recovery entry (Dr 1060100025 / Cr 3030100033) is confirmed for all freelook cases before refund payable creation. Separate entries are maintained for Life Asia and Group Asia as required by SOP. Maker-checker review applies.
Accounting of Individual Premium – Special Transactions
Incorrect or Delayed Accounting for Cheque Dishonour and Re-presentation

On cheque dishonour, the premium income credited at the time of collection must be reversed, and related commission and GST entries must also be reversed. If dishonour entries are delayed or incorrectly processed, premium income may be overstated, collections may be mismatched with bank statements, and commission payables may be incorrect. On re-presentation, entries must be re-processed only upon actual clearance. Failure to track re-presentation status may result in duplicate or premature income recognition.

Finance verifies cheque dishonour accounting entries in Life Asia for complete reversal of all related entries (Bank A/c, Proposal/Premium Deposit, Premium Income, Commission, GST). A register/tracker is maintained for all dishonoured cheques, recording: instrument details, dishonour date, reason, re-presentation date (if any), and final status (cleared/refunded). On re-presentation, Finance confirms clearance in the bank statement before recognising premium income. Outstanding dishonoured cheques are reviewed monthly in the Proposal Deposit reconciliation. Maker-checker review applies to all dishonour and re-presentation entries.
Unreconciled Proposal Deposit Items Resulting in Misapplied or Unrecognised Premium Income

Proposal deposit accounts receive funds from Bank on collection. These are transferred to Premium Income on policy issuance, or refunded on rejection. Open/unreconciled proposal deposit items may indicate: (1) premiums received but policy not yet issued; (2) proposals rejected but refund not processed; (3) incorrect allocation to wrong policies; or (4) potential unclaimed money liability. Failure to reconcile promptly may lead to misstated liabilities, delayed income recognition, and regulatory exposure.

Finance prepares a monthly Proposal Deposit MIS (maintained at Z:\4. Technical Accounting\01.Premium\Proposal Deposit\_Internal) reconciling the Proposal Deposit GL against Bank collections, policy issuances, and refunds processed. Open items are categorised by age and reason. Items outstanding beyond 30 days are escalated to Operations for clearance. Dishonoured cheque amounts and pending refunds are tracked separately within the reconciliation. Maker-checker review is applied to the reconciliation before submission to HOD.
EOD Reporting and Daily Activity Sign-off
Non-Compliance with EOD Checklist – Missed Daily Activities, Unsigned Sign-offs, and Unescalated Exceptions

The SOP defines a detailed EOD daily checklist (Section 17) covering: LA/GA file processing via BizTalk, manual TRD upload, upload confirmation mails, duplicate upload checks, LA/GA trial balance reconciliation, GSLI manual entry, and month-end activities. Failure to complete or sign off the checklist may result in: (1) unposted Sun files creating next-day GL mismatch; (2) undetected duplicate uploads; (3) missed confirmation mails to downstream teams; (4) delayed escalation of unresolved items.

The EOD checklist (as defined in SOP Section 17) is completed daily by the Primary Owner (Priti/Atish) and reviewed by the Supervisor (Pragnesh). Each activity is marked with status code (1-Yes / 2-No / 3-NA) and exceptions are investigated. If an activity is marked '2-No' (e.g., LA/GA file not received, recon not performed), the reason is documented and escalated to HOD Finance in writing. Completed and signed EOD checklists are retained as audit evidence. Monthly EOD checklists are additionally reviewed by Senior Manager for pattern analysis.
Incorrect or Unauthorised Manual Postings in Sun System

Manual journal entries in Sun System (including GSLI renewal entries manually posted, group premium uploads via Vision Q&A XL, and other manual adjustments) are susceptible to: (1) incorrect GL codes or amounts; (2) wrong accounting period; (3) unauthorised postings bypassing automated controls; (4) lack of supporting documentation. Such errors can lead to misstated GL balances, audit findings, and potential fraud.

All manual journal entries require: (1) preparation by one authorised Finance personnel (Maker); (2) independent review and approval by a second authorised personnel (Checker/Senior Manager) before posting; (3) supporting documentation attached — including source data, calculation workings, and reason for manual entry; (4) retention in the designated folder with journal reference number for audit trail. Manual journals for GSLI renewal premium are specifically evidenced by the Group MIS and Finance verification sign-off. User access rights in Sun System restrict posting capability to authorised users only.
Unresolved Exceptions Accumulating Across Premium Accounting Processes

Reconciliation differences between Life/Group Asia and Sun System, failed BizTalk uploads, unresolved IT escalations, open proposal deposit items, and quality check exceptions may not be tracked or resolved in a timely manner, leading to cumulative misstatements, compounding reconciliation gaps, and deterioration of internal controls.

An exception log/dashboard is maintained for all open items across Premium Accounting processes, including: (1) LA/GA vs. Sun reconciliation differences; (2) BizTalk/IT escalation tickets with open/closed status; (3) group MIS discrepancies; (4) proposal deposit open items; (5) quality check exceptions. Each exception is assigned an owner, escalation level, and target resolution date per the escalation matrix (SOP Section 14.3: L1=Deputy Manager, L2=Senior Manager, L3=VP). Exception ageing is reviewed by HOD on a weekly basis. Unresolved items older than 5 working days are escalated to the next level.
SOPs that are not regularly reviewed and updated may fail to reflect current regulatory requirements, industry standards or organisational practices, leading to non-compliance.

A structured governance mechanism is established to ensure all SOPs remain current, accurate and aligned with regulatory requirements and organisational practices. SOPs are reviewed at least annually; version control and change-log are maintained. Any change recommended by Internal Audit must be actioned within 30 days.
Inconsistent processes due to outdated policies or lack of staff awareness, resulting in regulatory non-compliance, financial penalties and operational errors.

SOPs are reviewed periodically; version control is maintained. Regular training is conducted for taxation team members. EOD checklists are prepared and submitted to AVP–Taxation/HOD to monitor daily adherence. TAT breaches are escalated per the defined escalation matrix.
Failure to file returns/mandatory documentation on time or deposit/report TDS for policy payouts may lead to financial penalties, interest, reputational damage and regulatory scrutiny.

Taxation team implements maker-checker validation for all payouts to policyholders made by Operations team prior to posting of entries to the accounting system by Finance team. System-calculated TDS (Life Asia) is independently verified daily; discrepancies are escalated and payments held until rectified.
Non-Compliance with TDS – Vendors & Policy Holders

Inaccurate or delayed deduction of TDS at the time of payment/credit to vendors and policyholders, delays or failures in remittance to the Income-tax Department, non-filing/late filing of TDS returns can lead to interest, penalties, disallowance of expenditure, increased regulatory scrutiny and reputational risk.

Taxation team ensures maker-checker controls for computation and deduction; timely remittance within statutory due dates (7th of following month; 30th April for March); filing of accurate TDS returns; and periodic reconciliation of challans, returns, and Form 26Q/27Q data.
Invalid / Missing PAN – TDS at Higher Rate

PAN not furnished / PAN not linked with Aadhaar / incorrect PAN / challan details, non-issuance of TDS certificates, or non-compliance with specific provisions (Sec206AA / Sec206AB) may result in TDS being deducted at 20% or higher rates, penalties and the company being treated as assessee-in-default.

PAN details are mandatorily verified through Income-tax Department systems (TRACES) at the time of payee onboarding and before each deduction. Maker-checker review is performed on all TDS statements. TDS certificates (Form 16A) are generated and distributed to vendors within 15 days of the due date of filing TDS returns.
Incorrect Application of Lower / Nil TDS Rates (§197)

Lower or nil TDS rates under Sec197 may be incorrectly applied due to non-adherence to validity period or monetary limits specified in the lower deduction certificate (LTDC), resulting in short deduction, regulatory non-compliance, interest and penalties.

Taxation team reviews and maintains hard copies of lower/nil deduction certificates. TDS is deducted at the lower rate only for the period and up to the monetary limit specified in the certificate. Validity and thresholds are re-checked for each payment; standard rates apply once the limit is exhausted.

TDS on employee salaries may be incorrectly computed or delayed in payment due to reliance on incomplete/inaccurate statutory report from HR, improper verification of ledger balances (2050100072 / 2050502025), or non-adherence to documented procedures.

HR department prepares and shares the monthly Statutory Report Sheet; taxation team reconciles and validates ledger balances (codes 2050100072 and 2050502025) before remittance. Finance team is responsible for payment. Any discrepancy is communicated back to HR before deposit.
Incorrect TDS on Vendor Payments (Non-Salary / Non-Commission)

TDS on vendor payments (excluding salary and commission) may be incorrectly deducted or reported due to improper application of rates, incorrect handling of LTDCs, resulting in under/over-deduction, regulatory non-compliance, interest/penalties and reputational risk.

Vendors submit valid LTDCs; taxation team verifies the certificate, retains the original for records, and facilitates creation and communication of a specific lower-rate tax code to the operations team. Creditor ledgers are extracted and scrutinised for missed or incorrect TDS entries before every payment cycle.
Incorrect TDS on Policy Payouts / NRI Payouts

Incorrect application of TDS rates for improper determination of taxable income portion under Sec10(10D), non-adherence to threshold limits (₹1 lakh for Residents; no limit for NRIs), failure to complete mandatory filings (Form 15CA/CB) for NRI payouts, or inadequate verification of system-calculated TDS, resulting in regulatory non-compliance, penalties and customer disputes.

TDS is automatically calculated by the Life Asia system. All system-calculated TDS is independently verified by the taxation team before payment to the policyholder. Any discrepancy is communicated to the claims and operations teams for correction, with payments released only after successful rectification. Form 15CA/CB is filed prior to NRI payouts.
Timely Payment to Income Tax Dept.

Incorrect preparation of monthly TDS payable summary, lack of timely coordination with Banking team for fund availability, mistakes while generating Challan on the Income-tax e-payment portal, or failure to complete the prescribed payment path in the TDS PAC system, resulting in interest, penalties, regulatory non-compliance and reputational impact.

TDS is deposited with the Income Tax Department on or before the 7th of the following month (30th April for March), after correctly selecting payment nature and bank details on Challan 281. Fund availability email is sent to Banking team on 5th/6th of every month. Challan evidence is obtained and retained. EOD checklist item #13 monitors TDS payment.
Late Filing / Errors in Quarterly TDS Returns

TDS returns (Forms 24Q/26Q/27Q/27EQ) may be filed late or with errors (incorrect PAN, challan mismatches, wrong TDS codes) due to inadequate data validation, resulting in late-filing fees under Sec234E, penalties under Sec 271H and reputational risk.

TDS data is uploaded into TDS PAC on a monthly basis; TDS rate, TDS head, gross amount, TDS amount and PAN are checked against a defined checklist before upload. Quarterly TDS returns are filed within 30 days from end of quarter (by 31st May for Q4). PAN numbers are verified with Operations department. FVU file is validated before submission. Correction returns are filed promptly where discrepancies arise.
Incorrect TDS rate configured in vendor master

There is a risk that an incorrect TDS rate is captured in the vendor master at the time of onboarding or not updated in case of amendments, leading to incorrect TDS deduction, non-compliance with tax regulations, interest/penalty exposure, and financial misstatements.

At the time of vendor onboarding, the applicable TDS rate is verified based on supporting documents (such as PAN, nature of payment, and applicable provisions) before being configured in the vendor master. The data entered is reviewed for accuracy by an authorized personnel. In case of any amendments (e.g., change in PAN, lower deduction certificate, or regulatory changes), the TDS rate in the vendor master is promptly updated after verification.
Failure to file the Tax Audit Report by 30 November or filing with errors due to inadequate preparation of schedules/information for the Tax Auditor may result in penalties under Sec271B.

Taxation team prepares all necessary information and schedules for the Tax Auditor. After completion of the audit, Tax Audit Report is filed by the due date (30 November). Compliance is verified with all clauses in the Audit Report format prior to filing.
SOPs that are not regularly reviewed and updated may fail to reflect current GST regulatory requirements, CBIC circulars or organisational practices, leading to non-compliance.

A structured governance mechanism is established to ensure all SOPs remain current, accurate and aligned with GST regulatory requirements and organisational practices. SOPs are reviewed at least annually; version control and change-log are maintained. Any change recommended by Internal Audit must be actioned within 30 days.
Inconsistent processes due to outdated GST policies or lack of staff awareness, resulting in regulatory non-compliance, interest and operational errors.

SOPs are reviewed periodically; version control is maintained. Regular training is conducted for taxation team members. EOD checklists are prepared and submitted to AVP–Taxation/HOD to monitor daily adherence. TAT breaches are escalated per the defined escalation matrix.
Late / Incorrect Payment of GST Liability

GST liability not paid within statutory timelines (20th of next month) or paid incorrectly due to errors in computation, wrong state-wise allocation, wrong type of tax (CGST/SGST/IGST), or insufficient fund availability, resulting in interest, penalties and non-compliance.

Taxation team confirms rate of GST as per provisions of law; UAT is done to check correctness of system-calculated GST. In case of rate change, Taxation team confirms after consultation with consultant. Monthly GSTR 3B working is cross-tallied with individual ledgers. Liability is discharged by 20th of next month. Banking team is requested in advance to make funds available.
Non-Filing / Late Filing of GST Returns (GSTR 1 & 3B)

GST returns (GSTR 1 and GSTR 3B) not filed within prescribed statutory timelines (11th and 20th of next month respectively), or filed with inaccuracies in outward supply, RCM liabilities or ITC claims.

Taxation team ensures monthly GSTR 1 and GSTR 3B are filed for outward supply for each state by 11th and 20th of next month respectively. All ledgers are cross-tallied with individual ledgers to avoid any manual error. Workings are shared with GST consultant for validation before filing. Returns are filed online using DSC/EVC of AVP – Taxation (authorised signatory).
Non-Filing / Late Filing of Annual GST Returns (GSTR 9 & 9C)
GSTR 9 and GSTR 9C not filed by 31 December or filed with inaccuracies due to inadequate reconciliation of monthly returns with audited financial statements.

Taxation team files annual return GSTR 9 and GSTR 9C by merging all monthly GSTR 1 and GSTR 3B for all states, before 31 December of next year. Prior to filing, a reconciliation statement is prepared to remove turnover items on which GST is not applicable. Workings are shared with GST consultant for validation. GSTR 9C reconciliation covers ITC reconciliation per audited accounts.
Non-Payment / Incorrect Payment of GST under RCM

GST liability under RCM on insurance commissions, legal services, director sitting fees, sponsorship, import of services (reinsurance), car hire and security services may not be booked, booked at incorrect rates, or booked in the wrong state, resulting in penalties, interest and disallowance of ITC.

RCM liability is booked at the time of booking the expense entry for each applicable service category. Training is provided to executives on correct SUN system booking. On a weekly basis, expense ledgers are reviewed to ensure correct GST is booked. For insurance commission, state-wise GST details are extracted from the system on the basis of agent addresses and verified against SUN system entries. Deviations are communicated to the concerned team for correction.
ITC Mismatch between Books and GSTR 2B

ITC availed in books may not match with GSTR 2B due to vendors not filing GSTR 1, SUD GSTIN not mentioned correctly by vendor, or invoice-level mismatches. Failure to reconcile may result in ITC being reversed with interest.
