ITC reconciliation is performed using IGZ Solutions (Super Tax) tool. ITC GL is extracted from Vision system, matched with GSTR 2B line items. Duplicate reversals, suffix/prefix differences in invoice numbers are cleaned before upload. Reconciliation is conducted monthly. Where vendor has not filed GSTR 1, a mail is sent to vendor to file. Annual ITC Reco is also performed.

Intra-day Liquidity Management Intra-day Liquidity Monitoring Tools  /Intra-day liquidity stress scenarios

Bank fails to adequately manage its liquidity position during the trading day, leading to insufficient liquidity to meet its obligations as they come due. If not properly managed, this could result in an inability to settle transactions on time, reputational damage, increased borrowing costs, or potential regulatory violations.

Short Term dynamic Liquidity (STDL) statement is maintained in which the budgeted deposits, loans, cash inflows and outflows are provided by the Finance Team after incorporating current market conditions on a monthly basis. Along with STDL intraday liquidity monitoring and stress testing is also done to incorporate worst case scenarios and verify whether internal limits breached. In case of breach a report is made in ALCO minutes by TMO along with a defined action plan to bring the breach within limts.

Inaccurate, delayed, or insufficient reporting of liquidity positions throughout the trading day can lead to poor decision-making regarding liquidity management, delayed responses to liquidity shortfalls, or an inability to meet obligations as they arise.

The bank has implemented a comprehensive intra-day liquidity reporting framework that provides real-time visibility into the liquidity position across all accounts and payment systems. Intra-day liquidity reports are reviewed by senior management and the risk management committee to ensure that liquidity risks are identified early and sufficient liquidity is available to meet obligations.

1. A mismatch between bank's assets and liabilities across different time periods, which could lead to exposure to interest rate changes, liquidity shortages, or mismatches in cash flow timing.
2. Adverse movements in interest rates leading to reduced Net Interest Income (NII) and economic value, affecting profitability and capital adequacy.

Duration Gap Analysis (DGA) and Traditional Gap Analysis (TGA) is used for comparing the timing and amounts of its assets and liabilities across different time periods (e.g., 0-30 days, 31-90 days, 91-180 days, etc.). The analysis is based on current financial data. In the event of breach of internal limits a report is made in ALCO minutes and a defined action plan is stated to bring the breaches within limits.
Impact Assessment on Market Value of Equity

Failure to properly assess or monitor the potential impact on MVE could lead to significant financial instability, regulatory breaches, or inadequate capital buffers, exposing the bank to unexpected losses.

The bank regularly (monthly basis) performs impact assessments on the Market Value of Equity by simulating various market scenarios, including shifts in interest rates, equity prices, and liquidity conditions.
Earnings at Risk for the banking book
Earnings at Risk (EaR) for the banking book arises from the potential adverse impact of changes in interest rates, credit spreads, and other market factors on the institution’s future earnings.

The bank regularly (montly basis) performs Earnings at Risk (EaR) assessments, using stress testing and scenario analysis to quantify the potential impact of interest rate changes, credit risk changes, and other market factors on future earnings.
Modified Duration for fixed income investment under AFS and HTM

When there is an inaccurate measurement of Modified Duration the sensitivity of Available-for-Sale (AFS) and Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities to interest rate changes. An improper assessment of the modified duration could expose the bank to higher-than-expected price volatility, if market interest rates move unfavorably.

The bank calculates the modified duration of all fixed income investments under AFS and HTM categories using reliable and up-to-date market data, ensuring that the sensitivity to interest rate movements is correctly assessed and accurate.
PV01 / PVBP for income securities and derivative instruments

The sensitivity of PV01 (Price Value of 1 Basis Point) or PVBP (Price Value of a Basis Point) for income securities and derivative instruments to interest rate changes is not accurately measured or managed. An incorrect assessment or failure to monitor PV01/PVBP could expose the bank to unanticipated losses from small changes in interest rates, affecting both the valuation and profitability of the portfolio, especially in volatile market conditions.

The bank regularly (monthly basis) calculates the PV01/PVBP for all income securities and derivative instruments using accurate and up-to-date market data. These calculations are integrated into the bank's risk management framework, with regular stress testing and scenario analysis to assess potential impacts of interest rate fluctuations on the portfolio.
Risk weighted assets for Interest Rate Risk as per Basel III guidelines
Inaccurate Computation of Capital Charge and Regulatory Report

The bank's exposure to interest rate fluctuations is not accurately measured or appropriately capitalized. This could result in an underestimation of the capital required to buffer against potential losses arising from interest rate movements. Non-compliance with Basel III capital adequacy requirements could expose the bank to financial instability and regulatory penalties.

Duration Gap Analysis (DGA) and Traditional Gap Analysis (TGA) is used for comparing the timing and amounts of its assets and liabilities across different time periods (e.g., 0-30 days, 31-90 days, 91-180 days, etc.). The analysis is based on current financial data. In the event of breach of internal limits a report is made in ALCO minutes and a defined action plan is stated to bring the breaches within limits.
An exposure in a currency or position that exceeds the limits for a short period, typically due to timing differences in settlement cycles.

Daylight positions are monitored for individual currencies along with a predefined limit of which is monitored on a daily basis. In case of breach of limits TFO intimates TMO and report is made in ALCO minutes along with an action plan to bring the breaches with limits.
Excessive open positions overnight in foreign exchange or other financial instruments, exposing it to the risk of adverse price movements or liquidity issues.

NOOP report is maintained and monitored by Market Risk team on a daily and is computed by the bank using short hand method by taking max exposure for a given trading day. Limits are defined in ALM policy and an action plan is maintained in case of breach of limits .
Mismatches between assets and liabilities across different time periods (interest rate or liquidity gaps) exceed the set limit.

The bank has established clear and reasonable Aggregate Gap Limits that define the acceptable mismatch between assets and liabilities over different time horizons. Regular assessments of the bank's asset-liability position are conducted, with detailed reports presented to senior management or ALCO.
Value at Risk (VaR) based on FEDAI guidelines
The methodology, assumptions, or inputs used to calculate VaR are incorrect or not consistently applied.
The bank ensures that VaR calculations are consistently based on the latest FEDAI guidelines and incorporate all relevant market data and assumptions, such as historical volatility and correlations.
Calculation of Net Open Position of Single Currency
Potential errors or inaccuracies in assessing the exposure can lead to non-compliance with regulatory limits, inadequate risk management, and exposure to currency fluctuations.

All the relevant positions, including spot, forward, and derivative transactions are incorporated to calculate Net Open Position of Single Currency. The results are regularly reviewed for accuracy. The NOP is monitored daily, and any breaches of limits are promptly reported and escalated for corrective action.
Calculation of Overall Net Open Position
Consolidating positions across different currencies or incorrect valuation methods may lead to inaccurate assessments of the total exposure.

A structured and systematic process is in place for accurately calculating the overall Net Open Position by aggregating all currency exposures, including spot, forward, and derivative positions, using the Short Hand Method.
Calculation of Capital Charge on Forex Net Open Position
Potential for errors or inconsistencies in assessing the exposure or applying incorrect limits specified by the regulatory guidelines.

For calculating capital charge on Forex Net Open Position all the relevant positions are accurately included and appropriate risk-weighted calculations are applied in accordance with regulatory standards. Any discrepancies or breaches in capital requirements are promptly addressed to ALCO for corrective actions.
Limit for Forex Net Open Position
Risk of Forex Net Open Position arises when the position exceeds the approved limit due to errors in calculation, misreporting, or lack of proper monitoring.

A limit on Forex Net Open Position is set and continuously monitored to track exposure. Regular reviews and reconciliations of positions are conducted to ensure compliance with the established limits. Any breach of the limit triggers immediate escalation to senior management and relevant committees for corrective action.
Calculation of Capital Charge for Interest Rate Risk in the portfolio termed as 'General Market Risk'

Inaccuracies in assessing interest rate exposures or improper application of regulatory guidelines and errors in the calculation may result in insufficient capital charge for interest rate risk reserve to cover potential losses from interest rate movements.

The bank has established regulatory standards such as those outlined in Basel III or local regulatory guidelines. The calculation incorporates all relevant interest rate exposures across different asset classes, ensuring the correct application of risk-weighting factors.
Overall net short position or long position in trading book
The overall net open position in the trading book lies in the potential for significant financial loss if market conditions move unfavorably.

A clear limit is established for the overall net open position in the trading book, and these positions are continuously monitored. The trading book is regularly reviewed for alignment with risk tolerance limits, and any positions that exceed the predefined limits trigger immediate escalation for corrective action.
Vertical disallowance arises when a bank misclassifies or fails to account for certain positions or transactions in accordance with regulatory guidelines.

All positions are classified and treated in accordance with regulatory guidelines regarding vertical disallowance. This includes accurate risk weighting, consistent application of disallowance rules, and the proper segregation of positions in the trading book.

Horizontal disallowance arises when certain positions, typically within the same risk category, are improperly offset or aggregated, leading to a misrepresentation of the bank's capital charge or exposure.
A clear framework is established to ensure that horizontal disallowance rules are followed correctly, preventing the improper offsetting of positions within the same risk category.
Capital Charge for 'Specific Risk' of each security

The risk of capital charge for 'Specific Risk' of each security arises when their is insufficient capital buffer, leaving the institution exposed to losses from security-specific risks such as credit risk, market volatility, or issuer-specific events, potentially leading to financial instability and regulatory non-compliance.

A process is in place for calculating the capital charge for the specific risk of each security. This includes using appropriate risk models that account for factors like credit ratings, volatility, and the potential impact of specific events on individual securities.
Limit Management as mentioned in the Bank's Policy
Risk of no updates or untimely updates to ALM policy

Bank does not adequately enforce or monitor the limits set for various risk exposures as part of its risk management framework. Failure to adhere to established limits could result in excessive risk-taking, leading to financial losses, regulatory breaches, reputational damage, or an inability to absorb shocks during periods of market volatility or operational stress.

1. The Compliance Assurance Department(CAD) utilizes Knowledge Management Tools (KMT) to access, track, and stay updated with regulatory requirements. The CAD team also disseminates regulatory guidelines from RBI to respective business unit heads at the same time CAD maintains a tracker to monitor and adhere to all regulatory guidelines and evaluates compliance risk.
2. Internal Limits are defined in the ALM policy
Monitoring of Limits as per Bank's policy and regulatory guidelines
Risk of no updates or untimely updates to ALM policy
Breach of internal limits (e.g., liquidity mismatches, interest rate gaps) may lead to excessive risk exposures, potential financial losses, regulatory non-compliances.

1. TMO team monitors the various limits as mentioned in the ALM policy & also been reported to ALCO in their monthly meeting. Further, in case of the breach of limit, it is reported in the subsequent month ALCO meeting.
2. Action plan is defined in ALCO minutes to bring the breaches within limits.
Market Rate Monitoring and Valuation Risk.

Bank fails to properly track and evaluate the market rates used in its transactions, leading to discrepancies in pricing, inaccurate valuations, or inappropriate hedging strategies. The failure to correctly monitor and validate market rates in real-time could also lead to unauthorized exposures or mispricing of transactions.

The bank has implemented a comprehensive Rate Scan process to continuously track and monitor market rates used in transactions, ensuring they align with reliable and independent sources. The treasury or risk management team conducts regular reconciliations of market rates to ensure consistency with trusted benchmarks (e.g., FEDAI, Reuters, or Bloomberg).
Bank fails to regularly review and update its stress testing policies in response to changing market conditions, regulatory requirements, or internal risk profiles.

The bank has established a formal process for the periodic review and update of its stress testing policies. This review is conducted at least annually or more frequently if there are significant changes in market conditions, business operations, or regulatory requirements. The results of the stress testing policy review are presented to senior management, the risk management committee, and regulatory authorities, as required.
Stress Testing Framework is not comprehensive, up-to-date, or accurately reflects potential risk scenarios, leading to a failure to identify vulnerabilities in the institution’s financial position.

The bank has implemented a stress testing framework that accurately reflects a wide range of potential risk scenarios, including market shocks, liquidity crises, operational disruptions, and regulatory changes. The framework is regularly reviewed and updated to account for changes in market conditions, business operations, and emerging risks. Stress tests are conducted using both historical data and hypothetical scenarios to assess the institution’s resilience under extreme but plausible conditions.
Failure to conduct regular and comprehensive stress tests may leave the bank unprepared for adverse events, leading to inadequate risk management and potential financial distress.

1. The Bank conduct monthly stress tests covering liquidity, interest rate risk, and intraday liquidity scenario which Include bank-specific and market-wide stress events in testing.
2. The Bank conduct quarterly stress tests covering market risk, including duration gap analysis and traditional gap analysis and PV01 / PVBP. 
2. Stress Testing results are presented to the ALCO on the monthly basis and quarterly basis respectively.

All arrangements with Exchange House would be reviewed annually (calendar year) by the Board of KMBL. sheets.name: 7 Parameters checklist
rows:
Functional Independence:-
. The Internal Audit Department should be independent from the internal control process in order to avoid any conflict of interest.
. It should not be assigned the responsibility of performing other accounting or operational functions.
.  The management should ensure that the internal audit staff perform their duties with objectivity and impartiality.
. The internal audit head should report to the Board of Directors through Audit Committee of the Board.
. The Board of Directors and top management will be responsible for having in place an effective risk-based internal audit system
RBI Guidance note on  risk-based internal audit
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Independence and Objectivity:-
The internal audit activity must be independent, and internal auditors must be objective in performing their work.
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

Organizational Independence:-
The chief audit executive must report to a level within the organization that allows the internal audit activity to fulfill its responsibilities. The chief audit executive must confirm to the board, at least annually, the organizational independence of the internal audit activity.
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

The internal audit activity must be free from interference in determining the scope of internal auditing, performing work, and communicating results. The chief audit executive must disclose such interference to the board and discuss the implications
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

Direct Interaction with the board:-
The chief audit executive must communicate and interact directly with the board.
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Individual Objectivity:-
Internal auditors must have an impartial, unbiased attitude and avoid any conflict of interest.
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

If independence or objectivity is impaired in fact or appearance,whether the details of the impairment are disclosed to appropriate parties? The nature of the disclosure being dependent on the impairment?
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

Whether the Internal auditors have refrained from assessing specific operations for which they were previously responsible? If not, whether Objectivity is presumed to be impaired if an internal auditor provides assurance services for an activity for which the internal auditor had responsibility within the previous year and such impairment is disclosed as above?
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)
Whether Assurance engagements for functions over which the chief audit executive has responsibility has been overseen by a party outside the internal audit activity?
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

The internal audit activity may provide assurance services where it had previously performed consulting services, provided the nature of the consulting did not impair objectivity and provided individual objectivity is managed when assigning resources to the engagement.
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)
Whether the Internal auditors have provided consulting services relating to operations for which they had previous responsibilities, in order to improve the operations?
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

If internal auditors have potential impairments to independence or objectivity relating to proposed consulting services, whether disclosures were made to the engagement client prior to accepting the engagement?
INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS FOR THE PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE OF INTERNAL AUDITING (STANDARDS)

Internal Auditor
- Should be a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant, whether in practice or not, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board to conduct internal audit of the functions and activities of the company
- May or may not be an employee
HIA as well as the internal audit function shall have the authority to communicate with any staff member and have access to all records and files that necessary to carry out the responibility.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Reporting Line:-
The HIA shall directly report to either the Audit Committee of the Board (ACB) / MD & CEO or Whole Time Director (WTD)
. BOD decide to allow the MD/CEO/WTD to be reporting authority of the HIA. Further in such cases the ACB shall meet the HIA at least once in a quarter, without presence of the senior management inculding the MD & CEO/WTD
. HIA shall not have any reporting relationship with the business verticales of the bank & shall not given any business target.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Remuneration:-
The independence and objectivity of the internal audit function could be undermined if the remuneration of internal audit staff is linked to the financial performance of the business lines for which they exercise audit responsibilities. The remuneration policies should be structured in a way that it avoids creating conflict of interest and compromising audit’s independence and objectivity.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements
Whether the Internal Audit Function, comprises of the Chief Internal Auditor and a team of individuals performing internal audits in an organisation
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)  - 210

Bank are required to put in place a risk based audit system a part of their internal control  framework that relies on a well defined policy for internal audit functional independence with sufficient standing and authority within the bank.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

The functions of the Risk Management Committee/ Department (RMC/RMD) and the role of risk-based internal audit need to be distinguished, RMC/RMD focuses on areas such as: - 
 - Identification
 - Monitoring
 - Measurement of Risk & Development of policies & procedure , use of risk management model etc.

The risk-based internal audit, on the other hand, undertakes an independent risk assessment solely for the purpose of formulating the risk-based audit plan keeping in view the inherent business risks of an activity/location and the effectiveness of the control systems for monitoring the inherent risks of the business activity
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Policy for risk based internal audit:-
Under risk-based internal audit, the focus will shift from the present system of full-scale Transaction testing to risk Identification,prioritization of audit areas and allocation of audit resources in accordance with the risk assessment, Bank will therefore need to develop a well defined policy, duly approve by the board to undertae risk based internal audit. Policy should inculde the following
Risk Assessment methodology for identifying the risk areas.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Risk Assessment:-
The risk assessment would, as an independent activity, cover risks at various levels (corporate and branch; the portfolio and individual transactions, etc)  as also the processes in place to identify, measure, monitor and control the risks. The internal audit department should
devise the risk assessment methodology, with the approval of the Board of Directors.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The risk assessment process should, inter alia, include the following :-
a. Identification of inherent business risks
b. Evaluation of the effectiveness of the control systems for monitoring the inherent risks.
c. Drawing up a risk-matrix for taking into account both the factors.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The basis for determination of the level (high, medium, low) and trend (increasing, stable, decreasing) of inherent business risks and control risks should be clearly spelt out.
Refer guideline issued by RBI for matrix and factor of risk.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The risk assessment methodology inculde the following parameters.
Previous internal audit report and compliance
Proposed changes in business lines
Significant change in management / key personnel
· Results of latest regulatory examination report
· Reports of external auditors
· Industry trends and other environmental factors
· Time lapsed since last audit
· Volume of business and complexity of activities
· Substantial performance variations from the budget
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit
All banks need to put in place an independent risk assessment system in the internal audit department for focusing on the material risk areas and prioritizing the audit work.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

Audit Plan:-
The annual audit plan, approved by the Board, should include the schedule and the rationale for audit work planned. It should also include all risk areas and their prioritisation based on the level and direction of risk.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The Audit Plan should prioritize audit work to give greater attention to the areas of:
 (i)High Magnitude and high frequency
(ii) High Magnitude and medium frequency
(iii) Medium magnitude and high frequency
(iv) High magnitude and low frequency
(v) Medium Magnitude and medium frequency.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit
The risk assessment should invariably be undertaken on a yearly basis (paragraph 4.3 of the 'Guidance note on risk based internal audit'.)
Implementation of Risk-based internal audit (RBIA) in banks

As indicated in paragraph 6.1 of the 'Guidance note on risk based internal audit', the bank has to prepare a Risk Audit Matrix which would be based on the magnitude and frequency of risk. Preparation of the Risk Audit Matrix can also enable the bank to move towards the Advanced Measurement Approach for Operational Risk under Basel II.

Scope and Objectives of the Internal Audit Function
The objectives of internal audit functions vary widely and depend on the size and structure of the entity and the requirements of management and, where applicable, those charged with governance. The activities of the internal audit function may include one or more of the following:
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 230
Monitoring of internal control. The internal audit function may be assigned specific responsibility for reviewing controls, monitoring their operation and recommending improvements thereto.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 230

Examination of financial and operating information. The internal audit function may be assigned to review the means used to identify, measure, classify and report financial and operating information, and to make specific inquiry into individual items, including detailed testing of transactions, balances and procedures
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 230

Review of operating activities. The internal audit function may be assigned to review the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of operating activities, including non- financial activities of an entity.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 230

Review of compliance with laws and regulations. The internal audit function may be assigned to review compliance with laws, regulations and other external requirements, and with management policies and directives and other internal requirements.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 230

Risk management. The internal audit function may assist the organization by identifying and evaluating significant exposures to risk and contributing to the improvement of risk management and control systems.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 230

Governance. The internal audit function may assess the governance process in its accomplishment of objectives on ethics and values, performance management and accountability, communicating risk and control information to appropriate areas of the organization and effectiveness of communication among those charged with governance, external and internal auditors, and management.

Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

Banks must ensure and demonstrate through proper documentation that their risk-based 
internal audit framework captures all the significant criteria / principles suited for their 
organisational structure, the business model and the risks.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Scope:-
. The primary focus of risk-based internal audit will be to provide reasonable
assurance to the Board and top management about the adequacy and effectiveness of the
risk management and control framework in the banks.
. While examining the effectiveness of control framework, the risk-based internal audit should report on proper
recording and reporting of major exceptions and excesses.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The precise scope of risk-based internal audit must be determined by each bank for low, medium, high, very high and extremely high risk areas. However, at the minimum, it must review/report on:-
Process on risk identification
Control envirnment in various areas
Gaps if any in control
Data integrity, reliability, Intergirty, MIS
Regulatory & Statutory compliance
Budgetary control
Trans testing and verification of assets to the extent.
Monitoring compliance.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The scope of risk-based internal audit should also include a review of the systems in place for ensuring compliance with money laundering controls; identifying potential inherent business risks and control risks,
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

Performance Evaluation:-
. The Internal Audit Department should conduct periodical reviews, annually or more frequently, of the risk-based internal audit undertaken by it vis-à-vis the approved
audit plan.
. The Board of Directors/Audit Committee of Board should periodically assess theperformance of the risk-based internal audit for reliability, accuracy and objectivity
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

As mentioned in paragraph 6.1 of the 'Guidance note on risk based internal audit', the bank should undertake 100 per cent transaction testing if an area falls in cell “C- Extremely High Risk” of the risk matrix.
 The bank has to decide on the level oftransaction testing based on its risk based internal audit policy duly approved by the Board.
Implementation of Risk-based internal audit (RBIA) in banks

Banks are advised to review the methodology of conducting the risk-based internal audit and the policy in this regard so as to align the same with the guidelines issued by RBI. As already indicated in paragraph 3 of our letter dated December 27, 2002, mentioned above, banks should form a Task Force comprising senior executives and entrust them with the responsibility of chalking out an action plan for switching over to risk-based internal audit. This process may be expedited and compliance with our guidelines ensured at an early date.
Implementation of Risk-based internal audit (RBIA) in banks

Scope of the internal audit, ordinarily, includes
a. Examination and evaluation of the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal control systems.
B. Review of the application and effectiveness of risk management procedures and risk assessment methodologies
c. Review of the management and financial information systems, including the electronic information systems
d. Review of the accuracy and reliability of the accounting records and financial reports
e. Review of the means of safeguarding assets
f. Appraisal of the economy and efficiency of the operations
g. Testing of both transactions and the functioning of specific internal control procedures
h. Review of the systems established to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, code(s) of conduct and the implementation of policies and procedures
i. Testing of the reliability and timeliness of the regulatory reporting

This SIA distinguishes the internal auditor’s responsibilities in relation to compliance with two different categories of laws and regulations as follows:
(a) The provisions of those laws and regulations generally recognised to have a direct effect on the determination of material amounts and disclosures in the financial statements such as tax and laws regulating the reporting framework; and
(b) Other laws and regulations that do not have a direct effect on the determination of the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, but compliance with which may be fundamental to the operating aspects of the business, to an entity’s ability to continue its business, or to avoid material penalties (for example, compliance with the terms of an operating license, compliance with regulatory solvency requirements, or compliance with environmental regulations). Non-compliance with other laws and
regulations may result in fines, litigation or other consequences for the entity, the costs of which may need to be provided for in the financial statements, or may even have a significant impact on the operations of the entity, but are not considered to have a direct effect on the financial statements, as described in paragraph 18(a). Non-compliance with laws and regulations that have a significant impact on the operations of the entity may cause the entity to cease operations, or call into question the entity’s continuance as a going concern. For example, non-compliance with the requirements of the entity’s license or other entitlement to perform its operations could have such an impact (for example, for a bank, noncompliance with capital or investment requirements).

Outsourced internal audit arrangements:-
The Board of Directors and top management are responsible for ensuring that the risk-based internal audit continues to function effectively even though it is outsourced.
The following aspects may prevent any risk of breakdown in internal controls on account of outsourcing arrangements:
Before entering into an outsourcing arrangement the bank should perform due diligence to satisfy outsourced has the necessary expertise and skills.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The contract, in writing, should at the minimum, specify the following:
. scope and frequency of work
. manner and frequency of reporting to the bank
. Incorporation of changes in the terms of contract, 
. locations where the work papers will be stored
. Internal audit reports are the property of the bank
. employees authorized  for the access of working papers
. supervisors are to be granted immediate and full access to relatedwork papers
. The management should continue to satisfy itself that the outsourced activity is being competently managed
. All work done by the vendor should be documented and reported to the top
management through the internal audit department.
 To avoid significant operational risk that may arise on account of a sudden termination the bank should have in place a contingency plan to mitigate any discontinuity in audit coverage.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

Following area audit can be outsource

Whether the internal auditor should consider the effect of an IT environment on the internal audit engagement, inter alia:
a. the extent to which the IT environment is used to record, compile, process and analyse information; and
b. the system of internal control in existence in the entity with
regard to:
 the flow of authorised, correct and complete data to the
processing centre;
 the processing, analysis and reporting tasks undertaken in
the installation; and
 the impact of computer-based accounting system on the

Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

The internal auditor should have sufficient knowledge of the
information technology systems to plan, direct, supervise, control
and review the work performed. The sufficiency of knowledge would depend on the nature and extent of the IT environment. The internal auditor should consider whether any specialised IT skills are needed in the conduct of the audit, for example, the operating knowledge of a specialised ERP system. Specialised skills may be needed, for example, to:
a) obtain sufficient understanding of the effect of the IT environment on
systems, processes, internal control and risk management systems;
b) design and perform appropriate tests of control and  substantive procedures; and
c) determine the effect of the IT environment on assessment of overall audit risk.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

If specialized skills are needed, the internal auditor should seek the assistance of a technical expert possessing such skills, who may either be the internal auditor's staff or an outside professional. Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Planning:
The internal auditor should obtain an understanding of the systems, processes, control environment, risk-response activities and internal control systems sufficient to plan the internal audit and to determine the nature, timing and extent of the audit procedures, in accordance with SIA 1, “Planning an Internal Audit”. Such an understanding would help the internal auditor to develop an effective audit approach
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Risk Assessment
The internal auditor should make an assessment of inherent and control risks for material assertions related to significant processes and systems.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

The internal auditor should review whether the information technology system in the entity considers the confidentiality, effectiveness, integrity, availability, compliance and validity of data and information processed. The internal auditor should also review the effectiveness and safeguarding of IT resources, including – people, applications, facilities and data.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Audit Procedures:
The internal auditor should consider the IT environment in designing audit procedures to review the systems, processes, controls and risk management framework of the entity.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Review of Information Technology Environment:
The internal auditor should review the robustness of the IT
environment and consider any weakness or deficiency in the design
and operation of any IT control within the entity, by reviewing:
a) System Audit reports of the entity, conducted by independent
Information System auditors;
b) Reports of system breaches, unsuccessful login attempts,
passwords compromised and other exception reports;
c) Reports of network failures, virus attacks and threats to
perimeter security, if any;
d) General controls like segregation of duties, physical access
records, logical access controls;
e) Application controls like input, output, processing and run-torun
controls; and
f) Excerpts from the IT policy of the entity relating to business
continuity planning, crisis management and disaster recovery
procedures.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Outsourced Information Processing:
The internal auditor should assess and review the reliance which the management of the entity places on the outsourced agency, in case where such information processing has been outsourced to the outside party. The risks associated with such outsourced services should be considered by the internal auditor in light of the review of IT controls prevalent in such outside entity. The internal auditor should also review the extent to which the entity’s controls provide reasonable assurance regarding the completeness, validity, reliability and availability of the data and information processed by such outsourced agency.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Documentation:
The internal auditor should document the internal audit plan, nature, timing and extent of audit procedures performed and the
conclusions drawn from the evidence obtained. In an internal audit in IT environment, some or all of the audit evidence may be in the electronic form. The internal auditor should satisfy himself that such evidence is adequately and safely stored and is retrievable in its entirety as and when required.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI) - 390

Definition
- Risk Management is a process with a series of steps, taken on a continuous basis to identify the threats and vulnerabilities, assess them for severity and likelihood, monitor risks, prioritize them for action and to minimize their possible negative impact through mitigation 
- Risk Management Framework is the combination of structure, systems and processes put in place to organise the various risk management activities and to integrate them seamlessly into the organisation.
actions

Responsibility of IA
- Unless specifically excluded, IA shall plan & conduct RBIA
- Where RM Framework is implemented - plan and perform audit procedures to evaluate the design, implementation and operating effectiveness 
- Where no formal risk management framework exists - design and conduct audit procedures to highlight any exposures arising from weak or absent risk management activities, make recommendations to implement and strengthen related processes
- not assume any responsibility to manage the risks or to execute risk management decisions & mitigate or resolve risks
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Definition
- Governance is defined as a set of relationships between the company and its various stakeholders (both internal and external), and provides the
structure through which the company’s objectives are achieved
- Governance Activities generally form part of ELC

Responsibility of IA
- where management has implemented a formal governance framework, and unless specifically excluded - plan and perform internal audit procedures to evaluate the design, implementation and operating effectiveness
- no formal governance framework exists -  conduct audit to highlight any exposures arising from weak or absent governance activities and processes, make recommendations to implement and strengthen

- where formal Compliance framework exists - plan and perform internal audit procedures to evaluate the design, implementation and operating effectiveness
-  no formal compliance framework exists - shall design and conduct audit procedures with a view to highlight any exposures arising from weak or absent compliance activities and processes, make recommendations to implement and strengthen
 - findings shall be reported along with the following:
(a) the scope, listing all the specific laws and regulations tested;
(b) audit procedures performed, sample selected, and population
covered;

Applicability u/s 138:
1. Listed Companies

2. Unlisted Companies:
- Paid up Share in PY Capital >= 50 Cr 
                         OR
- Turnover in PY >= 200 Cr
                        OR

                        OR

3. Private Companies:
- Turnover in PY >= 200 Cr
                        OR
- O/s Loans/Borrowings from Bank or Public FI at any point of time in PY >= 100 Cr

Internal Auditor
- Should be a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant, whether in practice or not, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board to conduct internal audit of the functions and activities of the company
- May or may not be an employee

Scope
AC or Board in consultation with the IA shall formulate
- Scope
- Functioning
- Periodicity
- Methodology
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Framework
- Every IA is bound by Code of Ethics of the Organization &/or Professional Institution
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Basic Principles
1. Independence
- Position & Reporting of Chief IA
- Powers & Authority derived from superiors by Chief IA
- Direct Reporting to Board/AC i.e. highest authority
- IA function to be positioned outside functions subject to IA
- If IA is assigned operational role following to be ensured
* due approvals
* short duration
* limitations communicated:
(a) Unable to assume ownership/accountability of the process 
(b) Inability to take operational decisions which may be subject to IA later on
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

2. Integrity and Objectivity
- Avoid Conflict of Interest & not seek undue personal benefit
- not allow prejudice or bias to override his objectivity, in arriving at conclusions or reporting his opinion
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

3. Due Professional Care
- Attention to 
(a) establishing the scope
(b) prevent omission of key aspects
(c )  recognizing the risks and materiality of the areas
(d)  establishing the extent of testing required
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

4. Confidentiality
- not disclose any such information to a party outside the internal audit function
-  keep confidential information secure
- not share with third parties outside the company, without the specific approval of the Management or Client or unless there is a legal or a professional responsibility
 - Internal audit reports shall be addressed to specified internal auditees 
- Internal audit reports distributed to only those who appointed or engaged the Internal Auditor and as per their directions
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

5. Skills and Competence
- Internal Auditor shall have or obtain sound knowledge, strong interpersonal skills, practical experience and professional expertise in certain areas and other competence required
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

6. Risk Based Audit
-  identify the important audit areas through a risk assessment exercise 
- tailor the audit activities prioritising high risk areas with more time & vice-a versa
- Objectives:
(a) Audit procedures need not cover whole process, can be limited to important controls
(b) Establish linkage to aspects relevant and connected with company and functional objectives
(c) Findings and issues highlighted are significant and important & time is not devoted to areas with low probability of significant observations
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

7. System and Process Focus
- root cause analysis to be conducted on deviations for system improvement or automation, to strengthen the process and prevent  repetition of errors
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

8. Participation in Decision Making
- avoid passing any judgement or render an opinion on past management decisions
- avoid participation in operational decision making which may be subject of a subsequent audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

9. Sensitive to Multiple Stakeholder Interest
 - evaluate the implications of his observations and recommendations on multiple stakeholders
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

10. Quality and Continuous Improvement
(a) ensure factual accuracy of the observations;
(b) to validate the accuracy of all findings; and
(c) continuously improve the quality of the internal audit process and the internal audit reports. 
- self-assessment mechanism Ito monitor his own performance and also that of his
subordinates and external experts on whom he is relying
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Applicability:

Type of Assignments not covered:
1. only a summary of observations, along with recommendations

3. Reviews of statutory filings or compliance reports, where only a report of non-compliance is submitted;
4. Consulting (or advisory) assignments, such as operational, technical or strategic reviews, due-diligence and other

2. Limited Assurance

Key components:
1. 3 Parties - Internal Auditor, Auditee & Assurance User (egg: AC/Board)

Introducation:-
Dissemination of the results of internal audit and reporting the findings to management, and those charged with governance, is an essential part of any internal audit.

Reporting of internal audit results is generally undertaken in two stages:
. At the end of a particular audit assignment, an “Internal Audit Report” covering a specific area, function or part of the entity is prepared by the Internal Auditor highlighting key observations arising from those assignments
. On a periodic basis, at the close of a plan period, a comprehensive report of all the internal audit activities covering the entity and the plan period is prepared by the Chief Internal Auditor (or the Engagement Partner, in case of external service provider).

Also, this SIA does not cover the form or content of the Internal Audit Report where an assurance (i.e. a written opinion as per SIA 110) is being provided, for which a separate Standard on Internal Audit (SIA) 380, “Issuing Assurance Reports” should be referred to.

. A summary of the corrective actions required 
. Nature of assurance

. No internal audit report shall be issued in final form unless a written draft of the report has previously been shared with the auditee.
. The internal audit report shall be issued within a reasonable time frame from the completion of the internal audit work.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Explantory comments:-
. Basis of internal audit report
. Conduected in accordance with SIA
. Content and format of internal audit report
. Documentation
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Introduction:-
This Standard deals with the responsibility of the Internal Auditor in monitoring and reporting of prior audit issues, usually in the form of an “Action Taken Report (ATR) of previous audits”

Scope: This Standard applies to all prior internal audits where audit issues remain open, pending the implementation of audit recommendations within pre-agreed timelines.
SIA- 390 Monitoring and reporting of perior audit issues
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Requirements:-
. The Chief Internal Auditor is responsible for continuously monitoring the closure of prior audit issues through a timely implementation of action plans included in past audits.
. After receiving confirmation from the auditee regarding the implementation of corrective actions, additional audit procedures shall be performed by the Internal Auditor to confirm that the issues have 
been adequately addressed.
. In case of delays or ineffective implementation of the agreed corrective actions, the Internal Auditor shall escalate such delays and concerns to the appropriate levels of management.
. The internal auditor shall periodically report to the management, and the Audit Committee, the status of prior issues (generally in the form of an “Action Taken Report”)
SIA- 390 Monitoring and reporting of perior audit issues
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Explanatory commnents:-
Monitoring of prior issues
Closure of prior issue
Escalation Procedure
Documentation
SIA- 390 Monitoring and reporting of perior audit issues
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Introduction:-
. This Standard deals with the responsibility of the Internal Auditor to conduct internal audit in an Information Technology (IT) environment.
 The two main components of ITE include:-
IT infrastructure.
Application software and data

Scope: This Standard applies to internal audit assignments conducted in an IT environment, where the IT systems are managed by the company. A separate Standard on Internal Audit (SIA) 530 “Third Party 
Service Provider” covers those situations where the IT systems are managed by external third-party service providers.

SIA-520 INTERNAL AUDITING IN AN INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY ENVIRONMENT
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Requirement:-
. Internal Auditor shall gain an understanding of the business operations and the corresponding IT Environment
. Internal Auditor shall have or acquire the requisite qualifications, skillsets and experience to perform IT audits
. Internal Auditor shall assess the ITE to define the scope of the IT audit and identify internal controls relevant to the audit.
. Appropriate planning activities shall be performed by the Internal Auditor before commencing the field work.
. As part of audit execution phase, Internal Auditor shall test the design, implementation and operating effectiveness of relevant IT controls and identify control gaps.
. Internal Auditor shall document the ITE understanding, scope of work, risk assessment, planning, testing and reporting related activities.
. The outcome of the audit procedures shall be shared with the process owners and action plans to address the areas of concerns drawn jointly.

SIA-520 INTERNAL AUDITING IN AN INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY ENVIRONMENT
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Explanatory comments:-
. IT Understanding and Risk Assessment
. Internal Auditor Credentials
. IT Audit Scoping
. IT Audit Planning 
. Audit Execution
. Audit documentation
. Management Disucssinon on deficiencies

SIA-520 INTERNAL AUDITING IN AN INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY ENVIRONMENT
Para 4.1 to 4.7 and pg no 3 to 5
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Introduction:-
. This Standard deals with the responsibility of the Internal Auditor and management with regard to risks arising from situations where some parts of the entity’s business operations, processes and information reside with Third-Party Service Providers (TPSPs)
They are External outsourced service provider to whom either full or some aspect of business function, operation or processing or activity is outsourced.
. These risks relate to, and can adversely impact, business processing, financial and operational management, information security, legal compliance, business continuity, etc.  With increased reliance being placed by 
the User Entity on the TPSPs, there is a need to review and assess these risks, residing elsewhere, in an effective manner.
. The nature and extent of work to be performed by the User Entity’s Internal Auditor depends upon the importance of the business process and information to the organisation and the significance and relevance 
of the outsourced services in the view of audit.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)
Scope: This Standard applies to both the TPSPs and their User Entities and outlines the requirements for conducting an internal audit.
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Requirements:-
. The Internal Auditor shall study and evaluate the scope of TPSP’sservices, governance and oversight process in place to outsource and manage risks of deploying TPSPs
.  The Internal Auditor shall review both, the Pre-engagement and Post_x0002_engagement due diligence undertaken by the User Entity, including an assessment of the control environment at the TPSP.
. A periodic independent risk assessment of each third-party arrangement shall be conducted by the management and reviewed by the Internal Auditor to ensure adequate mitigation steps and control
activities are designed, implemented, and operated effectively.
. The Internal Auditor shall conduct an independent audit of the TPSP (where permissible), which shall include TPSPs’ entity’s level controls, IT controls and process controls
. In case, the Internal Auditor is not performing an independent audit but obtains TPAA reports, the review of the TPAA reports shall be undertaken in compliance with Standard
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Explanatory Comments:-
.Third party governance and oversight
. Third party due diligence
. Third party risk assessment
. Third party performance monitoring
.  Evaluation of Independent Third-party Audit and Assurance Report
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Introduction:-
“Internal audit is an independent management function, which involves a continuous and critical appraisal of the functioning of an entity with a view to suggest improvements thereto and add value to and strengthen the overall governance mechanism of the entity, including the entity’s strategic risk management and internal control system.

. The internal auditor should either have or obtain such skills and competence, acquired through general education, technical knowledge obtained through study and formal courses, as are necessary for the purpose of discharging his responsibilities.
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Scope:-
. This Standard on Internal Audit shall apply whenever an internal audit is carried out, whether carried out by an in house internal audit department or by an external firm of professional accountants. For the purpose of this Standard, the term “firm” means a sole practitioner/ proprietor, partnership or any such entity of professional accountants as may be permitted by law1.
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Objectives:-
In the case of the in – house internal audit or a firm carrying out internal audit, the person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit should ensure that the system of quality assurance include policies and procedures addressing each of the following elements:
. Leadership responsibilities for quality in internal audit.
. Ethical requirements
. Acceptance and continuance of client relationship and specific engagement, as may be applicable.
. Human resources
. Engagment performance
. Monitoring
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

The person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit needs to ensure that the quality assurance framework is embedded in the internal audit.
. Developing an internal audit manual clearly defining the specific role and responsibilities, policies and procedures, documentation requirements, reporting lines and protocols, targets and training requirements for the staff, internal audit performance measures and the indicators.
. Ensuring that the internal audit staff at all levels is appropriately  trained and adequately supervised
. Identifying the customers of the internal audit activity
. Establishing a formal process of feedback from the users of the internal audit services, such as the senior management executives.
. The responses received from the users of the internal audit services should also be shared with the
appropriate levels of management and those charged with governance
. Establishing appropriate performance criteria for measuring the performance of the internal audit function.
. Identify and benchmark with industry/ peer group performance
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

The quality assurance framework established by the person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit should, therefore, cover all the elements of the internal audit activity:-
. Development and implementation of the internal audit policies and procedures.
. Maintenance and monitoring of the budget for the IA activity.
. Maintenance and updation of audit plan
. Identification risk areas.
. Acquisition and deployment of audit tools and use of tech to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness.
. Co-ordination with external audit
. Staffing related aspects of internal audit- recruitment, traning
. Planning and implementation of the training and professional development of the internal audit staff
. Implementation of the performance monitoring for the internal audit activity and periodic monioring for the same.
. Review of the follow up action taken on the finding of the internal audit activity.
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Internal Quality review:-
. The internal quality review framework should be designed with a view to provide reasonable assurance to that the internal audit is able to efficiently and effectively achieve its objectives of adding value and strengthening the overall governance mechanism of the entity.
Internal Quality Reviewer:-
.  The internal quality review should be done by the person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit and/ or other experienced member(s) of the internal audit function.
. The internal quality reviews should be undertaken on an ongoing basis.
Communicating the Results of the Internal Quality Review:-
The person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit should also ensure that the results of the internal quality reviews are also communicated to the appropriate levels of management and those charged with governance on a timely basis along with the proposed plan of action to address issues and concerns raised in the review report.
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

External Quality Review:-
. External quality review is a critical factor in ensuring and enhancing the quality of internal audit
. The frequency should not in any case be less than once in three years.
External Quality Reviewer:-
. The external quality review should be done by a professionally qualified person having an in depth knowledge and experience.
. The external quality reviewer should be appointed in consultation with the person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit, senior management and those charged with governance.
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit
Compendium of Standards on Internal Audit - IASB (ICAI)

Communicating Results of the External Quality Review:-
. The external quality reviewer should discuss his findings with the person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit. His final report should contain his opinion on all the parameters of the internal audit activity.
. The person entrusted with the responsibility for the quality in internal audit should, also submit to those charged with governance, a plan of action to address the issues and concerns raised by the external quality
reviewers in his report.
SIA-7 Quality Assurance In internal audit

sheets.name: Risk based IA
rows: Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005
Each bank under the proposed Risk Based Supervision (RBS) framework of RBI, To prepare a risk profile of its own, taking into account the various risks to which the bank is exposed.
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

The risk profile of the bank would determine the supervisory programme comprising off-site surveillance, targeted on-site inspections, structured meetings with banks, commissioned external audits, specific supervisory directions and new policy action, as warranted
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Implementation of the RBS framework -
a. Setting up of risk management architecture
b. Adoption of risk focused internal Audit
c. Strengthening of management information system and information technology 
d. Addressing Human Resources Department (HRD) issues
e. Setting up of a compliance unit
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Scope of the internal audit, ordinarily, includes
a. Examination and evaluation of the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal control systems.
B. Review of the application and effectiveness of risk management procedures and risk assessment methodologies
c. Review of the management and financial information systems, including the electronic information systems
d. Review of the accuracy and reliability of the accounting records and financial reports
e. Review of the means of safeguarding assets
f. Appraisal of the economy and efficiency of the operations
g. Testing of both transactions and the functioning of specific internal control procedures
h. Review of the systems established to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, code(s) of conduct and the implementation of policies and procedures
i. Testing of the reliability and timeliness of the regulatory reporting
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005
The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision of the Bank for International Settlements has also pronounced certain principles required to be followed for an effective internal audit in banks
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Following area audit can be outsource
 a. Those which are routine in nature.
B. Those which are exceptional and/or for which no expertise is available within the bank.
C. Those where cost of being carried out in-house would exceed the benefits to be derived
there from provided that the cost of outsourcing is lesser than the former cost
d. System Audit
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005
Cost Benefit Analysis of the Internal audit Function
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005
Risk assessment should be carried out & units to be categorized into  high, medium or low risk units
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Scope of audit.
As a general principle, high-risk audit units such as
treasury division of the bank should be subject to 100% transactions testing
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005
Sampling technique proposed to be so adopted should first be placed for the approval of the audit committee
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Four Major Steps to be adopted by the internal auditors:
1. Preparation / Creation of Organisation Structure - Audit Plan is required
2. Identification of auditable units. Determine the risk
 of non-audit of unidentifiable auditable units
3. Conduct risk assessment - To identify the risks and categorize the risks as high, medium and low, depending upon the nature of the risks. Internal audit of banks can be classified as inherent banking business risks such as credit and market risks. 
    - Control risks arise out of inadequate control systems, deficiencies/gaps and/or likely failures in the existing control processes.. 
  -Prepare the Risk Matrix
4. The riskbased internal audit plan as prepared by the internal audit function of the bank is duly approved
by the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors of the Bank
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

In line with the proposed Operational Risk Management framework enunciated by RBI, the identification of auditable units can be taken at three different levels as follow
 -  lists the main business groups such as corporate finance, trading and sales (treasury function),retail banking, commercial banking, etc
 - lists the product teams in these business groups such as transaction banking, trade finance, general banking, cash management services, etc.
 - lists out the products offered in these business groups such as import bills, letter of credit, bank guarantee under trade finance, etc.
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Risk assessment exercise can be undertaken using the
following steps:  -
a. Inherent Business Risks - Such as Credit, Market and Operational Risk
b. Control Risk
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Qualitative and quantitative approaches for risk assessment: -
    -  Quantum of credit, market, and operational risks could largely be determined by quantitative assessment
 - the qualitative approach may be adopted for assessing the quality of controls in various business activities
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Auditing and Assurance Standard (AAS) 20,
Knowledge of the Business,should be noted
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005
Risk Matrix to be formulated & Risk appetite to be explained for each of the auditable units
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Risk-based Internal Audit Plan - detailing out the priorities, nature, timing and extent of internal audit procedures in an auditable unit with reference to the risk categorization of the auditable unit
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Scope of risk-based internal audit must be determined by each bank for low, medium, high, very high and extremely high risk areas. It must be reviewed / Report on
 -  Process by which risks are identified and managed in various areas
 - The control environment in various areas
 - Gaps, if any, in control mechanism which might lead to frauds, identification of fraud prone areas
 - Data integrity,reliability and integrity of MIS
 - Internal,regulatory and statutory compliance
 - Budgetary control and performance reviews
 - Transaction testing/verification of assets to the extent considered necessary
 - Monitoring compliance with the risk-based internal audit report
 - Variation, if any, in the assessment of risks under the audit plan vis-à-vis the risk-based internal audit
 - Review of the systems in place for ensuring compliance with money laundering controls; identifying potential inherent business risks and control risks
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Contents of Risk-based Audit Plan
 - Audit Universe
 - Priority of each auditable unit -Plan should give
importance to the magnitude and the frequency of the risks also as observed in the risk assessment exercise.
 - Type of IA assignment - Assurance and consulting
 - Frequency  - all the auditable units as decided by the management but atleast once in every 3 years
 - Extent of testing - The extent of transaction testing would be determined on the basis of risk assessment.
Illustratively, the bank should undertake 100 per cent transaction testing if an area falls in cell
“Extremely High Risk” of the risk matrix. The bank may also consider 100 per cent transaction testing if an area falls in cell “B-Very High Risk” or “F-Very High Risk”.
Resource requirements - requisite skills should be assigned the job of undertaking risk-based internal audit. Also be trained periodically to enable them to understand the bank's business activities, operating procedures,risk management and control systems, MIS, etc.
Submission of the internal audit plan - Review of audit plan by senior and final plan to be placed before the Audit Committee for approval
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Independence
 1. The internal audit head should report to the Board of Directors through Audit Committee of the Board
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Communication
Significant issues  should be promptly brought to the notice of the Audit Committee or top management
Technical guide on risk based internal audit in banks (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India) w.e.f. 27th October 2005

Performance evaluation
 - The Internal audit function should conduct periodical reviews, annually or more frequently, of the risk-based internal audit undertaken by it vis-à-vis the approved audit plan.
  - Variations, if any, in the risk profile as revealed by the risk-based internal audit vis-à-vis the risk profile as documented in the audit plan should also be looked into to evaluate the reasonableness of risk assessment methodology of the internal audit function

sheets.name: RBI noteon RBIA
header: RBI Framework on risk based internal auditing
rows: Risk Based Internal Audit framework & guidance
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Bank are required to put in place a risk based audit system a part of their internal control  framework that relies on a well defined policy for internal audit functional independence with sufficient standing and authority within the bank.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements
Banks are encouraged to adopt the International Internal Audit standards, like those issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) and the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA).
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

To bring uniformity in approach followed by the banks align with expectations on internal audit function with best practice, are as under
Authority, Stature and Independence:-
The internal audit function must have sufficient authority, stature, independence and resources within the bank to carry out assignment with objectivity.

the Head of InternalAudit (HIA) shall be a senior executive of the bank who shall have the ability to exercise 
independent judgement.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements
HIA as well as the internal audit function shall have the authority to communicate with any staff member and have access to all records and files that necessary to carry out the responibility.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Competence:-
. Requisite professional competence, knowledge and experience of each internal auditor is essential for the effectivness of the bank internal audit function.
. Banks should ensure that internal audit function has the requisite skills to audit all areas of the 
bank
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Staff Rotation:-
.  The Board should prescribe a minimum period of service for staff in the Internal Audit function.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Tenor for appointment of Head of Internal Audit:-
The HIA shall be appointed for a reasonably long period, preferably for a minimum of three years.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Reporting Line:-
The HIA shall directly report to either the Audit Committee of the Board (ACB) / MD & CEO or Whole Time Director (WTD)
. BOD decide to allow the MD/CEO/WTD to be reporting authority of the HIA. Further in such cases the ACB shall meet the HIA at least once in a quarter, without presence of the senior management inculding the MD & CEO/WTD
. HIA shall not have any reporting relationship with the business verticales of the bank & shall not given any business target.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Remuneration:-
The independence and objectivity of the internal audit function could be undermined if the remuneration of internal audit staff is linked to the financial performance of the business lines for which they exercise audit responsibilities. The remuneration policies should be structured in a way that it avoids creating conflict of interest and compromising audit’s independence and objectivity.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

The internal audit function shall not be outsourced, However, where required, experts,including former employees, could be hired on contractual basis subject to the ACB being assured that such expertise does not exist within the audit function of the bank.
Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA) Framework-Strengthening Governance arrangements

Banks must ensure and demonstrate through proper documentation that their risk-based 
internal audit framework captures all the significant criteria / principles suited for their 
organisational structure, the business model and the risks.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

Introducation:-
The evolvement of financial instruments and markets has enabled banks to undertake varied risk exposures.
This is also significant in view of proposed introduction of the New Basel Capital Accord under which capital maintained by a bank will be more closely aligned to the risks undertaken and Reserve Bank's proposed move towards risk-based supervision (RBS) of banks.
The supervisory process would seek to leverage the work done by internal auditors of banks.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The audit function should provide high quality counsel to management on the effectiveness of the following:-
Risk Management
Internal Control
regulatory compliance by the bank
However, in the changing scenario such testing by itself would not be sufficient. There is a need for widening as well as redirecting the scope of internal audit to evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of risk management procedures and internal control systems in the banks.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The functions of the Risk Management Committee/ Department (RMC/RMD) and the role of risk-based internal audit need to be distinguished
RMC/RMD focuses on areas such as 
identification
Monitoring
Measurement of Risk & Development of policies procedure , use of risk management model etc.
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

The risk-based internal audit, on the other hand, undertakes an independent risk assessment solely for the purpose of formulating the risk-based audit plan keeping in view the inherent business risks of an activity/location and the effectiveness of the control systems for monitoring the inherent risks of the business activity
Guidance note on risk-based internal audit

Policy for risk based internal audit:-
