sheets.name: Sec 2(76) - Related Party
header: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 2(76) – Definition of 'Related Party'
rows: A key managerial personnel or his relative.
A firm, in which a director, manager or his relative is a partner.
A private company in which a director or manager or his relative is a member or director.
A public company in which a director or manager is a director and holds along with his relatives, more than 2% of its paid-up share capital.
Any body corporate whose Board of Directors, managing director or manager is accustomed to act in accordance with the advice, directions or instructions of a director or manager.

Any person on whose advice, directions or instructions a director or manager is accustomed to act. [Nothing in sub-clauses (vi) and (vii) shall apply to advice, directions or instructions given in a professional capacity.]

Any body corporate which is—
(A) a holding, subsidiary or an associate company of such company;
(B) a subsidiary of a holding company to which it is also a subsidiary; or
(C) an investing company or the venturer of the company.
[Substituted by Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017, w.e.f. 09-Feb-2018]
Explanation: 'the investing company or the venturer of a company' means a body corporate whose investment in the company would result in the company becoming an associate company of the body corporate.
Such other person as may be prescribed.
Rule 3 – Companies (Specification of Definitions Details) Rules, 2014

For the purposes of sub-clause (ix) of clause (76) of section 2 of the Act, a director (other than an independent director) or key managerial personnel of the holding company or his relative with reference to a company, shall be deemed to be a related party.

sheets.name: Sec 2(77) - Relative
rows:
'Relative', with reference to any person, means any one who is related to another, if—
(i) they are members of a Hindu Undivided Family;
(ii) they are husband and wife; or
(iii) one person is related to the other in such manner as may be prescribed.
Rule 4 – Companies (Specification of Definitions Details) Rules, 2014

A person shall be deemed to be relative of another if he or she is related in the following manner:
1. Father (includes step-father)
2. Mother (includes step-mother)
3. Son (includes step-son)
4. Son's Wife
5. Daughter
6. Daughter's husband
7. Brother (includes step-brother)
8. Sister (includes step-sister)
The list under Rule 4 is exhaustive. Step-daughter is not included. On partition of HUF, members ceasing to be part of HUF are not treated as relatives unless covered under Rule 4.

sheets.name: Sec 184 - Disclosure of Interes
header: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 184 – Disclosure of Interest by Director
rows: Every director shall, at the first meeting of the Board in which he participates as director and thereafter at the first meeting of the Board in every financial year or whenever there is any change in the disclosures already made, disclose his concern or interest in any company, body corporate, firm or other association of individuals (including shareholding) in Form MBP-1.

Every director who is directly or indirectly concerned or interested in a contract or arrangement entered or proposed to be entered with:
(a) body corporate in which such director or such director in association with any other director holds more than 2% shareholding, or is a promoter/manager/CEO; or
(b) firm/entity in which director is a partner, owner or member
shall disclose the nature of his concern or interest at the Board meeting and shall not participate in such meeting.
Contract or arrangement entered into in contravention of provisions of sub-section (2) shall be voidable at the option of the company.
Penalty for contravention: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine of ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000, or both.

Nothing shall apply to any contract or arrangement entered into between two companies where any of the directors, jointly or singly, hold not more than 2% of the paid-up share capital in the other company.

sheets.name: Sec 188 - RPT
header: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 188 – Related Party Transactions
rows: Company having paid-up share capital or transactions exceeding prescribed sums (as per Rule 15) shall require prior approval of members by resolution.
No member of the company shall vote on such resolution to approve any contract or arrangement which may be entered into by the company if such member is a related party.
Nothing contained in the second proviso shall apply to a company in which 90% or more members, in number, are relatives of promoters or are related parties.
Nothing in sub-section (1) shall apply to any transactions entered into by the company in its ordinary course of business other than transactions which are not on an arm's length basis.

Requirement of resolution shall not apply to transactions entered into between a holding company and its wholly-owned subsidiary whose accounts are consolidated with such holding company and placed before the shareholders at the general meeting for approval.

Every contract or arrangement entered into under sub-section (1) shall be referred to in the Board's report to the shareholders along with the justification for entering into such contract or arrangement.

Where any contract or arrangement is entered into by a director or any other employee, without obtaining the consent of the Board or approval by resolution, and it is not ratified by the Board or by the shareholders at a meeting within 3 months, such contract or arrangement shall be voidable at the option of the Board or shareholders. The concerned director shall indemnify the company against any loss incurred by it.

Without prejudice to sub-section (3), the company may proceed against a director or any other employee who had entered into such contract or arrangement in contravention of the provisions of this section for recovery of any loss sustained by it.

Penalty for contravention:
– Listed company: Fine up to ₹25 lakh
– Any other company: Fine up to ₹5 lakh

sheets.name: Rule 15 - RPT Threshold
header: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014 – Rule 15 – Contract or Arrangement with a Related Party
rows:
Agenda of the Board meeting at which the resolution is proposed to be moved shall disclose:
(a) Name of related party and nature of relationship
(b) Nature, duration of contract, and particulars of the contract/arrangement
(c) Material terms including value
(d) Advance paid/received, if any
(e) Manner of determining pricing and commercial terms
(f) Whether all relevant factors have been considered (else rationale)
(g) Any other relevant information
Where any director is interested in any contract or arrangement with a related party, such director shall not be present at the meeting during discussions on the subject matter.

Sale, purchase or supply of any goods or materials, directly or through appointment of agent, amounting to 10% or more of the turnover of the company [Rs.100 crore monetary cap omitted by MCA Notification dated 18-Nov-2019].
Selling or otherwise disposing of, or buying, property of any kind, directly or through appointment of agent, amounting to 10% or more of the net worth of the company.
Leasing of property of any kind amounting to 10% or more of turnover of the company.
Availing or rendering of services, directly or through appointment of agent, amounting to 10% or more of turnover of the company.
Appointment to any office or place of profit in the company, its subsidiary or associate, at a monthly remuneration exceeding Rs. 2,50,000.
Remuneration for underwriting the subscription of any securities or derivatives thereof of the company exceeding 1% of net worth.
Limits of turnover/net worth shall be computed on the basis of the audited financial statement of the preceding financial year.

Requirements do not apply to transactions in the ordinary course of business at arm's length, or between a holding company and its wholly-owned subsidiary whose accounts are consolidated with the holding company.

sheets.name: Sec 189 - MBP-4 Register
header: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 189 – Register of Contracts / Arrangements in which Directors are Interested (MBP-4)
rows: Every company shall maintain one or more registers in Form MBP-4 giving separately the particulars of all contracts or arrangements to which sub-section (2) of section 184 or section 188 applies.
The register(s) shall be placed before the next meeting of the Board and signed by all the directors present at the meeting.
Register shall be kept at the registered office of the company and shall be preserved permanently and kept in the custody of the company secretary or any other person authorised by the Board.
The register shall be open for inspection at the registered office during business hours and extracts may be taken by any member.
The register shall also be produced at the commencement of every AGM and shall remain open and accessible during the continuance of the meeting to any person having the right to attend.

Every director or key managerial personnel shall, within a period of 30 days of his appointment (or relinquishment) disclose to the company the particulars specified in sub-section (1) as may be relevant.

The register need not include:
(a) transactions of sale/purchase between the company and any related party where the value does not exceed ₹5 lakh in aggregate in any FY; and
(b) contracts by a banking company for the collection of bills in the ordinary course of business.

sheets.name: SEBI LODR Reg 2(1)(zb)-(zc)
rows:
'Related party' means:
(a) A related party as defined under sub-section (76) of section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013; OR
(b) A related party as defined under the applicable accounting standards.

Additional inclusions:
(i) Any person or entity forming part of the promoter or promoter group of the listed entity; OR
(ii) Any person or entity holding equity shares of 20% or more (with effect from 01-Apr-2023: 10% or more) in the listed entity, either directly or on a beneficial interest basis at any time during the immediately preceding financial year.

'Related party transaction' means a transaction involving a transfer of resources, services or obligations between:
(i) A listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on one hand; AND
(ii) A related party of the listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on the other hand;
regardless of whether a price is charged.

A 'transaction' shall be construed to include a single transaction or a group of transactions in a contract.
Proviso (First) – Exclusions [As amended by SEBI LODR Fifth Amendment 2025]

Retail purchase exemption now expressly covers Directors and KMPs of the listed entity as well as its subsidiary, and relatives of such Directors/KMPs — bringing greater clarity and reducing routine compliance burden for retail-oriented listed entities.

sheets.name: SEBI LODR Reg 23 - RPT
header: SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 – Regulation 23 – Related Party Transactions (as updated by Fifth Amendment 2025)
rows: Listed entity shall formulate a policy on materiality of RPTs and dealing with RPTs (including omnibus approval clear criteria) — approved by Board (on Audit Committee recommendation) and reviewed at least once every 3 years. Materiality is determined as per Schedule XII (introduced by Fifth Amendment 2025, effective 18-Dec-2025).

Payment for brand usage or royalty to related parties exceeding 5% of the annual consolidated turnover of the listed entity as per the last audited financial statements shall be treated as material and require prior shareholder approval.

All RPTs and subsequent material modifications shall require prior approval of the Audit Committee (only independent directors shall approve). Applies to listed entity and its subsidiaries.

For RPTs where a subsidiary of the listed entity is a party but the listed entity is not:
– Audit Committee approval of the listed entity required if transaction value exceeds lower of:
  (i) 10% of the subsidiary's standalone annual turnover; OR
  (ii) The Schedule XII materiality threshold of the listed entity.
– Additionally, any such subsidiary RPT exceeding ₹1 crore requires prior approval of the Audit Committee of the listed entity (Fifth Amendment 2025).

Audit Committee may grant omnibus approval subject to criteria — name of RP, nature of transaction, period, maximum value, indicative base price, formula for pricing variation, etc.
– Valid for maximum 1 year (fresh approval required thereafter).
– Quarterly review by Audit Committee is mandatory.
– Omnibus approval may also cover subsidiary-level RPTs (Fifth Amendment 2025).

All material RPTs (as per Schedule XII) and material modifications require prior shareholder approval by resolution. No related party shall vote on such resolution, whether the entity is a party to the transaction or not.
Provisions of this regulation are applicable to all prospective transactions.
The provisions apply from the financial year beginning on or after 01-Apr-2019, subject to phased implementation.

Ratification and Post-facto approval:
– Post-facto approval may be granted by Audit Committee/ratification obtained within 3 months for transactions not exceeding ₹1 crore.
– Otherwise, transaction becomes voidable at the option of the Audit Committee.
– Ratification framework tightened by Fifth Amendment 2025.

Listed entity shall submit disclosures of RPTs in the format specified by SEBI to stock exchanges within 30 days from the date of publication of standalone/consolidated financial results for the half-year, and simultaneously publish on its website.

sheets.name: Schedule XII - Materiality
header: SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 – Schedule XII – Materiality of Related Party Transactions
rows: 10% of the annual consolidated turnover of the listed entity.
Above ₹20,000 Crore and up to ₹40,000 Crore
₹2,000 Crore PLUS 5% of the annual consolidated turnover of the listed entity exceeding ₹20,000 Crore.
₹3,000 Crore PLUS 2.5% of the annual consolidated turnover of the listed entity exceeding ₹40,000 Crore; OR ₹5,000 Crore — whichever is LOWER.
Introduced by SEBI (LODR) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations, 2025 notified on 18-Nov-2025. Provisions relating to Schedule XII come into force on the 30th day from publication (i.e., 18-Dec-2025).

Annual consolidated turnover to be considered as per the last audited financial statements of the listed entity. Applicable for FY 2025-26 (for transactions after effective date) and FY 2026-27 onwards.
Separate materiality threshold — 5% of annual consolidated turnover — retained under Regulation 23(1A).

The graded turnover-linked framework replaces the earlier flat threshold of 'lower of ₹1,000 Crore or 10% of turnover'. It reduces disproportionate compliance burden for large-cap entities while preserving investor protection via an overall cap of ₹5,000 Crore.

sheets.name: Industry Standards 26-Jun-2025
header: SEBI Industry Standards on Minimum Information for RPT Approval – Circular dated 26-Jun-2025
rows: SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated 26-Jun-2025 on 'Industry Standards on Minimum Information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transactions'.
Applicable to all listed entities effective 01-Sep-2025 and continuing for FY 2025-26 and 2026-27 onwards.
To standardise the minimum information placed before the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of RPTs, and to enhance transparency and quality of disclosures.

Applicable to ALL RPTs. Minimum details:
– Name of related party and nature of relationship
– Type, material terms and monetary value of transaction
– Tenure of the proposed transaction
– Previous transaction history with the same related party
– Percentage of listed entity's annual consolidated turnover represented by the transaction
– Interest of promoter, director, KMP, or their relatives
– Justification/business rationale for the transaction
– Details of contract/arrangement (draft agreement or key terms)

Additional disclosures for 7 specific transaction types:
(1) Sale/purchase/supply of goods, services, works, trade advances
(2) Sale/purchase/lease of property (movable or immovable)
(3) Availing or rendering of services
(4) Loans, inter-corporate deposits, advances or investments
(5) Guarantees, sureties, indemnities, collateral, security
(6) Issuance of securities on preferential/private placement basis
(7) Any other transactions not covered above
Part C – Additional Disclosures for Material RPTs

For material RPTs requiring shareholder approval:
– Auditor certification
– Independent valuation reports (where applicable)
– Comparison with arm's length benchmarks / third-party pricing
– Any independent professional opinion obtained
– Impact on the listed entity's financial position
Notice to shareholders for approval of material RPTs must contain a summary of Parts A, B and C, along with the Audit Committee's justification and recommendation.
Listed entities must update their RPT SOPs, Audit Committee agenda formats, and shareholder notices to align with the standardised framework.

sheets.name: Ind AS 24 - RP Disclosures
rows: To ensure that an entity's financial statements contain the disclosures necessary to draw attention to the possibility that its financial position and profit or loss may have been affected by the existence of related parties and by transactions and outstanding balances (including commitments) with such parties.

A person or a close member of that person's family is related to a reporting entity if that person:
(i) has control or joint control of the reporting entity;
(ii) has significant influence over the reporting entity; or
(iii) is a member of the key management personnel of the reporting entity or of a parent of the reporting entity.
Include children, spouse or domestic partner, children of spouse/domestic partner, and dependants of the entity or spouse/domestic partner.
Regardless of whether there have been transactions, an entity shall disclose the name of its parent and, if different, the ultimate controlling party.

Total KMP compensation to be disclosed in aggregate and for each of the following categories:
(a) Short-term employee benefits
(b) Post-employment benefits
(c) Other long-term benefits
(d) Termination benefits
(e) Share-based payments

If related party transactions occurred, entity to disclose nature of relationship and information about the transactions and outstanding balances (including commitments):
(i) Amount of transactions
(ii) Outstanding balances and commitments (terms, security, settlement)
(iii) Provisions for doubtful debts related to outstanding balances
(iv) Expense recognised in the period for bad/doubtful debts due from related parties

Disclosures shall be made separately for each of the following categories:
(a) Parent
(b) Entities with joint control or significant influence over the entity
(c) Subsidiaries
(d) Associates
(e) Joint ventures in which the entity is a venturer
(f) Key management personnel of the entity or its parent
(g) Other related parties

A reporting entity is exempt from certain disclosures in relation to related party transactions and balances with:
(i) a government that has control, joint control or significant influence over the entity; and
(ii) another entity that is a related party because the same government has control, joint control or significant influence over both entities.
However, sufficient information must still be provided to enable users to understand the effect of such transactions.

sheets.name: AS 18 - RP Disclosures
header: AS 18 – Related Party Disclosures (applicable to non-Ind AS reporting entities)
rows:
To establish requirements for disclosure of:
(a) related party relationships; and
(b) transactions between a reporting enterprise and its related parties.

Applies to reporting of related party relationships and transactions between a reporting enterprise and its related parties. Does not apply in circumstances where such reporting would conflict with the reporting enterprise's duties of confidentiality specifically arising out of any statute or by virtue of any regulator.

Parties are considered to be related if at any time during the reporting period one party has the ability to control the other party or exercise significant influence over the other party in making financial and/or operating decisions.

'Control' means:
(a) Ownership, directly or indirectly, of more than one half of the voting power of an enterprise; OR
(b) Control of the composition of the board of directors in the case of a company or of the composition of the corresponding governing body in case of any other enterprise; OR
(c) A substantial interest in voting power AND the power to direct, by statute or agreement, the financial and/or operating policies of the enterprise.

Participation in the financial and/or operating policy decisions of an enterprise, but not control of those policies. May be gained by share ownership, statute or agreement.

Shareholding threshold: If an investor holds, directly or indirectly through subsidiaries, 20% or more of the voting power of the investee, it is presumed that the investor has significant influence, unless it can be clearly demonstrated otherwise.

In relation to an individual, means the spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father and mother who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, that individual in his/her dealings with the reporting enterprise.
Those persons who have the authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the reporting enterprise.

Name of the related party and nature of the related party relationship where control exists should be disclosed irrespective of whether or not there have been transactions between the related parties.

Items of a similar nature may be disclosed in aggregate by type of related party. However, aggregation is not permitted if separate disclosure is necessary for an understanding of the effects of related party transactions on the financial statements of the reporting enterprise.
AS 18 vs Ind AS 24 – Key Differences

– AS 18 does not require disclosure of KMP compensation break-up in the detail required under Ind AS 24 (short-term, post-employment, other long-term, termination, share-based payments).
– Ind AS 24 covers post-employment benefit plans as related parties; AS 18 does not.
– Ind AS 24 treats two joint ventures of the same third party as related parties; AS 18 does not.
– Ind AS 24 provides government-related entity exemption; AS 18 does not.
– Ind AS 24 uses the concept of 'close family members'; AS 18 uses 'relatives' (narrower definition — only spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, mother).
– AS 18 exempts state-controlled enterprises from disclosing transactions with other state-controlled enterprises; Ind AS 24 provides a partial exemption for government-related entities requiring qualitative disclosures.

AS 18 continues to apply to enterprises to which the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021 are applicable (i.e., companies not required to comply with Ind AS as per the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015). Ind AS 24 applies to Ind AS reporting entities.

sheets.name: IRDAI - RPT Regulations
header: IRDAI Regulations on Related Party & Related Party Transactions (for Insurance Companies)
rows: Notified on 20-Mar-2024 (F. No. IRDAI/Reg/7/201/2024). Establishes framework for governance of insurers including Board composition, committees, KMPs, conflict of interest and related party transactions. Effective from date of notification. Repeals earlier IRDAI Corporate Governance Guidelines, 2016.
Applicable to all Indian insurers registered under Insurance Act, 1938. Not applicable to foreign reinsurance branches operating in India.
IRDAI Master Circular on Corporate Governance for Insurers, 2024
Ref: IRDAI/F&I/CIR/MISC/82/5/2024 dated 22-May-2024. Provides operational and procedural aspects for adoption by all insurers. Insurers were given time up to 30-Jun-2024 to ensure compliance.

Every insurer shall formulate a Board-approved Policy on Related Party Transactions covering:
– Definition of transactions in the ordinary course of insurance business
– Method of determining arm's length pricing
– List of items requiring approvals under applicable laws and/or from Audit Committee, Board and Shareholders
– Any other relevant matter related to RPT
Policy to be reviewed at least once every 3 years.
Definition of 'Related Party' under IRDAI framework

Related party for insurer includes:
(a) Related party as defined under Section 2(76) of the Companies Act, 2013 and rules thereunder
(b) Related party as defined under applicable accounting standards (Ind AS 24 / AS 18)
(c) Any promoter or promoter group entity of the insurer
(d) Any entity holding 10% or more equity (for listed insurers, as per SEBI LODR)
(e) Key Management Persons (KMPs) as defined by IRDAI

Includes members of the core management team of an insurer including:
– All Whole-time Directors / Managing Director / Chief Executive Officer
– Functional heads one level below MD/CEO including:
   • Chief Financial Officer
   • Appointed Actuary
   • Chief Investment Officer
   • Chief Risk Officer
   • Chief Compliance Officer
   • Company Secretary

As per Corporate Governance Regulations 2024:
– Audit Committee shall be chaired by an Independent Director
– Minimum 3 members, majority being Independent Directors
– All members shall be non-executive directors

Responsibilities include:
– Review of RPTs and prior approval for all RPTs of the insurer
– Grant of omnibus approval for repetitive transactions
– Quarterly review of RPTs entered into
– Reviewing the RPT Policy periodically
– Recommending policy to Board

(a) Audit Committee approval — Required for ALL RPTs
(b) Board approval — Required under Section 188 of Companies Act, 2013
(c) Shareholder approval — Required for material RPTs exceeding thresholds under Section 188 read with Rule 15
(d) Omnibus approval — Permitted for repetitive transactions, valid for 1 year and subject to quarterly review
Arm's Length Pricing and Ordinary Course of Business

– Insurer shall document methodology for determining arm's length price
– Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP), Cost Plus, or other transfer pricing methods may be adopted
– Ordinary course of insurance business includes: reinsurance arrangements, premium collection, claim settlement, investment transactions, agent/broker commissions in accordance with regulatory approved rates, outsourcing of activities in line with IRDAI Outsourcing Regulations.

Insurers to disclose:
– Related party transactions in Notes to Accounts as per applicable accounting standards (AS 18 / Ind AS 24)
– Related party transactions in the Annual Report
– Details of transactions with promoters, KMPs and their relatives
– Quarterly reporting to Audit Committee
– Reporting in Public Disclosure formats (L-42 formats prescribed by IRDAI)
– Corporate Governance Report as part of Annual Return
IRDAI (Registration, Capital Structure, Transfer of Shares and Amalgamation of Insurers) Regulations, 2024

Notified on 20-Mar-2024. Consolidated framework for registration and capital structure. Key related party aspects:
– Provisions on transfer of shares to related parties/promoters require IRDAI approval
– Lock-in period on promoter shareholding
– Shareholders exceeding 10% can nominate directors only in one insurance company in same line of business
– Reporting requirement: Changes in shareholding exceeding 5% to be reported immediately; between 1% and 5% quarterly.
IRDAI Guidelines on Conflict of Interest and Common Directorship (Ref: IRDAI/INT/GDL/MISC/202/9/2022 dated 28-Sep-2022)

Applicable to intermediaries/insurance intermediaries in same group:
– Maximum directorships as per Section 165 of Companies Act, 2013
– Board-approved policy on RPT with related parties as per Section 2(76)
– All RPTs shall comply with Section 188 of Companies Act and AS 18
– Statutory Auditor to certify compliance with Section 188 to IRDAI by 30-Sep of subsequent FY
– Communication to IRDAI on appointment of common director within 30 days
– Compliance with Section 184 by common directors
– No common director shall hold position of KMP/CEO/Principal Officer/Whole-time Director in another intermediary (Non-Executive Director position permitted)
IRDAI (Outsourcing of Activities by Indian Insurers) Regulations, 2017

Outsourcing to related parties/group entities requires:
– Board-approved outsourcing policy
– Prior Audit Committee approval
– Arm's length pricing
– Ongoing monitoring
– Written outsourcing agreement
– Reporting of outsourcing arrangements to IRDAI
Investment in Related Parties (IRDAI Investment Regulations, 2016)

– Investments by insurers in promoter/promoter group entities restricted
– Group exposure limits prescribed under IRDAI Investment Regulations
– 'Group' defined under Section 2(g) of IRDAI Investment Regulations
– Investment in shares/debentures of related parties requires specific Board approval and disclosure
– Adherence to prudential exposure norms

– Reinsurance ceded to related parties (e.g., group reinsurance companies) require careful assessment
– Compliance with IRDAI Reinsurance Regulations, 2018
– Priority to Indian reinsurers as per Order of Preference
– Board-approved Reinsurance Programme
– Documentation of arm's length pricing

As per CG Regulations 2024:
– Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) is responsible for continuous compliance monitoring
– Annual compliance report to be submitted to IRDAI
– Reporting of any non-compliance in RPT approvals
– Minimum tenure of CCO: 3 years

– Joint Statutory Auditors (minimum 2) mandated for insurers
– Statutory Auditors to certify RPT disclosures
– Auditor's report to comment on adequacy of RPT identification and disclosure processes
– Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) to include RPT observations

IRDAI Master Circular on Public Disclosures:
– Segment reporting including RPT
– Related party disclosures in financial statements as per AS 18 / Ind AS 24
– Web-based disclosures on insurer's website
– L-42 formats prescribed for RPT disclosures

– Board approval of RPT Policy: To be reviewed at least once every 3 years
– Audit Committee review of RPTs: Quarterly
– Public disclosures: As per applicable timelines under Master Circular
– Statutory Auditor certification (common directorship compliance): By 30-Sep of subsequent FY
– Communication to IRDAI on new common director: Within 30 days

– Non-compliance with CG Regulations may attract IRDAI regulatory action
– Voidable contracts under Section 188 of Companies Act
– Directors/KMPs personally liable for unapproved RPTs
– Impact on insurer's Certificate of Registration (CoR) status

sheets.name: BG
rows: Check whether the customer request letter/application along with the date and time stamp is available

Check whether following details match as per CRL in the BG 
- Applicant
- Beneficiary 
- Expiry date and claim date (same is as per credit facility) 
- Amount 
- Purpose
- Debit Account Number
- Issuance should be within 5 Days
- FEMA Declaration (if applicable)
Check whether transaction are approved as per the approval grid mentioned in LOP

Check whether guarantee issued for more than Rs. 50,000 is signed by two officials jointly . In exceptional circumstances, If signed by one official then system should be in place and more scrutiny from Auditors.
Check that BG is not for more than 10 years. If yes, then check whether Trade Ops Head approval is in place for this Guarantee. Check for the Board Approved Policy.
Check whether limits are blocked as per the guarantee amount
Check that no exceptions noted in Nature of Goods/Purpose/Name of the Counter Parties of the Guarantee and the same is to be clearly stated in the text of the guarantee
Check whether bank guarantees has been issued in serially numbered security forms
Check whether claim clause and mode of raising claim is clear and specified with specified claim date beyond which the claim will not be valid

BG /LC may be issued by scheduled commercial banks to clients of co-operative banks against counter guarantee of the co-operative bank. In such cases, banks may be guided by the provisions of paragraph 2.3.9.2 of the Master Circular on Loans and Advances-Statutory and Other Restrictions dated July 1, 2014. Further, banks must satisfy themselves that the concerned co-operative banks have sound credit appraisal and monitoring systems as well as robust Know Your Customer (KYC) regime. Before issuing BG/LCs to specific constituents of co-operative banks, they must satisfy themselves that KYC has been done properly in these cases.

Banks may issue guarantees favouring other banks/ FIs/ other lending agencies for the loans extended by the latter, subject to strict compliance with the following conditions.
(i) The Board of Directors should reckon the integrity/ robustness of the bank?s risk management systems and, accordingly, put in place a well-laid out policy in this regard.
(ii) The guarantee shall be extended only in respect of borrower constituents and to enable them to avail of additional credit facility from other banks/FIs/lending agencies.
(iii) The guaranteeing bank should assume a funded exposure of at least 10% of the exposure guaranteed.
(iv) Banks should not extend guarantees or letters of comfort in favour of overseas lenders including those assignable to overseas lenders. However, AD banks may also be guided by the provisions contained in Notification No. FEMA 8/2000-RB dated May 3, 2000.
(v) The guarantee issued by the bank will be an exposure on the borrowing entity on whose behalf the guarantee has been issued and will attract appropriate risk weight, as per the extant guidelines.
(vi) Banks should ensure compliance with the recommendations of the Ghosh Committee and other internal requirements relating to issue of guarantees, to obviate the possibility of frauds in this area.

No person resident in India shall, except in accordance with Foreign Exchange Management (Guarantees) Regulations, 2026 or with approval of RBI, be a party (principal debtor, surety or a creditor) to a guarantee where any of the other parties to the guarantee is a person resident outside India

Eligible to act as a surety or a principal debtor - (a) - Check the transaction for which the guarantee is being given or arranged is not
prohibited. (b) - the surety and the principal debtor are eligible to lend to and borrow from each other, respectively, under the Foreign Exchange Management (Borrowing and Lending) Regulations, 2018 
 Exemption - (i). guarantee given by an authorised dealer bank and covered by a counter-guarantee or issued against 100% collateral in the form of a deposit, from a person resident outside India or (ii) given by an agent in India of a shipping or airline company incorporated outside India on behalf of such company in connection with its obligation or liability owed to any statutory or Government authority in India or (iii) where both the surety and the principal debtor are persons resident in India.

Eligible to obtain a guarantee as a creditor - A person resident in India being a creditor may arrange or obtain a guarantee in its favour, subject to the condition that where the principal debtor and surety both are persons resident outside India, the creditor shall ensure that the underlying transaction is not prohibited under the Act, or rules or regulations or directions issued under the Act.

Reporting:- Eligible person should submit Form GRN Issue, Form GRN Modification and ‘Form GRN Invocation to AD Bank on a quarterly basis within fifteen calendar days from the end of the respective quarter.

Further, AD Bank Should submit to RBI in Form GRN Issue, ‘Form GRN Modification, Form GRN Invocation within thirty calendar days from the end of the respective quarter
AD Bank shall provide a unique Guarantee Transaction Number for gurantees reported through ‘Form GRN Issue, before submission to RBI

Late Fees - In case of delayed reporting of ‘Form GRN Invocation’, the amount will be liability created towards the surety on invocation and in case of Delayed reporting of ‘Form GRN Issue’ and ‘Form GRN Modication - Nil charges

rows: Check that the good are not entered into Indian teritory, If goods enter India, separate import/export formalities apply. Check that the port of destination in transport document is not an Indian port
AD bank being satisfied with the documentary evidence and bonafides of the transaction.

The MTT shall be undertaken for the goods that are permitted for exports / imports under the prevailing Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) of India as on the date of shipment. All rules, regulations and directions applicable to exports (except Export Declaration Form) and imports (except Bill of Entry) shall be complied with for the export leg and import leg respectively
The entire merchanting trade is to be routed through the same AD bank.

The AD bank shall verify the documents like invoice, packing list, transport documents and insurance documents (if originals are not available, Nonnegotiable copies duly authenticated by the bank handling documents may be taken) and satisfy itself about the genuineness of the trade

The entire MTT shall be completed within an overall period of nine months and there shall not be any outlay of foreign exchange beyond six months. The commencement date of merchanting trade shall be the date of shipment / export leg receipt or import leg payment, whichever is first. The completion date shall be the date of shipment / export leg receipt or import leg payment, whichever is the last

Short-term credit either by way of suppliers' credit or buyers' credit may be extended for MTT to the extent not backed by advance remittance for the export leg, including the discounting of export leg LC by the AD bank, as in the case of import transactions. However, Letter of Undertaking (LoU)/ Letter of Comfort (LoC) shall not be issued for supplier’s/ buyer’s credit.

Any receipts for the export leg, prior to the payment for import leg, may be parked either in Exchange Earners Foreign Currency (EEFC) account or in an interest-bearing INR account till the import leg liability arises.
It shall be strictly earmarked/ lien-marked for the payment of import leg and the liability of the import leg,

Merchanting traders may be allowed to make advance payment for the import leg on demand made by the overseas supplier. In case where inward remittance from the overseas buyer is not received before the outward remittance to the overseas supplier, AD bank may handle such transactions based on its commercial judgement. It may, however, be ensured that any such advance payment for an import leg beyond USD 500,000/- per transaction, shall be made against Bank Guarantee / an unconditional, irrevocable standby Letter of Credit from an international bank of repute.

Letter of Credit to the supplier for the import leg is permitted against confirmed export order, keeping in view the foreign exchange outlay of six months and completion of the MTT within nine months and subject to compliance with the instructions issued by Department of Banking Regulation on “Guarantees and Co-acceptances”, as amended from time to time.

AD bank shall ensure one-to-one matching in case of each MTT and report defaults in any leg by the traders to the concerned Regional Office of the Reserve Bank, on half yearly basis in the format as annexed, within 15 days from the close of each half year, i.e. June and December;
Merchant traders with outstanding of 5% or more of their annual export earnings shall be liable for caution listing.
Third party payment for export and import leg not allowed.

Agency commission is not allowed in MTTs. However, AD banks may allow payment of agency commission up to a reasonable extent by way of outward remittance under exceptional circumstances, subject to the following conditions:
MTT has been completed in all respects.
The payment of agency commission shall not result in the MTT ending into a loss.
The Merchanting trader shall make a specific request to the AD bank in this regard.

The Export Leg should always fetch more sum in value than the Import leg.

Minimum Average Maturity Period (MAMP) for ECB will be 3 years. Call and put options, if any, shall not be exercisable prior to completion of minimum average maturity. An eligible borrower shall raise ECB with minimum average maturity period (MAMP) of three years. An eligible borrower engaged in manufacturing sector may also raise ECB with average maturity period between one year and three years, subject to the condition that outstanding amount of such ECBs shall not exceed USD 150 million.

For the categories mentioned at (b) to (e) above –
(i) ECB cannot be raised from foreign branches / subsidiaries of Indian banks
(ii) the prescribed MAMP will have to be strictly complied with under all circumstances.

ECB -Limit and Leverage:
An eligible borrower may raise ECB up to the higher of (a) outstanding ECB up to USD 1 billion; or (b) total outstanding borrowing (external and domestic) up to 300 per cent of net worth as per the last audited standalone balance sheet of the borrower.  Further, in case of FCY denominated ECB raised from direct foreign equity holder, ECB liability-equity ratio for ECB raised under the automatic route cannot exceed 7:1. However, this ratio will not be applicable if the outstanding amount of all ECB, including the proposed one, is up to USD 5 million or its equivalent. Further, the borrowing entities will also be governed by the guidelines on debt equity ratio, issued, if any, by the sectoral or prudential regulator concerned.

In case of eligible ECBs with average maturity period of less than three years, the cost of borrowing shall be in
compliance with cost ceiling specified for Trade Credit under these regulations. In the case of fixed rate loans, the floating
rate plus spread of the corresponding swap shall not be more than the ceiling

The borrowing entity shall inform about pendency of such investigation / adjudication / appeal to the AD Cat-I bank / RBI as the case may be. Accordingly, in case of all applications where the borrowing entity has indicated about the pending investigations / adjudications / appeals, the AD Cat I Banks / Reserve Bank while approving the proposal shall intimate the agencies concerned by endorsing a copy of the approval letter.

Issuance of Rupee denominated bonds overseas:
1) With fixing of aggregate limit of foreign investment in corporate debt in Rupee terms, the provision at Sr. No. 7 of the table in the Annex to the aforesaid circular dated September 29, 2015 regarding the amount of borrowing by issuance of Rupee denominated bonds overseas has also been modified. As the overall limit is now prescribed in Rupee terms, the maximum amount which can be borrowed by an entity in a financial year under the automatic route by issuance of these bonds will be Rs.50 billion. Proposals to borrow beyond Rs. 50 billion in a financial year will require prior approval of the Reserve Bank.
2) The minimum maturity period for Rupee denominated bonds issued overseas is three years.

ECB by entities under restructuring/ ECB facility for refinancing stressed assets:
An entity which is under a restructuring scheme/ corporate insolvency resolution process can raise ECB only if specifically permitted under the resolution plan.

Eligible corporate borrowers who have availed Rupee loans domestically for capital expenditure in manufacturing and infrastructure sector and which have been classified as SMA-2 or NPA can avail ECB for repayment of these loans under any one time settlement with lenders. Lender banks are also permitted to sell, through assignment, such loans to eligible ECB lenders, provided, the resultant external commercial borrowing complies with all-in-cost, minimum average maturity period and other relevant norms of the ECB framework. Foreign branches/ overseas subsidiaries of Indian banks are not eligible to lend for the above purposes. The applicable MAMP will have to be strictly complied with under all circumstances.

Eligible borrowers under the ECB framework, who are participating in the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 as resolution applicants, can raise ECB from all recognised lenders, except foreign branches/subsidiaries of Indian banks, for repayment of Rupee term loans of the target company. Such ECB will be considered under the approval route, procedure of which is given at paragraph No. 5 of Master Direction.

Issuance of any type of guarantee by Indian banks, All India Financial Institutions and NBFCs relating to ECB is not permitted. Further, financial intermediaries (viz., Indian banks, All India Financial Institutions, or NBFCs) shall not invest in FCCBs/ FCEBs in any manner whatsoever.

sheets.name: Letter of Credit
rows: Check that the guidelines regarding settlement in the currency not having direct exchange rate is followed

Banks should not extend any non-fund based facilities or additional/ad-hoc credit facilities to parties who are not their regular constituents, nor should they discount bills drawn under LCs, or otherwise, for beneficiaries who are not their regular clients. In the case of LCs for import of goods, banks should be very vigilant while making payment to the overseas suppliers on the basis of shipping documents. They should exercise precaution and care in comparing the clients. The payments should be released to the foreign parties only after ensuing that the documents are strictly in conformity with the terms of the LCs. There have been many irregularities in the conduct of LC business, such as the LC transactions not being recorded in the books of the branch by officials issuing them, the amount of LCs being much in excess of the powers vested in the officials, fraudulent issue of LCs involving a conspiracy/collusion between the beneficiary and the constituent. In such cases, the banks should take action against the concerned officials as well as the constituent on whose behalf the LCs were opened and the beneficiary of LCs, if a criminal conspiracy is involved.
Check that the followup letters are being sent to the customer as per the process for pending submission of the bill of entry
Check that there are no overdue bills under LC. Otherwise, the bills are immediately devolved or settled.
Check whether ACU reimburse clause has been included for ACU transactions

Check if LC is expired once documents are arrived at the counter of Issuing Bank.
If yes, it should be mentioned as discrepancy in MT734
Check if documents are received from nominated bank mentioned in field 41A of MT700
Check whether vessel checks are done as per Vessel Checking procedures.

Check that there are no import bills which are clean and not yet marked as 'accepted' in the TI plus system. Check that the customer's acceptance is obtained and necessary followup is done for the pending acceptance from the customer. Check that the acceptance SWIFT message is sent to the overseas bank in case of clean import bills.

To check that the charges and commission including GST is collected from the customer's account as per the standard pricing or as per the special pricing. Check whether the special pricing approval is on record as per the approval matrix
Check that the approval as per the exception matrix is obtained in case there are overdue Bill of Entry submission by the customer.

Check that the SWIFT MT MT202 is transmitted for the payment as per the covering schedule instructions. Check that the dbit authority is provided to the Reimbursing Bank in case of reimbursing bank is nominated in the LC and the payment is credited to the Nostro account as per the reimbursing bank. Check for Import Licence ( If applicable )is debited for the LC value.

Check that the Bill of Entry (for non EDI port) or details of the bill of entry (for EDI ports) is provided and the details on the Bill of entry is matching with the invoice and transport documents. Check that bill of entry is updated and settled in the IDPMS against the ORM. Check that the bill of entry mentions the name of the third party if applicable.
Check that the original bill of exchange is accepted and duly signed by the authorised signatory.

Check that the customer's request letter for acceptance or payment of the bill is as per the format and mentions correct details:

(Currency, Value, & Beneficiary Details)

(Not Applicable if Evidance is submitted)

Check that the discrepancies if any are mentioned in the intimation sent to the customer. Check that the discrepancies are informed to the overseas bank by MT734 message within 5 days from the receipt of documents.
Check that the LC terms and conditions are followed and the documents under the bill are complied as per the LC terms and ISBP.

Check that the Transport Document shows correct details as per the LC terms:
(i) Description of the Goods
(ii) Gross weight or Quantity (Always more than the Invoice Value)
(iii) Shipment date

Check the invoice mentions the correct details as  per the LC:
(i) Details of the Transaction
(Currency, Value, Beneficiary Details)
(ii) Location of the Beneficiary i.e. Port of Loading
(iii) Description of the Goods

Check that the Bill of Exchange contains correct details:
(if Applicable)
(i) Drawn on the Importer
(ii) Currency & Value Details
(iii) Availization or Co-acceptance should not be mentioned
(iii) Drawn to the Order of KMBL Limited
Check that the ACU mechanism for payment is followed for the bills involving the SAARC countries except Nepal and Bhutan.

(i) List of Documents mentioned should be attached
(ii) Dated

(iv) If ACU Country the payment should be made to ACU Mechanism
To check whether the BG is issued for beneficiaries or applicant belonging to the restricted countries declared by OFAC - Check live for updated list.
Check that the parties, places, countries, banks are screened in the watchlist through NCIF. Check that proper approvals are in place in case of positive match found.

To check that the devolvement process is followed. Check the devolvement loan account is created for correct amount, correct interest rate, limit blocking etc. Also check whether the customer's current account or CC account has been lien marked for the devolvement loan amount.

LC with tenor above 180 days should be reported as Trade Credit (Supplier's Credit). Also check whether the total trade credit including the usance period of LC exceeds 1 year for non-capital goods (which is the maximum permitted period)

Check that the cancellation of the LC before the expiry date is done after receipt of consent from the Beneficiary by authenticated SWIFT message. In all other cases, check that the LC is cancelled only post expiry date and the underlying bills were paid.

Check that the correct commission and charges including GST are collected from the customer for the LC amendment. Check that the commission is collected for extension in the Expiry date, Extension in the shipment date, extension in the tenor and increase in the LC amount etc.

Check that the LC amendment which are material to the beneficiary are not updated in the LC transaction without beneficiary's consent. E.g. reduction in the shipment date, expiry, tenor, goods quantity and LC amount.

Check that the prepayment of the bill under LC is done in adherence to the guidelines. Check that the amount has been reduced in proportion to the lapsed usance period in line with the SOFR interest rate.
Check that the status report (D&B) is obtained on the supplier in case of LC value is above USD 10,00,000 or equivalent. Check that the stauts report is satisfactory

Check that the approval/exception matrix is followed for cases such as:
Charter Bill is acceptable
OR
Insurance Policy Short in Tenor or Value
OR
HOD approval for NCIF Approved country

Check that the details in the SWIFT message sent to the beneficiary bank is accurate as per the customer request. Further check that the clauses mentioned in the LC are in line with the UCP600 and/or URR725. Further, check that the type of LC such as revolving or transferable LC etc. are as per the customer request letter. Check that the SWIFT message MT700 or MT707 was transmitted successfully to the advising bank.

Check that the import of goods by the government organization or institutions with the incoterms other than Exworks & FOB basis, requires Ministy of Surface Transports approval. Check for any other approval is necessary particulay for Gold LCs tenor should not be more than 90 days.

Check that the valid insurance policy is provided if the incoterms is below CIF, e.g. EXWorks, CFR etc. Verify the following details in the Insurance policy: (i) Name of the Applicant & Assigned to KMBL
(ii) Amount should be atleast 110%
(iii) Goods covered in Letter of Credit

Check that the import of goods under the restricted category is supported with the valid import license and check that the license is not expired and the amount is sufficient and endorsed on the original import license.

Check that the underlying invoice/purchase order/contract note is provided and the details are accurate:
(i) Value & Amount (Can be greater than LC)
(ii) Description of Goods
(iii) ITS HS Code

Check that the LC application form as per the process note and verify the following details:
(i) Stamping of LC Application or MFA Agreement
(ii) LC Application should be Signed  on all pages
(iii) Description of Goods matches with the PO Attached
(iv) Shipment date is prior to expiry date

Check that the customer request letter as per the process is provided and the details are accurate such as:
(i) Currency & Amount
(ii) Request should not be more than 5 day old
(iii) Debit Authority to Account Number
(iv) Customer Signature Verification
(v) FEMA Declaration
(Foreign Letter of Credit)
(vi) OGL or NNL Declaration

To check that the charges and commission including GST is collected from the customer's account as per the standard pricing or as per the special pricing. Check whether the special pricing approval is on record as per the approval matrix
To check that the margin is collected as per the credit facility or the process note and lien is marked on the margin amount

To check that the usance tenor of the LC is as per the credit facility terms. Also check that the guidelines regarding maximum tenor for import of specified goods such as gold, precious metal, silver, diamond etc. are adhered to. 
(i)Silver/Palladium/Platinum/Rhodium/Diamond Import - Maxiumu 90 days
(ii)  Raw Material - 1 Year (including suppliers credit period - check suppliers credit request letter provided)
(iii) Capital Goods - 3 years

To check the limit booking is correctly done and the limit was not overdrawn. Also check that the clients (Non-constituent Borrowers) who do not have a valid Limit uploaded in the system, the same have to be highligted Seperately as they are highly critical in Nature and governed by specific regulations pertaining to such facilies by the Reserve Bank.
Check whether LC provides for transfer of LC to third Party
Check in case of Partial Transfer whether partial shipment is permitted in original LC
Check the amount of transfer LC does not exceed the amount of original LC
To check the date of shipment and expiry date within the shipment date and expiry date of the original LC
To check the conditions in Transfer LC do not contradict the Conditions of the original LC

Import transactions involving INR settlement through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA). Following the January 2025 FEMA amendments promoting INR internationalisation, transactions settled through SRVAs should be verified for compliance with the permitted purposes and reporting requirements.

For LCs opened for import of gold/silver by Qualified Jewellers (QJs) through India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX), verify: (i) Importer is a SEBI-registered QJ; (ii) LC is strictly for gold/silver routed through IIBX; (iii) Usance ≤ 90 days. Ref: RBI AP (DIR Series) Circular on IIBX; SEBI Circular on QJs; IFSCA Framework.

Where LC is confirmed by KMBL or a foreign bank, verify: (i) Confirmation request is from the advising bank (MT 700/MT 707); (ii) Confirmation charges collected from the customer; (iii) Confirmed LC exposure is within approved bank limits (ALCO); (iv) For LC confirmed for sanctioned/high-risk countries, RBI/Trade Ops Head approval is in place.

- Import of physical goods into India within 6 months and 3 years in case of capital goods from the date of remittance
- In the event of non-import of goods, the amount of advance will be repatriated to India or is utilized for the purpose for which release of exchange is permissible under FEMA

(i) Details of the Transaction

If the invoice value for the advance payment is above USD 200,000 then the bank guarantee is provided by the supplier in favor of the importer for the advance payment amount. If such BG is not provided check that the approvals as per the exception matrix (as per a suitable policy framed by the bank's Board of Directors) is obtained for waiver of such BG upto USD 5,000,000.00
If the customer is a government organization/institute/A Public Sector Company or a Department/Undertaking of the Government of India / State Government, the BG is required for any advance payment amount above USD 100,000.00 otherwise an approval for waiver of the BG is required from the Ministry of Finance.
Advance Import remittance for Rough Diamond

Check if the advance payment amount as per the invoice exceeds USD 200,000 for import of rough diamond and the Bank gurantee is not provided by the customer (other than Public Sector Company or Department / Undertaking of Government of India / State Government). Check the following conditions are adhered to: 
i. The overseas mining company should have the recommendation of GJEPC.
ii. The importer should be a recognised processor of rough diamonds and should have a good track record.
iii. AD Category - I banks should, undertake the transaction based on their commercial judgment and after being satisfied about the bonafides of the transaction.
iv. Advance payments should be made strictly as per the terms of the sale contract and should be made directly to the account of the company concerned, that is, to the ultimate beneficiary and not through numbered accounts or otherwise and AD banks should ensure that they have created the Outward Remittance Message (ORM) for all such outward remittances in IDPMS.
v. Further, due caution may be exercised to ensure that remittance is not permitted for import of conflict diamonds (Declaration for submission of Kimberly Certificate to be obtained).
vi. D&B report is obtained on the overseas supplier.
vii. AD Category - I banks should follow-up submission of the Bill of Entry / documents evidencing import of rough diamonds into the country by the importer, in terms of the Act / Rules / Regulations / Directions issued in this regard.
b) In case of an importer entity in the Public Sector or a Department / Undertaking of the Government of India / State Government/s, AD Category - I banks may permit the advance remittance subject to the above conditions and a specific waiver of bank guarantee from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, where the advance payments is equivalent to or exceeds USD 100,000/- (USD one hundred thousand only).
viii. Based on the AD code declared by the importer, the banks shall download the Bill of Entry (BOE) issued by EDI ports from “BOE Master” in IDPMS. For non-EDI ports, AD banks of the importer shall upload the BoE data in IDPMS as per message format “Manual BoE reporting” on daily basis on receipt of BoE from the customer/Customs Office.
ix. AD banks will enter BOE details  and mark off ORMs as per the message format “BOE Settlement”
x. In case of payment after receipt of BoE, the AD bank shall generate ORM for import payments made by the importer customer as per the message format “BOE Settlement”
Check that a high value transaction approval as per the exception matrix is obtained for amount above USD 200,000.00

To check that the charges and commission including GST is collected from the customer's account as per the standard pricing or as per the special pricing. Check whether the special pricing approval is on record as per the approval matrix
Advance payment for Import of Aircraft, Helicopter or aviation related purchases

Check that the following guidelines are adhered to for import of aircraft/helicopter/aviation related purchases:
i. entities which have been permitted under the extant Foreign Trade Policy to import aircrafts and helicopters (including used / second hand aircraft and helicopters) or any other person who has been granted permission by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to operate Scheduled or Non-Scheduled Air Transport Service (including Air Taxi Services)
ii. advance import payment without Bank Guarantee upto USD 50 million for each aircraft, helicopter and other aviation related purchases
iii. Importers of Aircrafts/ Helicopters and other Aviation related Purchases, not eligible under clause (1) above can make advance remittance without bank guarantee, in terms of Para C.1.1 above
iv. D&B report on the overseas supplier is obtained and it is satisfactory.
v. Internal approval as per the exception matrix in obtained
vi. Payment is made directly to the manufacturer (supplier) concerned.
vii.  In the case of a Public Sector Company or a Department / Undertaking of Central /State Governments, the AD Category - I bank shall ensure that the requirement of bank guarantee has been specifically waived by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India for advance remittances exceeding USD 100,000.
viii. Physical import of goods into India is made within six months (three years in case of capital goods) from the date of remittance and the importer gives an undertaking to furnish documentary evidence of import within fifteen days from the close of the relevant period. It is clarified that where advance is paid as milestone payments, the date of last remittance made in terms of the contract will be reckoned for the purpose of submission of documentary evidence of import.
ix.  the requisite in principle approval of the Ministry of Civil Aviation in case of Scheduled Air Service Operators and in other cases approval of the Director General of Civil Aviation / other agencies in terms of the extant Foreign Trade Policy has been obtained by the company, for import.
x. In the event of non-import of aircraft and aviation sector related products, AD Category - I bank should ensure that the amount of advance remittance is immediately repatriated to India.

Check that the advance payment for import of services is subject to the following guidelines:
i. Where the amount of advance exceeds USD 500,000 or its equivalent, a guarantee from a bank of international repute situated outside India, or a guarantee from an AD Category – I bank in India, if such a guarantee is issued against the counter-guarantee of a bank of international repute situated outside India, should be obtained from the overseas beneficiary
ii. In the case of a Public Sector Company or a Department/ Undertaking of the Government of India/ State Governments, approval from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India for advance remittance for import of services without bank guarantee for an amount exceeding USD 100,000 (USD One hundred thousand) or its equivalent would be required.
iii. AD Category – I banks should also follow-up to ensure that the beneficiary of the advance remittance fulfils his obligation under the contract or agreement with the remitter in India, failing which, the amount should be repatriated to India.
iv. AD Category – I banks should ensure generation of ORMs and marking off in the IDPMS etc., as per extant IDPMS guidelines
Check that the invoice and the Bill of entry mention the third party beneficiary name in case the payment is being made to the third party.

Ensure adherence to the specific guidelines regarding the submission of proof of import in lieu of the Bill of Entry. Ensure to check all such cases during the audit. For e.g. verification of import evidences under Postal Appraisal Forms, or Customs Assessment Certificates, CA certificate etc
Check that the guidelines related to the replacement import is adhered to.
Check that the advance payment is not allowed for import of gold or precious metals.
Check that the ACU mechanism for payment is followed for the bills involving the SAARC countries except Nepal and Bhutan.
Advance Import Remittance – Third Party Payment
Check that the invoice and the Bill of entry mention the third-party beneficiary’s name in case the payment is being made to the third party.

Verify whether extant guidelines complied for advance remittance allowed towards import of gold /silver by resident Qualified Jewelers through IIBX or any other exchange approved by IFSCA and DGFT, Government of India. Also, whether transactions are reported on monthly / half-yearly basis. In case contract does not materialize whether amount is refunded within stipulated time. Verify whether BOE submitted for all such transactions.

For import payments for services, royalties, interest, or other payments to non-residents, verify whether TDS under Section 195 of the Income Tax Act is applicable. If yes, ensure Form 15CA/15CB is obtained and TDS deposited before remittance. Ref: Income Tax Act Section 195; CBDT Circular; FEMA A2 Form requirements.

Direct Import of Gold/Other precious metals/Gold Jewellery/Rough, cut or polished diamonds

Check that the Suppliers’ and Buyers’ Credit, including the usance period of Letters of Credit opened for import of Platinum, Palladium, Rhodium and Silver and rough, cut and polished Diamonds, Precious and semi-precious stones; should not exceed 90 days from the date of shipment. However for Clean Credit i.e. credit given by a foreign supplier to its Indian customer/ buyer, without any Letter of Credit (Suppliers’ Credit)/ Letter of Undertaking (Buyers’ Credit)/ Fixed Deposits from any Indian financial institution for import of rough, cut and polished diamonds, precious and semi-precious stones, may be permitted for a period not exceeding 180 days from the date of shipment
Direct Import of Gold/Other precious metals/Gold Jewellery/Rough, cut or polished diamonds

Check that the Suppliers’ and Buyers’ credit (trade credit) including the usance period of Letters of Credit opened for import of gold in any form, including jewellery made of gold/precious metals or/and studded with diamonds/semi- precious/precious stones, should not exceed 90 days from the date of shipment.
Direct Import of Gold/Other precious metals/Gold Jewellery/Rough, cut or polished diamonds
Check that only SEZ/EOU or Status Holder exporters are allowed to import the gold or precious metal.
Direct Import of Gold/Other precious metals/Gold Jewellery/Rough, cut or polished diamonds

AD banks may allow extension of time in respect of such clean credit for import of rough, cut and polished diamonds, for a period exceeding 180 days from the date of shipment to a maximum period of 180 days beyond the prescribed period/ due date beyond which they may refer the cases to the respective Regional Office of the Reserve Bank. Such extension by AD banks may be subject to the conditions such as: (i) AD banks being satisfied of the genuineness of the reason and bonafides of the transaction and also that no interest payment is involved for the additional period; (ii) reasons for such extension are due to financial difficulties and/ or quality disputes; (iii) importer is not under investigation and is not a frequent offender. AD banks may submit a half yearly report of such extensions allowed customer-wise, to the respective Regional Office of the Reserve Bank.
Import of Platinum / Silver on Unfixed Price Basis

The nominated agency/bank may allow import of platinum and silver, on outright purchase basis subject to the condition that although ownership of the same shall be passed on to the importers at the time of import itself, the price shall be fixed later as and when the importer sells to the user.

Check that the import payment above USD 300,000 per import is allowed only for the following cases:
(i) Importer is the Wholly owned subsidiary of the Exporter
(ii) Importer is a Public Limited Company, Private Limited Company, Deemed Limited Company or PSU
(iii) Importer is a Status Holder
(iv) Importer is a SEZ or EOU
For any other importer, the amount per import should be lesss than USD 300,000
Check that the import of foreign currency is allowed only for the FFMC/AD II category and prior RBI permission is obtained.

Ensure adherence to the specific guidelines regarding the submission of proof of import in lieu of the Bill of Entry. Ensure to check all such cases during the audit. For e.g. verification of import evidences under Postal Appraisal Forms, or Customs Assessment Certificates, CA certificate etc

AD Category I banks shall give extension for submission of BoE beyond the prescribed period in terms of the extant guidelines on the matter, and the same will be reported in IDPMS as per the message “Bill of Entry Extension” and the date up to which  extension is granted will be indicated in “Extension Date” column.
(x) AD Category I banks can consider closure of BoE/ORM in IDPMS that involves write off to the extent of 5% of invoice value in cases where the amount declared in BoE varies from the actual remittance due to operational reasons and AD bank is satisfied with the reason/s submitted by the importer.
Check that the guidelines related to the replacement import is adhered to.
Check that the ACU mechanism for payment is followed for the bills involving the SAARC countries except Nepal and Bhutan.
Re-export of unsold rough diamonds from Special Notified Zone of Customs without Export Declaration Form (EDF) formality
Verify whether there was any instance of re-export of unsold rough diamonds from special notified zone of customs and due diligence / records maintained for verification as per extant guidelines.

sheets.name: Buyers Credit
rows: Check that no roll-over/ extension is permitted beyond the permissible period i.e., the trade credit period for import of non-capital goods upto one year from the date of shipment or upto the operating cycle whichever is lower
Check that the buyers credit facility is provided only to the resident indian importer and constituent borrower of the Bank.

Check that the valid import transaction details is mentioned in the customer request letter. Check that the import transaction is falling due for payment on or after the Trade Credit funds are arranged. Check that the Trade Credit funds are not credited to the suspense or GL account. Also check that the import payment is processed only after sighting or receiving the funds in the Nostro account.

Check whether the hedging of the exchange rate risk is done if applicable. The entities raising TC are required to follow the guidelines for hedging, if any, issued by the concerned sectoral or prudential regulator in respect of foreign currency exposure. Such entities shall have a board approved risk management policy
Check that the currency of the existing INR currency Trade Credit is not changed from INR to any other currency

To check that the devolvement process is followed. Check the devolvement loan account is created for correct amount, correct interest rate, limit blocking etc. Also check whether the customer's current account or CC account has been lien marked for the devolvement loan amount.

Check that the tenor of the Buyers Credit is up to three years for import of capital goods. For non-capital goods, this period is up to one year or the operating cycle whichever is less. For shipyards / shipbuilders, the period of TC for import of non-capital goods can be up to three years.
Check that the customer request letter is as per the format and the details are in sync with the transaction and other documents.

Check that the lender of the buyers credit is as follows:
Banks, financial institutions, foreign equity holder(s) located outside India and financial institutions in IFSCs located in India.
Participation of Indian banks and non-banking financial companies (operating from IFSCs) as lenders will be subject to the prudential guidelines issued by the concerned regulatory departments of the Reserve Bank. Further, foreign branches/subsidiaries of Indian banks are permitted as recognised lenders only for FCY TC.

The all-in-cost ceiling for Trade Credit is: benchmark rate (SOFR/ARR) + 250 bps for TC up to 3 years. For TC between 3-5 years: benchmark + 350 bps. Verify the applicable ceiling based on TC tenor. Also note that 'minimum average maturity' requirement of 1 year (or operating cycle) applies. Ref: RBI Master Direction on Trade Credits (updated 2023)

Check that the Bank Guarantee is issued for the Trade credit and the details in the BG is accurate as per the underlying import transaction. Check that the expiry date is same as the due date of the Trade Credit. Check that the Letter of Undertaking or Letter of Comfort is not issued for the Trade Credit. Check that the BG is issued in MT760 format and not in MT799.
Check that the monthly and quarterly Trade Credit reporting is done correctly for the Buyers credit and Suppliers credit transactions.
Check that the direct import or import collection bills settled after 180 days from the shipment date are also reported in the Trade Credit.

Check that the NOC is obtained from the other bank in case the import transaction is handled by the other Bank. In such case, check that the Trade Credit proceeds is remitted to the other bank directly and not credited to the customer's account.

Check that the Bill of Entry or Bill of Entry details as per the IDPMS data is obtained oherwise valid reason from the customer for non availability of the bill of entry is obtained and necessary approval as per the exception matrix is obtained.
Check that the Trade credit for import of Gold, Diamond, Platinum, Palladium, Rhodium, Silver and precious stones is maximum 90 days from the shipment date (including any other usance period)
Check that the request letter as per the format alongwith Form A2, Form 15CA and CB are provided. Check that the details are correct in all documents.
Check that the Trade Credit arrangement and repayment is reported in the R-return.

Check that the Trade Credit disbursement proceeds are not credited to the customer's account. Check that the proceeds are used only for the import payment. Check that the inward remittance transaction is booked for the disbursement funds.
Check that all other regulatory guidelines as per the Master Directiion on ECB and Trade Credit is adhered to.
Check that the commission and charges are collected as per the process note or as per the special pricing approval.
Verify whether interest is correctly computed and added to principal amount for blocking of limit

FCY TC - Change of currency of TC from one freely convertible foreign currency to any other freely convertible foreign currency as well as to INR is freely permitted.
INR TC - Change of currency from INR to any freely convertible foreign currency is not permitted.

2. Prepare Opening Working Sheet
Extract all capital transactions from client inception up to the end of the previous quarter. (Corpus In transactions should be excluded from 16th to 30/31st and Corpus withdrawal should be included from 16th to 30/31st)
Calculate Net Capital Balance based on (a) = Total Credits – Total Debits.
Calculate Opening Payout = 2% × Net Capital Balance.
3. Prepare Quarterly Payout Working Sheet
Extract all capital transactions for the current quarter.
Client Rule: If the transaction is in the last month of the quarter, only capital withdrawals made after the 15th should be considered in the payout-in-transaction working and Capital deposits made after the 15th should not be considered.
For each eligible transaction, calculate prorated payout:
Payout = Transaction Amount × 2% × (No. of days from Transaction Date to Quarter End ÷ Total Days in Quarter)
Prepare the Pivot table for each client having the total payout amount for all eligible quarterly transactions.

Arrive at Final Quarterly Payout.
